original: Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ sappaṭighaṃ? Rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ sappaṭighaṃ.
ai: What is that material phenomenon which is not a faculty and has impingement? Visible object... up to... tangible object – this is that material phenomenon which is not a faculty and has impingement.

text: 981. Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ appaṭighaṃ? Kāyaviññatti…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ appaṭighaṃ.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are good?⤵The three roots of good (karma), to wit, absence of lust, absence of hate, absence of dullness; the skandhas of feeling, perception, activities and consciousness when they are associated with those three roots; whatever action, bodily, vocal and mental, springs from those three roots.
original: Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ appaṭighaṃ? Kāyaviññatti…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ appaṭighaṃ.
ai: What is that material phenomenon which is not a faculty and does not have impingement? Bodily intimation... up to... nutritive essence – this is that material phenomenon which is not a faculty and does not have impingement.

text: Evaṃ dasavidhena rūpasaṅgaho.
original: Evaṃ dasavidhena rūpasaṅgaho.
ai: Thus, the collection of material phenomena is tenfold.

text: Dasakaṃ.
original: Dasakaṃ.
ai: The Decad.

text: Ekādasakaṃ
original: Ekādasakaṃ
ai: The Undecad

text: 982. Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cakkhu catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmo peso – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ .
rys_davids: Which are the states that are bad?⤵The three roots of bad (karma), to wit, lust, hate, dullness; the vices that are united with them; the skandhas of feeling, perception, synergies and consciousness when these are associated with them; whatever action, bodily, vocal and mental, springs from them.
original: Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cakkhu catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmo peso – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ .
ai: What is that material phenomenon which is the eye-base? That eye which is a sensitive part dependent on the four great primaries... up to... a deserted village – this is that material phenomenon which is the eye-base.

text: 983. Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ sotāyatanaṃ…pe… ghānāyatanaṃ…pe… jivhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… saddāyatanaṃ…pe… gandhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ? Pathavīdhātu…pe… phoṭṭhabbadhātu pesā – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are indeterminate?⤵The results of good and bad states taking effect in the worlds of sense, form, or the formless, or in the [life that is] Unincluded; the skandhas of feeling, perception, synergies and consciousness, inoperative states, moreover, which are neither good, nor bad, nor the results of karma; lastly, all form and unconditioned element.
original: Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ sotāyatanaṃ…pe… ghānāyatanaṃ…pe… jivhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… saddāyatanaṃ…pe… gandhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ? Pathavīdhātu…pe… phoṭṭhabbadhātu pesā – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ.
ai: What is that material phenomenon which is the ear-base... up to... the tangible object-base? Earth element... up to... tangible element – this is that material phenomenon which is the tangible object-base.

text: 984. Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ? Itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are associated with a feeling of ease?⤵The skandhas of perception, activities and consciousness (the feeling itself being excepted) are the states associated [with the consciousness arising] in pleasurable soil, whether it belongs to the worlds of sense or of form, or to the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ? Itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro – idaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ.
ai: What is that material phenomenon which is non-manifesting, without impingement, and included in the dhamma-base? Femininity faculty... up to... nutritive essence – this is that material phenomenon which is non-manifesting, without impingement, and included in the dhamma-base.

text: Evaṃ ekādasavidhena rūpasaṅgaho.
original: Evaṃ ekādasavidhena rūpasaṅgaho.
ai: Thus, the collection of material phenomena is elevenfold.

text: Ekādasakaṃ.
original: Ekādasakaṃ.
ai: The Undecad.

text: Aṭṭhamabhāṇavāro.
original: Aṭṭhamabhāṇavāro.
ai: Eighth Recitation Section.

text: Rūpavibhatti.
original: Rūpavibhatti.
ai: Classification of Matter.

text: Rūpakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.
original: Rūpakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.
ai: The Section on Matter is concluded.

text: 3. Nikkhepakaṇḍaṃ
original: 3. Nikkhepakaṇḍaṃ
ai: 3. Compendium of Categories

text: Tikanikkhepaṃ
original: Tikanikkhepaṃ
ai: Exposition of Triads

text: 985. Katame dhammā kusalā? Tīṇi kusalamūlāni – alobho, adoso, amoho; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā kusalā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are associated with distressful feeling?⤵The skandhas of perception, synergies and consciousness (the feeling itself being excepted) are the states associated [with the consciousness arising] in a distressful soil belonging to the sensuous universe.
original: Katame dhammā kusalā? Tīṇi kusalamūlāni – alobho, adoso, amoho; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā kusalā.
ai: Which phenomena are wholesome? The three wholesome roots—non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with them; and the bodily kamma, verbal kamma, and mental kamma arisen from them—these phenomena are wholesome.

text: 986. Katame dhammā akusalā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā akusalā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are associated with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant?⤵The skandhas of perception, synergies and consciousness (the feeling itself being excepted) are the states associated [with the consciousness arising] in a neutral soil, whether it belong to the worlds of sense, form, or the formless, or to the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā akusalā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā akusalā.
ai: Which phenomena are unwholesome? The three unwholesome roots—greed, hatred, delusion; and the defilements co-existent with them; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with them; and the bodily kamma, verbal kamma, and mental kamma arisen from them—these phenomena are unwholesome.

text: 987. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā abyākatā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are results?⤵The results of good and bad states which take effect in the worlds of sense, form and the formless, and in the life that is Unincluded; [in other words] the four skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā abyākatā? Kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā abyākatā.
ai: Which phenomena are indeterminate? The resultants of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate; and those functional phenomena that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor kamma-resultants; and all matter, and the unconditioned element—these phenomena are indeterminate.

text: 988. Katame dhammā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā? Sukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, sukhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that involve resultant states?⤵Good and bad states belonging to the worlds of sense, form and the formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; [in other words] the four skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā? Sukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, sukhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with pleasant feeling? In the plane of pleasant feeling, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane, excluding pleasant feeling; the perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with it—these phenomena are associated with pleasant feeling.

text: 989. Katame dhammā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā? Dukkhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā .
rys_davids: Which are the states that neither are results, nor have the quality of involving resultant states?⤵Those states concerning action which are neither good, nor bad, nor the results of karma; all [material] form, moreover, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā? Dukkhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā .
ai: Which phenomena are associated with painful feeling? In the plane of painful feeling, in the sense sphere, excluding painful feeling; the perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with it—these phenomena are associated with painful feeling.

text: 990. Katame dhammā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā? Adukkhamasukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, arūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are both grasped at and favourable to grasping?⤵The co-Intoxicant results of good and bad states taking effect in the worlds of sense, form or the formless; in other words, the four skandhas; such form, moreover, as is due to karma having been wrought.
original: Katame dhammā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā? Adukkhamasukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, arūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?⤵The aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness, in the sense, fine-material, immaterial, and transcendent spheres, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, excluding the feeling itself.

text: 991. Katame dhammā vipākā? Kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā vipākā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not grasped at but are favourable to grasping?⤵Good and bad co-Intoxicant states taking effect in the worlds of sense, form, or the formless; in other words, the four skandhas; inoperative states, moreover, which are neither good, nor bad, nor the results of karma; as well as such form as is not due to karma having been wrought
original: Katame dhammā vipākā? Kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā vipākā.
ai: Which phenomena are results?⤵The results of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena in the sense, fine-material, immaterial, and transcendent spheres, namely, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.

text: 992. Katame dhammā vipākadhammadhammā? Kusalākusalā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā vipākadhammadhammā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are neither grasped at nor favourable to grasping?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā vipākadhammadhammā? Kusalākusalā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā vipākadhammadhammā.
ai: Which phenomena have the nature of producing results?⤵Wholesome and unwholesome phenomena in the sense, fine-material, immaterial, and transcendent spheres, namely, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.

text: 993. Katame dhammā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā? Ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are vitiated and vicious?⤵The three roots of bad (karma), to wit, lust, hate, dullness; the Corruptions that are united with them; the four skandhas when these are associated with them; whatever action, bodily, vocal and mental, springs from them.
original: Katame dhammā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā? Ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.
ai: Which phenomena are neither results nor having the nature of producing results?⤵Functional phenomena that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not kamma-results; all material phenomena; and the unconditioned element.

text: 994. Katame dhammā upādiṇṇupādāniyā? Sāsavā kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; yañca rūpaṃ kammassa katattā – ime dhammā upādiṇṇupādāniyā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not corrupt but baneful?⤵Good and indeterminate co-Intoxicant states taking effect in the worlds of sense, form and the formless; in other words, the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā upādiṇṇupādāniyā? Sāsavā kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; yañca rūpaṃ kammassa katattā – ime dhammā upādiṇṇupādāniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are clung to and graspable?⤵The results of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, subject to taints, in the sense, fine-material, and immaterial spheres, namely, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness; and matter born of kamma.

text: 995. Katame dhammā anupādiṇṇupādāniyā? Sāsavā kusalākusalā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā; yañca rūpaṃ na kammassa katattā – ime dhammā anupādiṇṇupādāniyā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are neither corrupt nor baneful?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā anupādiṇṇupādāniyā? Sāsavā kusalākusalā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā; yañca rūpaṃ na kammassa katattā – ime dhammā anupādiṇṇupādāniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are not clung to, but graspable?⤵Wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, subject to taints, in the sense, fine-material, and immaterial spheres, namely, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness; functional phenomena that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not kamma-results; and matter not born of kamma.

text: 996. Katame dhammā anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā.
rys_davids: Which are the states associated with applied and sustained thought?⤵The four skandhas (applied and sustained thought itself excluded) which are associated [with the consciousness arising] in a soil favourable to applied and sustained thought, whether it belong to the world of Sense or of Form, or to the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are neither clung to nor graspable?⤵The transcendent paths, their fruits, and the unconditioned element.

text: 997. Katame dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā.
rys_davids: Which are the states not so associated?⤵The four skandhas (sustained thought itself excluded) which are associated [with the consciousness arising] in a soil favourable not to applied, but only to sustained thought, whether it belong to the world of Form, or to the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā.
ai: Which phenomena are defiled and defiling?⤵The three unwholesome roots – greed, hatred, delusion; associated defilements; the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness associated with them; and bodily, verbal, and mental action arising from them.

text: 998. Katame dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā? Sāsavā kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho , saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not associated with either applied or sustained thought?⤵The four skandhas which are associated [with the consciousness arising] in a soil not associated with either, whether it belong to the world of Sense, Form, or the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; all [material] form, moreover, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā? Sāsavā kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho , saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā.
ai: Which phenomena are undefiled but defiling?⤵Wholesome and indeterminate phenomena, subject to taints, in the sense, fine-material, and immaterial spheres, namely, the aggregate of matter, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.

text: 999. Katame dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are accompanied by zest?⤵The four skandhas (zest itself being excluded) which are associated [with the consciousness arising] in a soil yielding zest, whether it belong to the worlds of Sense or Form, or to the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā.
ai: Which phenomena are neither defiled nor defiling?⤵The transcendent paths, their fruits, and the unconditioned element.

text: 1000. Katame dhammā savitakkasavicārā? Savitakkasavicārabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne , vitakkavicāre ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā savitakkasavicārā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are accompanied by ease?⤵The skandhas of perception, synergies and consciousness (ease being excluded) which are associated [with the consciousness arising] in an ease-yielding soil, whether it belong to the worlds of Sense or Form, or to the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā savitakkasavicārā? Savitakkasavicārabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne , vitakkavicāre ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā savitakkasavicārā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, associated with them, in the sphere of initial and sustained application (sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane), excluding initial application and sustained application. These phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application.

text: 1001. Katame dhammā avitakkavicāramattā? Avitakkavicāramattabhūmiyaṃ rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, vicāraṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā avitakkavicāramattā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are accompanied by indifference?⤵The skandhas of perception, synergies and consciousness (indifference itself excluded) which are associated [with the consciousness arising] in a soil favourable to indifference, whether it belong to the worlds of Form or the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā avitakkavicāramattā? Avitakkavicāramattabhūmiyaṃ rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, vicāraṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā avitakkavicāramattā.
ai: Which phenomena are without initial application, only sustained application?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, associated with them, in the sphere of only sustained application (fine-material sphere and supramundane), excluding sustained application. These phenomena are without initial application, only sustained application.

text: 1002. Katame dhammā avitakkaavicārā? Avitakkaavicārabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare , arūpāvacare, apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā avitakkaavicārā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are to be put away by vision?⤵The three Fetters, to wit, the theory of individuality, perplexity, and perversion as to rule and ritual.⤵In this connexion
original: Katame dhammā avitakkaavicārā? Avitakkaavicārabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare , arūpāvacare, apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā avitakkaavicārā.
ai: Which phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, in the sphere without initial and sustained application (sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane); all material phenomena; and the unconditioned element. These phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application.

text: 1003. Katame dhammā pītisahagatā? Pītibhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne , pītiṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā pītisahagatā.
rys_davids: What is the “theory of individuality”?⤵When in this world the ignorant, average man who perceives not the Noble Ones, who comprehends not, nor is trained according to the doctrine of the Noble Ones, who perceives not good men, who comprehends not, nor is trained according to, the doctrine of good men, regards (1) the self as bodily shape, or (2) as having bodily shape, or regards (3) bodily shape as being in the self, or (4) the self as being in bodily shape; or regards (5) the self as feeling, or (6) as having feeling, or regards (7) feeling as being in the self, or (8) the self as being in feeling; or regards (9) the self as perception, or (10) as having perception, or regards (11) perception as being in the self, or (12) the self as being in perception; or regards (13) the self as synergies, or (14) as having synergies, or regards (15) synergies as being in the self, or (16) the self as being in synergies; or regards (17) the self as consciousness, or (18) as having consciousness, or regards (19) consciousness as being in the self, or (20) the self as being in consciousness—then this kind of opinion, this walking in opinion, this jungle of opinion, wilderness of opinion, disorder of opinion, scuffling of opinion, this Fetter of opinion, the grip and tenacity of it, the inclination towards it, the being infected by it, this by-path, wrong road, wrongness, this sectarianism, this inverted grasp—this is called the theory of individuality.
original: Katame dhammā pītisahagatā? Pītibhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne , pītiṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā pītisahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by joy?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, associated with them, in the sphere of joy (sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane), excluding joy. These phenomena are accompanied by joy.

text: 1004. Katame dhammā sukhasahagatā? Sukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sukhasahagatā.
rys_davids: What is “perplexity”?⤵To doubt, to be perplexed about, (1) the Master, to doubt, to be perplexed about, (2) the Doctrine, to doubt, to be perplexed about, (3) the Order, about (4) the Discipline, about (5) the past, the future, about both the past and the future, (6) as to whether there be an assignable cause of states causally determined—it is this kind of doubt, this working of doubt, this dubiety, puzzlement, perplexity, distraction, standing at cross-roads; collapse, uncertainty of grasp; evasion, hesitation, incapacity of grasping thoroughly, stiffness of mind, mental scarifying, that is called perplexity.
original: Katame dhammā sukhasahagatā? Sukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sukhasahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by happiness?⤵The perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, associated with them, in the sphere of happiness (sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane), excluding happiness. These phenomena are accompanied by happiness.

text: 1005. Katame dhammā upekkhāsahagatā? Upekkhābhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, arūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upekkhāsahagatā.
rys_davids: What is perversion as to rule and ritual?⤵The theory, held by recluses and Brahmins outside our doctrine, that holiness is got by rules of moral conduct, that holiness is got by rites, that holiness is got by rules of moral conduct and by rites—this kind of opinion, this walking in mere opinion, this jungle of opinion, this wilderness of opinion, this disorder of opinion, scuffling of opinion, Fetter of opinion, the grip and tenacity of it, the inclination towards it, the being infected by it, this by-path, wrong road, wrongness, this sectarianism, this inverted grasp—this is called the perversion as to rule and ritual.
original: Katame dhammā upekkhāsahagatā? Upekkhābhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare, rūpāvacare, arūpāvacare, apariyāpanne, upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upekkhāsahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by equanimity?⤵The perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, associated with them, in the sphere of equanimity (sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane), excluding equanimity. These phenomena are accompanied by equanimity.

text: 1006. Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbā? Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.
rys_davids: These three Fetters, and the vices united with them, and the four skandhas associated with them, as well as the action, bodily, vocal and mental, springing from them—these are the states which are to be put away by insight.
original: Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbā? Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.
ai: Which phenomena are to be abandoned by vision?⤵The three fetters: personality view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals.

text: 1007. Tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ attato samanupassati, vedanāvantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā vedanaṃ, vedanāya vā attānaṃ. Saññaṃ attato samanupassati, saññāvantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā saññaṃ, saññāya vā attānaṃ. Saṅkhāre attato samanupassati, saṅkhāravantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā saṅkhāre, saṅkhāresu vā attānaṃ. Viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ [diṭṭhivisūkāyitaṃ (sī.)] diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho paṭiggāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sakkāyadiṭṭhi.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are to be put away by culture?⤵Whatever lust, hate and dullness still remain, and any vices united with them; the four skandhas that are associated with them; whatever action, bodily, vocal or mental, springs from them.
original: Tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ attato samanupassati, vedanāvantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā vedanaṃ, vedanāya vā attānaṃ. Saññaṃ attato samanupassati, saññāvantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā saññaṃ, saññāya vā attānaṃ. Saṅkhāre attato samanupassati, saṅkhāravantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā saṅkhāre, saṅkhāresu vā attānaṃ. Viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ [diṭṭhivisūkāyitaṃ (sī.)] diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho paṭiggāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sakkāyadiṭṭhi.
ai: What is personality view?⤵Here, an uninstructed worldling, not seeing noble ones, unskilled in the Dhamma of noble ones, untrained in the Dhamma of noble ones; not seeing good men, unskilled in the Dhamma of good men, untrained in the Dhamma of good men, regards form as self, or self as having form, or form as in self, or self as in form; regards feeling as self, or self as having feeling, or feeling as in self, or self as in feeling; regards perception as self, or self as having perception, or perception as in self, or self as in perception; regards volitional formations as self, or self as having volitional formations, or volitional formations as in self, or self as in volitional formations; regards consciousness as self, or self as having consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, distortion of views, vacillation of views, fetter of views, grasping, clinging, adherence, obsession, wrong path, false way, wrongness, sectarian position, inverted grasp – this is called personality view.

text: 1008. Tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati, dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati, saṅghe kaṅkhati vicikicchati, sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, aparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbantāparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati. Yā evarūpā kaṅkhā kaṅkhāyanā kaṅkhāyitattaṃ vimati vicikicchā dveḷhakaṃ dvedhāpatho saṃsayo anekaṃsaggāho āsappanā parisappanā apariyogāhanā thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are to be put away neither by vision nor by culture?⤵Good and indeterminate states relating to the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; the four skandhas; all [material] form, moreover, and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati, dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati, saṅghe kaṅkhati vicikicchati, sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, aparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbantāparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati. Yā evarūpā kaṅkhā kaṅkhāyanā kaṅkhāyitattaṃ vimati vicikicchā dveḷhakaṃ dvedhāpatho saṃsayo anekaṃsaggāho āsappanā parisappanā apariyogāhanā thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
ai: What is doubt?⤵Doubts, is perplexed about, the Teacher; doubts, is perplexed about, the Dhamma; doubts, is perplexed about, the Saṅgha; doubts, is perplexed about, the training; doubts, is perplexed about, the past; doubts, is perplexed about, the future; doubts, is perplexed about, both past and future; doubts, is perplexed about, dependent arising and dependently arisen phenomena. Whatever such wavering, state of wavering, perplexity, doubt, two-way path, uncertainty, grasping at many sides, vacillation, wandering, lack of penetration, stiffness of mind, mental defilement – this is called doubt.

text: 1009. Tattha katamo sīlabbataparāmāso? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ ‘sīlena suddhi, vatena suddhi, sīlabbatena suddhī’ti yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho paṭiggāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sīlabbataparāmāso.
rys_davids: Which are the states the causes of which are to be put away by vision?⤵The three Fetters, to wit, theory of individuality, perplexity, perversion as to rule and ritual.⤵In this connexion
original: Tattha katamo sīlabbataparāmāso? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ ‘sīlena suddhi, vatena suddhi, sīlabbatena suddhī’ti yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho paṭiggāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sīlabbataparāmāso.
ai: What is adherence to rites and rituals?⤵Among recluses and brahmins outside this doctrine, the view 'purification by virtue, purification by rites, purification by virtue and rites'. Whatever such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, distortion of views, vacillation of views, fetter of views, grasping, clinging, adherence, obsession, wrong path, false way, wrongness, sectarian position, inverted grasp – this is called adherence to rites and rituals.

text: 1010. Imāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā.
rys_davids: What is “theory of individuality”? … [Continue as in §§ 1003 – 1005 ] .
original: Imāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā.
ai: These three fetters; and defilements associated with them; the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them; bodily action, vocal action, mental action arising from them – these phenomena are to be abandoned by seeing.

text: 1011. Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Avaseso lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
rys_davids: Which are the states the causes of which are to be put away by culture?⤵Whatever lust, hate and dullness still remain, these are causes that are to be put away by culture. And the vices united with them, the four skandhas associated with them, and the action, bodily, vocal and mental, springing from them—these are states the causes of which are to be put away by culture.
original: Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Avaseso lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
ai: Which phenomena are to be abandoned by development? The remaining greed, hatred, delusion; and defilements associated with them; the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them; bodily action, vocal action, mental action arising from them – these phenomena are to be abandoned by development.

text: 1012. Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho ; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
rys_davids: Which are the states the causes of which are to be put away neither by vision, nor by cultivation?⤵The afore-mentioned states excepted, all other states, good, bad and indeterminate, relating to the worlds of Sense, Form and the Formless, and to the life that is Unincluded; in other words, the four skandhas; all [material] form, moreover, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho ; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
ai: Which phenomena are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development? Wholesome and indeterminate phenomena belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and unincluded; the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate; and all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development.

text: 1013. Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā? Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.
rys_davids: Which are the states that make for the piling up [of rebirth]?⤵Good and bad co-Intoxicant states relating to the worlds of Sense, Form and the Formless; [in other words], the four skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā? Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.
ai: Which phenomena have causes to be abandoned by seeing? The three fetters: identity view, doubt, clinging to rites and rituals.

text: 1014. Tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi…pe… ayaṃ vuccati sakkāyadiṭṭhi.
rys_davids: Which are the states that make for the undoing of rebirth?⤵The four Paths that are the Unincluded.
original: Tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi…pe… ayaṃ vuccati sakkāyadiṭṭhi.
ai: Therein, what is identity view? ... This is called identity view.

text: 1015. Tattha katamā vicikicchā…pe… ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that make neither for the piling up, nor for the undoing of rebirth?⤵The results of good and bad states taking effect in the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or in the life that is Unincluded; [in other words], the four skandhas; those inoperative states, moreover, which are neither good nor bad, nor the result of karma; all [material] form also and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katamā vicikicchā…pe… ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
ai: Therein, what is doubt? ... This is called doubt.

text: 1016. Tattha katamo sīlabbataparāmāso…pe… ayaṃ vuccati sīlabbataparāmāso.
rys_davids: Which are the states that appertain to training?⤵The four Paths that are the Unincluded and the three lowest Fruits of the life of the recluse.
original: Tattha katamo sīlabbataparāmāso…pe… ayaṃ vuccati sīlabbataparāmāso.
ai: Therein, what is clinging to rites and rituals? ... This is called clinging to rites and rituals.

text: 1017. Imāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā. Tadekaṭṭho lobho, doso, moho – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetū. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā.
rys_davids: Which are the states not appertaining to training?⤵The topmost fruit—the fruit that is Arahantship.
original: Imāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā. Tadekaṭṭho lobho, doso, moho – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetū. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā.
ai: These three fetters; and defilements associated with them; the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them; bodily action, vocal action, mental action arising from them – these phenomena have causes to be abandoned by seeing. The three fetters – identity view, doubt, clinging to rites and rituals – these phenomena are to be abandoned by seeing. Greed, hatred, delusion associated with them – these phenomena are the causes to be abandoned by seeing. And defilements associated with them; the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them; bodily action, vocal action, mental action arising from them – these phenomena have causes to be abandoned by seeing.

text: 1018. Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Avaseso lobho, doso, moho – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetū. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
rys_davids: Which are the states neither appertaining, nor not appertaining to training?⤵The afore-mentioned states excepted, all other states, good, bad and indeterminate, relating to the worlds of Sense, Form and the Formless; all [material] form also and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Avaseso lobho, doso, moho – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetū. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Which phenomena have causes to be abandoned by development? The remaining greed, hatred, delusion – these phenomena are the causes to be abandoned by development. And defilements associated with them; the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them; bodily action, vocal action, mental action arising from them – these phenomena have causes to be abandoned by development.

text: 1019. Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are limited?⤵All states, good, bad and indeterminate, which relate to the universe of sense; in other words, the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Which phenomena have causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development? Excluding those phenomena, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and unincluded; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, consciousness aggregate; and all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena have causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development.

text: 1020. Katame dhammā ācayagāmino? Sāsavā kusalākusalā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā ācayagāmino.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are sublime?⤵States, good, bad and indeterminate, which relate to the worlds of Form and the Formless; [in other words], the four skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā ācayagāmino? Sāsavā kusalākusalā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā ācayagāmino.
ai: States that lead to accumulation are: Tainted wholesome and unwholesome phenomena of the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, mental formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate.

text: 1021. Katame dhammā apacayagāmino? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā – ime dhammā apacayagāmino.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are infinite?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā apacayagāmino? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā – ime dhammā apacayagāmino.
ai: States that lead to reduction are: The four supramundane paths.

text: 1022. Katame dhammā neva ācayagāmi na apacayagāmino? Kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā ; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā neva ācayagāmi na apacayagāmino.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have limited objects of thought?⤵Conscious states and their mental properties which arise in connexion with limited matters.
original: Katame dhammā neva ācayagāmi na apacayagāmino? Kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā ; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā neva ācayagāmi na apacayagāmino.
ai: States that lead neither to accumulation nor to reduction are: Results of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena of the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, mental formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate; functional states that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor kamma-results; all material phenomena; and the unconditioned element.

text: 1023. Katame dhammā sekkhā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, heṭṭhimāni ca tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā sekkhā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have sublime objects of thought?⤵Conscious states and their mental properties which arise in connexion with sublime matters.
original: Katame dhammā sekkhā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, heṭṭhimāni ca tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā sekkhā.
ai: States of trainees are: The four supramundane paths, and the three lower fruits of spiritual attainment.

text: 1024. Katame dhammā asekkhā? Upariṭṭhimaṃ [uparimaṃ (syā.)] arahattaphalaṃ – ime dhammā asekkhā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have infinite objects of thought?⤵Those emotional, perceptual and active states, as well as those of mind and mental properties, which arise in connexion with infinite things.
original: Katame dhammā asekkhā? Upariṭṭhimaṃ [uparimaṃ (syā.)] arahattaphalaṃ – ime dhammā asekkhā.
ai: States of perfected ones are: The highest fruit, Arahantship.

text: 1025. Katame dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā, avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are base?⤵The three roots of bad (karma)—greed, hate, dullness—the vices united with them; the four skandhas associated with them; the action, bodily, vocal and mental, springing from them.
original: Katame dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā, avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā.
ai: States that are neither of trainees nor of perfected ones are: Excluding those states, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena of the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, mental formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate; all material phenomena; and the unconditioned element.

text: 1026. Katame dhammā parittā? Sabbeva kāmāvacarā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā parittā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are of medium worth?⤵Co-Intoxicant states, good, bad and indeterminate, relating to the worlds of Sense, Form and the Formless; [in other words], the four skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā parittā? Sabbeva kāmāvacarā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā parittā.
ai: Limited states are: All wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena of the sense sphere; the matter aggregate, feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, mental formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate.

text: 1027. Katame dhammā mahaggatā? Rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, kusalābyākatā dhammā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā mahaggatā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are excellent?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā mahaggatā? Rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, kusalābyākatā dhammā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā mahaggatā.
ai: Sublime states are: Wholesome and indeterminate phenomena of the fine-material and immaterial spheres; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, mental formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate.

text: 1028. Katame dhammā appamāṇā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā appamāṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the states the wrongfulness of which is fixed as to its consequences?⤵The five acts that have immediate results, and those wrong views that are fixed in their consequences.
original: Katame dhammā appamāṇā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā appamāṇā.
ai: Illimitable states are: The supramundane paths, the fruits of the paths, and the unconditioned element.

text: 1029. Katame dhammā parittārammaṇā? Paritte dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā parittārammaṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the states the righteousness of which is fixed as to its consequences?⤵The four Paths that are the Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā parittārammaṇā? Paritte dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā parittārammaṇā.
ai: States with limited objects are: Those consciousness and mental factors that arise taking limited states as their object.

text: 1030. Katame dhammā mahaggatārammaṇā? Mahaggate dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā mahaggatārammaṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that do not entail fixed consequences?⤵The afore-mentioned states excepted, all other states, good, bad, and indeterminate, relating to the worlds of Sense, Form and the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; in other words, the four skandhas; all [material] form, moreover, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā mahaggatārammaṇā? Mahaggate dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā mahaggatārammaṇā.
ai: Which are the states that have a sublime object? Mental states and mental factors that arise taking sublime phenomena as their object are states with a sublime object.

text: 1031. Katame dhammā appamāṇārammaṇā? Appamāṇe dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā appamāṇārammaṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have the Path as their object of thought?⤵Conscious states and their mental properties which arise in connexion with the Noble Path.
original: Katame dhammā appamāṇārammaṇā? Appamāṇe dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā appamāṇārammaṇā.
ai: Which are the states that have an immeasurable object? Mental states and mental factors that arise taking immeasurable phenomena as their object are states with an immeasurable object.

text: 1032. Katame dhammā hīnā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā hīnā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are causally dependent upon the Path?⤵[Firstly] the four skandhas when associated with the stages of the Path as experienced by one who is conversant with the Path (the stages themselves being excepted).
original: Katame dhammā hīnā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā hīnā.
ai: Which are the inferior states? The three unwholesome roots—greed, hatred, delusion—and associated defilements; the feeling aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them; and bodily, verbal, and mental kamma originating from them are inferior states.

text: 1033. Katame dhammā majjhimā? Sāsavā kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā majjhimā.
rys_davids: [Secondly] the four skandhas when associated with the right views—these being both Path and Cause—of one who is conversant with the Path (the right views themselves being excepted).⤵[Thirdly] the four skandhas when associated with the states of freedom from lust, hate and dullness peculiar to one who is conversant with the Path.⤵Now, these [last named] states are the “Path-causes”; the former (the skandhas) are those states which are causally dependent upon the Path.
original: Katame dhammā majjhimā? Sāsavā kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā majjhimā.
ai: Which are the middling states? Wholesome and indeterminate states subject to taints, belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; and the form aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate are middling states.

text: 1034. Katame dhammā paṇītā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā paṇītā.
rys_davids: Which are the causes that are Path-governed?⤵[Firstly] those conscious states, and their mental properties, which in arising make the Noble Path their governor.⤵[Secondly] the four skandhas when associated with the investigation carried on by one who is conversant with the Path, and who is cultivating a way wherein investigation is the dominant factor.
original: Katame dhammā paṇītā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā paṇītā.
ai: Which are the sublime states? The unincluded paths, the fruits of the paths, and the unconditioned element (Nibbāna) are sublime states.

text: 1035. Katame dhammā micchattaniyatā? Pañca kammāni ānantarikāni, yā ca micchādiṭṭhiniyatā – ime dhammā micchattaniyatā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that “have arisen”?⤵Those states that have been born, have become, have been gotten, created, re-created, made manifest,—that have arisen, have come to pass, have happened, have supervened, have been caused to arise, are classed together among the things that have arisen, to wit, form, feeling, perception, synergies, consciousness.
original: Katame dhammā micchattaniyatā? Pañca kammāni ānantarikāni, yā ca micchādiṭṭhiniyatā – ime dhammā micchattaniyatā.
ai: Which are the states fixed in wrongness? The five heinous actions and wrong view fixed in certainty are states fixed in wrongness.

text: 1036. Katame dhammā sammattaniyatā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā – ime dhammā sammattaniyatā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have “not arisen”?⤵Those states that are unborn, have not become, have not been gotten, nor created, nor re-created, nor made manifest; that have not arisen nor come to pass; nor happened, nor supervened; that have not been caused to arise, that are classed together among the things that have not arisen, to wit, forms, feelings, perceptions, synergies, consciousness.
original: Katame dhammā sammattaniyatā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā – ime dhammā sammattaniyatā.
ai: Which are the states fixed in rightness? The four unincluded paths are states fixed in rightness.

text: 1037. Katame dhammā aniyatā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā, avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā aniyatā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are bound to arise?⤵The results of those good and bad states related to the worlds of Sense, Form and the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded, the consequences of which are not yet matured, to wit, the four skandhas and that form due to karma having been wrought which will arise.
original: Katame dhammā aniyatā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā, avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā aniyatā.
ai: Which are the indeterminate states? Except for those states, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and unincluded; the feeling aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate; all matter; and the unconditioned element (Nibbāna) are indeterminate states.

text: 1038. Katame dhammā maggārammaṇā? Ariyamaggaṃ ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā maggārammaṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are past?⤵Those states that are past, are extinct, dissolved, changed, terminated, exterminated; are past and classed among the things that are past; in other words, the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā maggārammaṇā? Ariyamaggaṃ ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā maggārammaṇā.
ai: Which are the states that have the Noble Path as their object? Mental states and mental factors that arise taking the Noble Path as their object are states with the Noble Path as their object.

text: 1039. Katame dhammā maggahetukā? Ariyamaggasamaṅgissa maggaṅgāni ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā maggahetukā. Ariyamaggasamaṅgissa sammādiṭṭhi maggo ceva hetu ca, sammādiṭṭhiṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā maggahetukā. Ariyamaggasamaṅgissa alobho, adoso, amoho – ime dhammā maggahetū. Taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā maggahetukā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are future?⤵The states that are unborn, that have not become, not been gotten, nor created, nor re-created, nor made manifest; that have not arisen, nor come to pass, nor happened, nor supervened; that have not arrived, and are classed among the things that have not arrived.
original: Katame dhammā maggahetukā? Ariyamaggasamaṅgissa maggaṅgāni ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā maggahetukā. Ariyamaggasamaṅgissa sammādiṭṭhi maggo ceva hetu ca, sammādiṭṭhiṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā maggahetukā. Ariyamaggasamaṅgissa alobho, adoso, amoho – ime dhammā maggahetū. Taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā maggahetukā.
ai: Which are the states rooted in the Path? For one endowed with the Noble Path, the feeling aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate associated with the path factors (excluding the path factors themselves) are states rooted in the Path. For one endowed with the Noble Path, right view is both path and root; the feeling aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate associated with it (excluding right view itself) are states rooted in the Path. For one endowed with the Noble Path, non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion are the roots of the Path; the feeling aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them are states rooted in the Path.

text: 1040. Katame dhammā maggādhipatino? Ariyamaggaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā maggādhipatino. Ariyamaggasamaṅgissa vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayantassa vīmaṃsaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā maggādhipatino.
rys_davids: Which are the things that are present?⤵Those states that have been born, have become, have been gotten, created, re-created, made manifest; that have arisen, have come to pass, have supervened, have been caused to arise; that have arisen over against and are classed among the things that have so arisen.
original: Katame dhammā maggādhipatino? Ariyamaggaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā maggādhipatino. Ariyamaggasamaṅgissa vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayantassa vīmaṃsaṃ ṭhapetvā; taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā maggādhipatino.
ai: Which are the dhammas that have the path as their dominant condition? Those consciousness and mental factors that arise making the Noble Path predominant. These dhammas have the path as their dominant condition. For one endowed with the Noble Path, cultivating the path with investigation as predominance, excluding investigation; the associated feeling aggregate...pe...consciousness aggregate. These dhammas have the path as their dominant condition.

text: 1041. Katame dhammā uppannā? Ye dhammā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā uppannā uppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ [rūpā (bahūsu)], vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā uppannā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have the past … future … present as their object of thought?⤵Conscious states and their mental properties which arise in connexion with states that are past … future … present.
original: Katame dhammā uppannā? Ye dhammā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā uppannā uppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ [rūpā (bahūsu)], vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā uppannā.
ai: Which are the arisen dhammas?⤵Those dhammas that are born, become, arisen, produced, manifested, appeared, arisen, come to pass, supervened, caused to arise, and are included in the category of arisen: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness. These dhammas are arisen.

text: 1042. Katame dhammā anuppannā? Ye dhammā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anuppannā anuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā anuppannā.
original: Katame dhammā anuppannā? Ye dhammā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anuppannā anuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā anuppannā.
ai: Which are the not arisen dhammas? Those dhammas that are not born, not become, not arisen, not produced, not manifested, not appeared, not arisen, not come to pass, not supervened, not caused to arise, and are included in the category of not arisen: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness. These dhammas are not arisen.

text: 1043. Katame dhammā uppādino? Kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ avipakkavipākānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; yañca rūpaṃ kammassa katattā uppajjissati – ime dhammā uppādino.
original: Katame dhammā uppādino? Kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ avipakkavipākānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; yañca rūpaṃ kammassa katattā uppajjissati – ime dhammā uppādino.
ai: Which are the dhammas capable of arising? The unripened results of wholesome and unwholesome dhammas, which are resultant, belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and not included in these; the feeling aggregate...pe...consciousness aggregate; and also the form that will arise due to kamma. These dhammas are capable of arising.

text: 1044. Katame dhammā atītā? Ye dhammā atītā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā uppajjitvā vigatā atītā atītaṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā atītā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are personal?⤵Those states which, for this or that being, are of the self, self-referable, one's own, individual, the issue of grasping; [in other words,] the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā atītā? Ye dhammā atītā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā uppajjitvā vigatā atītā atītaṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā atītā.
ai: Which are the past dhammas? Those dhammas that are past, ceased, gone, changed, set, completely set, having arisen and then gone, past, and are included in the category of past: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness. These dhammas are past.

text: 1045. Katame dhammā anāgatā? Ye dhammā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anāgatā anāgataṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā anāgatā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are external?⤵Those states which, for this or that other being, for other individuals, are of the self, self-referable, their own, individual, grasped at; [in other words,] the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā anāgatā? Ye dhammā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anāgatā anāgataṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā anāgatā.
ai: Which are the future dhammas? Those dhammas that are not born, not become, not arisen, not produced, not manifested, not appeared, not arisen, not come to pass, not supervened, not caused to arise, future, and are included in the category of future: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness. These dhammas are future.

text: 1046. Katame dhammā paccuppannā? Ye dhammā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannā paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā paccuppannā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are personal-external?⤵States which are both [personal and external].
original: Katame dhammā paccuppannā? Ye dhammā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannā paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā paccuppannā.
ai: Which are the present dhammas?⤵Those dhammas that are born, become, arisen, produced, manifested, appeared, arisen, come to pass, supervened, caused to arise, present, and are included in the category of present: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness. These dhammas are present.

text: 1047. Katame dhammā atītārammaṇā? Atīte dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā atītārammaṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have an object of thought concerning the self … concerning that which is external [to the self] … concerning that which is “personal-external”?⤵Conscious states and their mental properties, which arise in connexion with states of the self … states that are external … states that are personal-external.
original: Katame dhammā atītārammaṇā? Atīte dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā atītārammaṇā.
ai: Which are the dhammas with past objects?⤵Those consciousness and mental factors that arise taking past dhammas as their object. These dhammas have past objects.

text: 1048. Katame dhammā anāgatārammaṇā? Anāgate dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā anāgatārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā anāgatārammaṇā? Anāgate dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā anāgatārammaṇā.
ai: Which are the dhammas with future objects?⤵Those consciousness and mental factors that arise taking future dhammas as their object. These dhammas have future objects.

text: 1049. Katame dhammā paccuppannārammaṇā? Paccuppanne dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā paccuppannārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā paccuppannārammaṇā? Paccuppanne dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā paccuppannārammaṇā.
ai: Which are the dhammas with present objects?⤵Those consciousness and mental factors that arise taking present dhammas as their object. These dhammas have present objects.

text: 1050. Katame dhammā ajjhattā? Ye dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyatā pāṭipuggalikā upādiṇṇā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā ajjhattā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are both visible and reacting?⤵The sphere of visible shapes.
original: Katame dhammā ajjhattā? Ye dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyatā pāṭipuggalikā upādiṇṇā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā ajjhattā.
ai: What are internal phenomena?⤵Those phenomena of those beings that are internal, personal, fixed, pertaining to the individual, and appropriated: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness – these phenomena are internal.

text: 1051. Katame dhammā bahiddhā? Ye dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyatā pāṭipuggalikā upādiṇṇā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā bahiddhā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are invisible, but reacting?⤵The spheres of the five senses and the spheres of sound, odour, taste, and the tangible.
original: Katame dhammā bahiddhā? Ye dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyatā pāṭipuggalikā upādiṇṇā, rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā bahiddhā.
ai: What are external phenomena?⤵Those phenomena of other beings, other individuals, that are internal, personal, fixed, pertaining to the individual, and appropriated: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness – these phenomena are external.

text: 1052. Katame dhammā ajjhattabahiddhā? Tadubhayaṃ – ime dhammā ajjhattabahiddhā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are both invisible and non-reacting?⤵The four skandhas; that [material] form, moreover, which, being invisible and non-reacting, is yet included in the sphere of [mental] states; also unconditioned element.⤵[End of] the Triplets.⤵A Buddhist Manual of Psychological Ethics , a rys_davids of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī, Compendium of States or Phenomena, by Caroline A.F.
