original: Katame dhammā ajjhattabahiddhā? Tadubhayaṃ – ime dhammā ajjhattabahiddhā.
ai: What are internal and external phenomena?⤵Both of these – these phenomena are internal and external.

text: 1053. Katame dhammā ajjhattārammaṇā? Ajjhatte dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā ajjhattārammaṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are root-conditions?⤵The three root-conditions of good (karma).⤵The three root-conditions of bad (karma).⤵The three root-conditions of the indeterminate: [these are]⤵The nine root-conditions operative in the sensuous universe.⤵The six root-conditions operative in the universe of Form.⤵The six root-conditions operative in the universe of the Formless.⤵The six root-conditions operative in the life that is the Unincluded.⤵(A) In this connexion
original: Katame dhammā ajjhattārammaṇā? Ajjhatte dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā ajjhattārammaṇā.
ai: What are phenomena with internal objects?⤵Those consciousness and mental factors that arise taking internal phenomena as object – these phenomena have internal objects.

text: 1054. Katame dhammā bahiddhārammaṇā? Bahiddhā dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā bahiddhārammaṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the three causes of good (karma)?⤵Disinterestedness, absence of hate and dullness.⤵In this connexion,
original: Katame dhammā bahiddhārammaṇā? Bahiddhā dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā bahiddhārammaṇā.
ai: What are phenomena with external objects?⤵Those consciousness and mental factors that arise taking external phenomena as object – these phenomena have external objects.

text: 1055. Katame dhammā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā? Ajjhattabahiddhā dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā.
rys_davids: What is disinterestedness?⤵The absence of greed, showing greed, greediness is the absence of lust, of lusting, of lustfulness; the absence of covetousness, that absence of greed which is the root of good (karma).
original: Katame dhammā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā? Ajjhattabahiddhā dhamme ārabbha ye uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā.
ai: What are phenomena with internal and external objects?⤵Those consciousness and mental factors that arise taking internal and external phenomena as object – these phenomena have internal and external objects.

text: 1056. Katame dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā? Rūpāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā.
rys_davids: What is the absence of hate?⤵The absence of hate, hating, hatred; love, loving, loving disposition; tender care, forbearance, considerateness; seeking the [general] good, compassion; the absence of malice, of malignity; that absence of hate which is the root of good (karma).
original: Katame dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā? Rūpāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā.
ai: What are visible and impinging phenomena?⤵The visible object – these phenomena are visible and impinging.

text: 1057. Katame dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ , rasāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā.
rys_davids: What is the absence of dullness?⤵Knowledge about ill, about the uprising of ill, about the cessation of ill, and about the way leading to the cessation of ill; knowledge about the former things, about the latter things, about both taken together; knowledge about the assignable causation of causally determined states—even that kind of insight which is understanding, search, research, searching the Truth, etc. [Continue as in § 34 ] . These are the three causes of good (karma).⤵(B) In this connexion
original: Katame dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ , rasāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā.
ai: What are invisible and impinging phenomena?⤵The eye-base, ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, sound-base, smell-base, taste-base, tangible-base – these phenomena are invisible and impinging.

text: 1058. Katame dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ; asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā.
rys_davids: Which are the three causes of bad (karma)?⤵Greed, hate, dullness.⤵In this connexion,
original: Katame dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho; yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ; asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā.
ai: What are invisible and non-impinging phenomena?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, mental formations aggregate, consciousness aggregate; and that matter which is invisible and non-impinging, included in the dhamma-base; and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are invisible and non-impinging.

text: Tikaṃ.
original: Tikaṃ.
ai: The Triad.

text: Dukanikkhepaṃ
original: Dukanikkhepaṃ
ai: Exposition of Dyads

text: Hetugocchakaṃ
original: Hetugocchakaṃ
ai: Cluster of Roots

text: 1059. Katame dhammā hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū, nava kāmāvacarahetū cha rūpāvacarahetū, cha arūpāvacarahetū, cha apariyāpannahetū.
rys_davids: What is greed?⤵That which is⤵lust ( rāgo ),⤵passion ( sarāgo ),⤵seducing ( anunayo ),⤵compliance ( anurodho ),⤵delighting in ( nandī ),⤵taking lustful delight in ( nandī-rāgo ),⤵heart's passion ( cittassasarāgo ),⤵wanting ( icchā ),⤵languishing ( mucchā ),⤵gulping at, devouring ( ajjhosānaṃ ),⤵cupidity ( gedho ),⤵voracity ( paligedho ),⤵cleaving to ( saṇgo ),⤵a slough ( panko ),⤵longing ( ejā ),⤵illusion ( māyā ),⤵genitrix ( janikā ),⤵progenitrix ( sañjananī ),⤵seamstress ( sibbanī ),⤵she who ensnares ( jālinī ),⤵the flowing stream ( saritā ),⤵she who is diffused ( visattikā ),⤵the thread ( suttaṃ ),⤵diffusion ( visatā ),⤵she who urges ( āyūhanī ),⤵the consort ( dutiyā ),⤵aiming at ( paniḍhi ),⤵she who leads to rebirth ( bhavanetti ),⤵the forest ( vanaṃ ),⤵the jungle ( vanatho ),⤵intimacy ( santhavo ),⤵fondness ( sineho ),⤵affection ( apekkhā ),⤵connexion ( paṭibandhu ),⤵appetite for ( āsā ),⤵hoping for ( āsiṃsanā ),⤵anticipation ( āsiṃsitattaṃ ),⤵appetite for visual shapes ( rūpāsā , etc.), for sounds, for odours, for tastes, for the tangible, for getting, for wealth, for children, for life,⤵mumbling ( jappā ), mumbling on, and over,⤵muttering,⤵murmuring,⤵self-indulgence ( loluppaṃ ),⤵self-indulging,⤵intemperateness,⤵agitation ( puñcikatā ),⤵longing for the agreeable ( sādukamyatā ),⤵incestuous passion ( adhammarāgo ),⤵lawless greed ( visamalobho ),⤵wish ( nikanti ),⤵hungering for ( nikāmanā ),⤵entreating ( patthanā ),⤵envying ( pihanā ),⤵imploring ( sampatthanā ),⤵craving for sensual indulgence ( kāmataṇhā ), for existence ( bhavataṇhā ), for non-existence ( vibhava-taṇhā ), for [material] form, for immateriality, for annihilation, for visible shapes, for sounds, for smells, for tastes, for the tangible, for mental states ( dhammataṇhā ),⤵a flood ( ogho ),⤵a yoke ( yogo ),⤵a tie ( gantho ),⤵grasping ( upādānaṃ ),⤵obstruction ( āvaraṇaṃ ),⤵hindrance ( nīvaraṇaṃ ),⤵covering ( chadanaṃ ),⤵bondage ( bandhanaṃ ),⤵depravity ( upakkileso ),⤵latent bias ( anusayo ),⤵obsession ( pariyuṭṭhānaṃ ),⤵a creeper ( latā ),⤵avarice ( vevicchaṃ ),⤵root of ill,⤵source of ill ( dukkhanidānaṃ ),⤵production of ill ( dukkhappabhavo ),⤵Māra's trap ( mārapāso ),⤵Māra's fish-hook ( mārabalisaṃ ),⤵Māra's domain ( māravisayo ),⤵craving, the flux of craving for ( sandataṇhā ), the fishing-net of ( jalaṃtaṇhā ), the leash of ( gaddulataṇhā ),⤵the ocean ( samuddo ),⤵covetousness ( abhijjhā ),⤵greed as the root of evil—⤵this is what is called greed.
original: Katame dhammā hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū, nava kāmāvacarahetū cha rūpāvacarahetū, cha arūpāvacarahetū, cha apariyāpannahetū.
ai: Which states are roots? Three wholesome roots, three unwholesome roots, three indeterminate roots, nine sense-sphere roots, six fine-material sphere roots, six immaterial sphere roots, six supramundane roots.

text: 1060. Tattha katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho, adoso, amoho.
rys_davids: What is hate?⤵When annoyance springs up at the thought: he has done me harm, is doing, will do me harm; he has done harm, is doing harm, will do harm to someone dear and precious to me; he has conferred a benefit, is conferring, will confer a benefit on someone I dislike and object to; or when annoyance springs up groundlessly: all such vexation of spirit, resentment, repugnance, hostility; ill-temper, irritation, indignation; hate, antipathy, abhorrence; mental disorder, detestation; anger, fuming, wrath; hate, hating, hatred; disorder, getting upset, derangement; opposition, hostility; churlishness, abruptness, disgust of heart—this is what is called hate.
original: Tattha katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho, adoso, amoho.
ai: Among these, which are the three wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion.

text: 1061. Tattha katamo alobho? Yo alobho alubbhanā alubbhitattaṃ asārāgo asārajjanā asārajjitattaṃ anabhijjhā alobho kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati alobho.
rys_davids: What is dullness?⤵Lack of knowledge about Ill, lack of knowledge about the uprising of Ill, lack of knowledge about the cessation of Ill, lack of knowledge about the way leading to the cessation of Ill; lack of knowledge about the former things, about the latter things, and about both taken together; lack of knowledge about the assignable causation of causally determined states—even all that kind of lack of knowledge which is lack of insight, of understanding, of comprehension, of enlightenment, of penetration, of grasping, of sounding, of judging, of reflection, of perspicacity; unwisdom, childishness, unintelligence, the dullness that is stupidity, obtuseness, ignorance, a flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent bias of ignorance, the being obsessed by ignorance, the barrier of ignorance, the dullness that is the root of evil—this is called dullness.⤵These are the three causes of bad [karma].⤵(C) In this connexion
original: Tattha katamo alobho? Yo alobho alubbhanā alubbhitattaṃ asārāgo asārajjanā asārajjitattaṃ anabhijjhā alobho kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati alobho.
ai: Among these, what is non-greed?⤵That which is non-greed, not being greedy, the state of not being greedy, non-attachment, not being attached, the state of not being attached, non-covetousness, non-greed, a wholesome root—this is called non-greed.

text: 1062. Tattha katamo adoso? Yo adoso adussanā adussitattaṃ metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ anuddā anuddāyanā anudāyitattaṃ hitesitā anukampā abyāpādo abyāpajjo adoso kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati adoso.
rys_davids: Which are the three causes of the indeterminate?⤵The absence of greed, hate and dullness [coming to pass] as the result of good states or as inoperative indeterminates.
original: Tattha katamo adoso? Yo adoso adussanā adussitattaṃ metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ anuddā anuddāyanā anudāyitattaṃ hitesitā anukampā abyāpādo abyāpajjo adoso kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati adoso.
ai: Among these, what is non-hatred?⤵That which is non-hatred, not being hateful, the state of not being hateful, loving-kindness, being loving, the state of being loving, sympathy, being sympathetic, the state of being sympathetic, wishing for welfare, compassion, non-ill-will, not being ill-willed, non-hatred, a wholesome root—this is called non-hatred.

text: 1063. Tattha katamo amoho? Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ, pubbante ñāṇaṃ, aparante ñāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante ñāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ, yā evarūpā paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo sallakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇā paṇḍiccaṃ kosallaṃ nepuññaṃ vebhabyā cintā upaparikkhā bhūrī medhā pariṇāyikā vipassanā sampajaññaṃ patodo paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ paññāsatthaṃ paññāpāsādo paññāāloko paññāobhāso paññāpajjoto paññāratanaṃ amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati amoho.
rys_davids: Which are the nine root-conditions operative in the sensuous universe ( kāmavacarahetū )?⤵The three roots of good [karma], the three roots of bad [karma], the three roots of indeterminate [states]—these are the nine.
original: Tattha katamo amoho? Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ, pubbante ñāṇaṃ, aparante ñāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante ñāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ, yā evarūpā paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo sallakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇā paṇḍiccaṃ kosallaṃ nepuññaṃ vebhabyā cintā upaparikkhā bhūrī medhā pariṇāyikā vipassanā sampajaññaṃ patodo paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ paññāsatthaṃ paññāpāsādo paññāāloko paññāobhāso paññāpajjoto paññāratanaṃ amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati amoho.
ai: Among these, what is non-delusion?⤵Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the past, knowledge of the future, knowledge of both past and future, knowledge of dependent arising in conditionally arisen states;⤵that which is such wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, observation, close observation, sagacity, skill, proficiency, analysis, thought, examination, insight, intelligence, leading wisdom, insight, clear comprehension, goad, wisdom, wisdom faculty, power of wisdom, wisdom-weapon, wisdom-palace, wisdom-light, wisdom-radiance, wisdom-lamp, wisdom-gem, non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called non-delusion.

text: Ime tayo kusalahetū.
original: Ime tayo kusalahetū.
ai: These are the three wholesome roots.

text: 1064. Tattha katame tayo akusalahetū? Lobho, doso, moho.
rys_davids: Which are the six roots operative in the universe of Form?⤵The three roots of good [karma], the three roots of indeterminate [states]—these are the six.
original: Tattha katame tayo akusalahetū? Lobho, doso, moho.
ai: Among these, which are the three unwholesome roots? Greed, hatred, delusion.

text: 1065. Tattha katamo lobho? Yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandīrāgo [nandirāgo (sī.)] cittassa sārāgo icchā mucchā ajjhosānaṃ gedho paligedho saṅgo paṅko ejā māyā janikā sañjananī sibbinī [sibbanī (sī.)] jālinī saritā visattikā suttaṃ visaṭā āyūhinī [āyūhanī (sī. syā.)] dutiyā paṇidhi bhavanetti vanaṃ vanatho santhavo sineho apekkhā paṭibandhu āsā āsisanā āsisitattaṃ [āsiṃsanā āsiṃsitattaṃ (sī. syā.)] rūpāsā saddāsā gandhāsā rasāsā phoṭṭhabbāsā lābhāsā dhanāsā puttāsā jīvitāsā jappā pajappā abhijappā jappā jappanā jappitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañjikatā [puñcikatā (syā.) pucchikatā (sī.)] sādhukamyatā adhammarāgo visamalobho nikanti nikāmanā patthanā pihanā sampatthanā kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā rūpataṇhā arūpataṇhā nirodhataṇhā rūpataṇhā saddataṇhā gandhataṇhā rasataṇhā phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dhammataṇhā ogho yogo gantho upādānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ chādanaṃ bandhanaṃ upakkileso anusayo pariyuṭṭhānaṃ latā vevicchaṃ dukkhamūlaṃ dukkhanidānaṃ dukkhappabhavo mārapāso mārabaḷisaṃ māravisayo taṇhānadī taṇhājālaṃ taṇhāgaddulaṃ taṇhāsamuddo abhijjhā lobho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati lobho.
rys_davids: Which are the six roots operative in the universe of the Formless?⤵The three roots of good [karma], the three roots of indeterminate [states]—these are the six.
original: Tattha katamo lobho? Yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandīrāgo [nandirāgo (sī.)] cittassa sārāgo icchā mucchā ajjhosānaṃ gedho paligedho saṅgo paṅko ejā māyā janikā sañjananī sibbinī [sibbanī (sī.)] jālinī saritā visattikā suttaṃ visaṭā āyūhinī [āyūhanī (sī. syā.)] dutiyā paṇidhi bhavanetti vanaṃ vanatho santhavo sineho apekkhā paṭibandhu āsā āsisanā āsisitattaṃ [āsiṃsanā āsiṃsitattaṃ (sī. syā.)] rūpāsā saddāsā gandhāsā rasāsā phoṭṭhabbāsā lābhāsā dhanāsā puttāsā jīvitāsā jappā pajappā abhijappā jappā jappanā jappitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañjikatā [puñcikatā (syā.) pucchikatā (sī.)] sādhukamyatā adhammarāgo visamalobho nikanti nikāmanā patthanā pihanā sampatthanā kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā rūpataṇhā arūpataṇhā nirodhataṇhā rūpataṇhā saddataṇhā gandhataṇhā rasataṇhā phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dhammataṇhā ogho yogo gantho upādānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ chādanaṃ bandhanaṃ upakkileso anusayo pariyuṭṭhānaṃ latā vevicchaṃ dukkhamūlaṃ dukkhanidānaṃ dukkhappabhavo mārapāso mārabaḷisaṃ māravisayo taṇhānadī taṇhājālaṃ taṇhāgaddulaṃ taṇhāsamuddo abhijjhā lobho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati lobho.
ai: Among these, what is greed?⤵That which is lust,⤵passion,⤵seducing,⤵compliance,⤵delighting in,⤵taking lustful delight in,⤵heart's passion,⤵wanting,⤵languishing,⤵gulping at, devouring,⤵cupidity,⤵voracity,⤵cleaving to,⤵a slough,⤵longing,⤵illusion,⤵genitrix,⤵progenitrix,⤵seamstress,⤵she who ensnares,⤵the flowing stream,⤵she who is diffused,⤵the thread,⤵diffusion,⤵she who urges,⤵the consort,⤵aiming at,⤵she who leads to rebirth,⤵the forest,⤵the jungle,⤵intimacy,⤵fondness,⤵affection,⤵connexion,⤵appetite for,⤵hoping for,⤵anticipation,⤵appetite for visual shapes, for sounds, for odours, for tastes, for the tangible,⤵for getting, for wealth, for children, for life,⤵mumbling, mumbling on and over, muttering, murmuring,⤵self-indulgence, self-indulging, intemperateness,⤵agitation,⤵longing for the agreeable,⤵incestuous passion,⤵lawless greed,⤵wish,⤵hungering for,⤵entreating,⤵envying,⤵imploring,⤵craving for sensual indulgence, for existence, for non-existence,⤵for [material] form, for immateriality, for annihilation,⤵for visible shapes, for sounds, for smells, for tastes, for the tangible, for mental states,⤵a flood,⤵a yoke,⤵a tie,⤵grasping,⤵obstruction,⤵hindrance,⤵covering,⤵bondage,⤵depravity,⤵latent bias,⤵obsession,⤵a creeper,⤵avarice,⤵root of ill,⤵source of ill,⤵production of ill,⤵Māra's trap,⤵Māra's fish-hook,⤵Māra's domain,⤵craving, the flux of craving, the fishing-net of craving, the leash of craving,⤵the ocean of craving,⤵covetousness,⤵greed as the root of evil—this is what is called greed.

text: 1066. Tattha katamo doso? Anatthaṃ me acarīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me caratīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me carissatīti āghāto jāyati, piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati. Yo evarūpo cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati doso.
rys_davids: Which are the six roots operative in the Unincluded?⤵The three roots of good [karma], the three roots of indeterminate [states]—these are the six.⤵In this connexion,
original: Tattha katamo doso? Anatthaṃ me acarīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me caratīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me carissatīti āghāto jāyati, piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati. Yo evarūpo cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati doso.
ai: What is hatred? Resentment arises thinking: "He harmed me," "He is harming me," "He will harm me." Or thinking: "He harmed my dear and beloved one," "He is harming my dear and beloved one," "He will harm my dear and beloved one." Or thinking: "He benefited my disliked and unloved one," "He is benefiting my disliked and unloved one," "He will benefit my disliked and unloved one." Or resentment arises without reason. This mental resentment, repugnance, opposition, anger, wrath, ill-will, mental corruption, displeasure of mind, fury, fierceness, lack of satisfaction of mind—this is called hatred.

text: 1067. Tattha katamo moho? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ, pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃ, yaṃ evarūpaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṃgāhanā apariyogāhanā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati moho.
rys_davids: Which are the three roots of good [karma]?⤵The absence of greed, hate and dullness.⤵In this connexion,
original: Tattha katamo moho? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ, pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃ, yaṃ evarūpaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṃgāhanā apariyogāhanā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati moho.
ai: What is delusion? Ignorance of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path to its cessation. Ignorance of the past, future, and both past and future. Ignorance of dependent arising in conditionally arisen phenomena. This kind of ignorance, non-seeing, non-comprehension, non-awakening, non-realization, non-grasping, non-penetration, non-reflection, non-reviewing, non-direct knowledge, dullness, folly, lack of clear comprehension, delusion, confusion, ignorance, flood of ignorance, bond of ignorance, latent disposition of ignorance, obsession of ignorance, root of unwholesome kamma—this is called delusion.

text: Ime tayo akusalahetū.
original: Ime tayo akusalahetū.
ai: These are the three unwholesome roots.

text: 1068. Tattha katame tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ vā dhammānaṃ vipākato kiriyābyākatesu vā dhammesu alobho adoso amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū.
rys_davids: What is the absence of greed … of hate … of dullness?⤵Answers as in §§ 1055 – 1057 , omitting, in § 1056 , from “hatred” to “the absence of malice” exclusively.⤵These are the three root conditions of good [karma].⤵(D) In this connexion
original: Tattha katame tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ vā dhammānaṃ vipākato kiriyābyākatesu vā dhammesu alobho adoso amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū.
ai: Which are the three indeterminate roots? Non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, whether as results of wholesome states or as functional indeterminate states—these are the three indeterminate roots.

text: 1069. Tattha katame nava kāmāvacarahetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū – ime nava kāmāvacarahetū.
original: Tattha katame nava kāmāvacarahetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū – ime nava kāmāvacarahetū.
ai: Which are the nine sense-sphere roots? The three wholesome roots, the three unwholesome roots, the three indeterminate roots—these are the nine sense-sphere roots.

text: 1070. Tattha katame cha rūpāvacarahetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū – ime cha rūpāvacarahetū.
original: Tattha katame cha rūpāvacarahetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū – ime cha rūpāvacarahetū.
ai: Which are the six fine-material-sphere roots? The three wholesome roots, the three indeterminate roots—these are the six fine-material-sphere roots.

text: 1071. Tattha katame cha arūpāvacarahetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū – ime cha arūpāvacarahetū.
rys_davids: Which are the three roots of indeterminate [states]?⤵The absence of greed, hate and dullness coming to pass as the effect of good states—these are the three.⤵These are the six root-conditions operative in the Unincluded.⤵These are the states which are root-conditions.
original: Tattha katame cha arūpāvacarahetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū – ime cha arūpāvacarahetū.
ai: Which are the six immaterial-sphere roots? The three wholesome roots, the three indeterminate roots—these are the six immaterial-sphere roots.

text: 1072. Tattha katame cha apariyāpannahetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū – ime cha apariyāpannahetū.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not root-conditions?⤵Every state, good, bad and indeterminate, whether related to the worlds of Sense, of Form, of the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded, except the states enumerated above; [in other words] the four skandhas; all [material] form also and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katame cha apariyāpannahetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū – ime cha apariyāpannahetū.
ai: Which are the six unincluded roots? The three wholesome roots, the three indeterminate roots—these are the six unincluded roots.

text: 1073. Tattha katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho, adoso, amoho.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have root-conditions as concomitants?⤵Those states, [to wit] the four skandhas, which have as concomitant roots the states enumerated above.
original: Tattha katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho, adoso, amoho.
ai: Which are the three wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion.

text: 1074. Tattha katamo alobho? Yo alobho alubbhanā alubbhitattaṃ asārāgo asārajjanā asārajjitattaṃ anabhijjhā alobho kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati alobho.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have not concomitant roots?⤵Those states, [to wit] the four skandhas, all [material] form also, and unconditioned element, which have not as concomitant roots the states enumerated above.
original: Tattha katamo alobho? Yo alobho alubbhanā alubbhitattaṃ asārāgo asārajjanā asārajjitattaṃ anabhijjhā alobho kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati alobho.
ai: What is non-greed? That non-greed, not being greedy, the state of not being greedy, non-attachment, not being attached, the state of not being attached, non-covetousness, non-greed, the root of wholesome kamma—this is called non-greed.

text: 1075. Tattha katamo adoso? Yo adoso adussanā adussitattaṃ…pe… abyāpādo abyāpajjo adoso kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati adoso.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are associated with a root-condition?⤵The states, [to wit] the four skandhas, which are associated with those states enumerated above.
original: Tattha katamo adoso? Yo adoso adussanā adussitattaṃ…pe… abyāpādo abyāpajjo adoso kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati adoso.
ai: Therein, what is non-hatred? That which is non-hatred, non-aversion, non-malice, non-ill-will, non-harming, is the wholesome root of non-hatred. This is called non-hatred.

text: 1076. Tattha katamo amoho ? Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ, pubbante ñāṇaṃ, aparante ñāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante ñāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ, yā evarūpā paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo sallakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇā paṇḍiccaṃ kosallaṃ nepuññaṃ vebhabyā cintā upaparikkhā bhūrī medhā pariṇāyikā vipassanā sampajaññaṃ patodo paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ paññāsatthaṃ paññāpāsādo paññāāloko paññāobhāso paññāpajjoto paññāratanaṃ amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati amoho.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not associated with a root-condition?⤵The states, [to wit] the four skandhas, all [material] form also, and unconditioned element, which are not associated with the states enumerated above.
original: Tattha katamo amoho ? Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ, pubbante ñāṇaṃ, aparante ñāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante ñāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ, yā evarūpā paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo sallakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇā paṇḍiccaṃ kosallaṃ nepuññaṃ vebhabyā cintā upaparikkhā bhūrī medhā pariṇāyikā vipassanā sampajaññaṃ patodo paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ paññāsatthaṃ paññāpāsādo paññāāloko paññāobhāso paññāpajjoto paññāratanaṃ amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati amoho.
ai: Therein, what is non-delusion? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the past, knowledge of the future, knowledge of both past and future, knowledge of dependent arising in conditionally arisen phenomena; such wisdom, discernment, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, observation, close observation, repeated observation, sagacity, skill, dexterity, analysis, thought, examination, wisdom, intelligence, guidance, insight, clear comprehension, goad, wisdom, wisdom faculty, power of wisdom, weapon of wisdom, palace of wisdom, light of wisdom, aura of wisdom, radiance of wisdom, jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a path factor, included in the path – this is called non-delusion.

text: Ime tayo kusalahetū.
original: Ime tayo kusalahetū.
ai: These are the three wholesome roots.

text: 1077. Tattha katame tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākato alobho adoso amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū. Ime cha apariyāpannahetū – ime dhammā hetū.
rys_davids: Which are the states that both are root-conditions and have such as their concomitants?⤵Greed with dullness is both. Dullness with greed is both. Hate with dullness is both. Dullness with hate is both.⤵The absence of greed, the absence of hate, the absence of dullness—these also, taken one with the other, both are root-conditions and have such as their concomitants.
original: Tattha katame tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākato alobho adoso amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū. Ime cha apariyāpannahetū – ime dhammā hetū.
ai: Therein, what are the three indeterminate roots? Non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, as results of wholesome phenomena – these are the three indeterminate roots. These six are the unclassified roots – these phenomena are roots.

text: 1078. Katame dhammā na hetū? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā, avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na hetū.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have root-conditions as their concomitants, but are not root-conditions?⤵The states, [to wit] the four skandhas, which have as their concomitant roots those states [enumerated above as roots], the latter states themselves excepted.
original: Katame dhammā na hetū? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā, avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na hetū.
ai: Which phenomena are not roots? Excluding those phenomena, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena of the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and not included in any sphere; the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formation aggregate, the consciousness aggregate; all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not roots.

text: 1079. Katame dhammā sahetukā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sahetukā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sahetukā .
rys_davids: Which are the states that are both root-conditions and associated with such?
original: Katame dhammā sahetukā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sahetukā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sahetukā .
ai: Which phenomena are root-conditioned?⤵The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formation aggregate, the consciousness aggregate, which are root-conditioned by those phenomena (the roots) – these phenomena are root-conditioned.

text: 1080. Katame dhammā ahetukā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā ahetukā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā ahetukā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are associated with a root-condition, but are not such?⤵Answers identical with those in the foregoing pair.
original: Katame dhammā ahetukā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā ahetukā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā ahetukā.
ai: Which phenomena are rootless? The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formation aggregate, the consciousness aggregate, which are rootless by those phenomena (the roots); all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are rootless.

text: 1081. Katame dhammā hetusampayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā hetusampayuttā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not root-conditions, but have such as their concomitant?⤵The states, [to wit] the four skandhas, which are not the root-conditions of those states enumerated above, but which have any of them as their concomitants.
original: Katame dhammā hetusampayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā hetusampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with roots?⤵The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formation aggregate, the consciousness aggregate, which are associated with those phenomena (the roots) – these phenomena are associated with roots.

text: 1082. Katame dhammā hetuvippayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā hetuvippayuttā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not root-conditions and have not such as their concomitants?⤵The states, [to wit] the four skandhas, all [material] form also, and unconditioned element, which neither are the root-conditions of those states enumerated above, nor have any of them as their concomitants.⤵The Short Intermediate Set of Pairs ( cūḷantaradukaṃ )
original: Katame dhammā hetuvippayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā hetuvippayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from roots?⤵The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formation aggregate, the consciousness aggregate, which are dissociated from those phenomena (the roots); all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are dissociated from roots.

text: 1083. Katame dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca? Lobho mohena hetu ceva sahetuko ca, moho lobhena hetu ceva sahetuko ca, doso mohena hetu ceva sahetuko ca, moho dosena hetu ceva sahetuko ca; alobho adoso amoho, te aññamaññaṃ hetū ceva sahetukā ca – ime dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are causally related?⤵The five skandhas, to wit, the skandhas of [material] form, feeling, perception, synergies and consciousness.
original: Katame dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca? Lobho mohena hetu ceva sahetuko ca, moho lobhena hetu ceva sahetuko ca, doso mohena hetu ceva sahetuko ca, moho dosena hetu ceva sahetuko ca; alobho adoso amoho, te aññamaññaṃ hetū ceva sahetukā ca – ime dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are both roots and root-conditioned?⤵Greed with delusion is both a root and root-conditioned. Delusion with greed is both a root and root-conditioned. Hatred with delusion is both a root and root-conditioned. Delusion with hatred is both a root and root-conditioned.⤵Non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, they are mutually both roots and root-conditioned – these phenomena are both roots and root-conditioned.

text: 1084. Katame dhammā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sahetukā te dhamme ṭhapetvā, vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not causally related?⤵“And unconditioned element”.
original: Katame dhammā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sahetukā te dhamme ṭhapetvā, vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū.
ai: Which phenomena are rooted but not roots?⤵The aggregates of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, excluding the roots themselves, are rooted but not roots.

text: 1085. Katame dhammā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca? Lobho mohena hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, moho lobhena hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, doso mohena hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, moho dosena hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca; alobho adoso amoho , te aññamaññaṃ hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca – ime dhammā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are conditioned?⤵Those states which are causally related.
original: Katame dhammā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca? Lobho mohena hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, moho lobhena hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, doso mohena hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, moho dosena hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca; alobho adoso amoho , te aññamaññaṃ hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca – ime dhammā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are roots and associated with roots?⤵Greed with delusion, delusion with greed, hatred with delusion, delusion with hatred; non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion are mutually roots and associated with roots.

text: 1086. Katame dhammā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā te dhamme ṭhapetvā, vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are unconditioned?⤵That state which is not causally related.
original: Katame dhammā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā te dhamme ṭhapetvā, vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with roots but not roots?⤵The aggregates of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, excluding the roots themselves, are associated with roots but not roots.

text: 1087. Katame dhammā na hetū sahetukā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā na hetū sahetukā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā na hetū sahetukā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have visibility?⤵The sphere of [visible] shapes.
original: Katame dhammā na hetū sahetukā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā na hetū sahetukā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā na hetū sahetukā.
ai: Which phenomena are not roots but are rooted?⤵The aggregates of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not roots but are rooted.

text: 1088. Katame dhammā na hetū ahetukā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā na hetū ahetukā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na hetū ahetukā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have no visibility?⤵The spheres of the senses and sense-objects; the four skandhas; that [material] form also which, being neither visible nor reacting, is included under [mental] states; and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā na hetū ahetukā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā na hetū ahetukā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na hetū ahetukā.
ai: Which phenomena are not roots and are rootless?⤵The aggregates of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, all matter, and the unconditioned element are not roots and are rootless.

text: Cūḷantaradukaṃ
original: Cūḷantaradukaṃ
ai: Minor Intermediate Pair

text: 1089. Katame dhammā sappaccayā? Pañcakkhandhā – rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho , saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sappaccayā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that react?⤵The spheres of the senses and sense-objects.
original: Katame dhammā sappaccayā? Pañcakkhandhā – rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho , saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sappaccayā.
ai: Which phenomena are conditioned?⤵The five aggregates: the aggregate of form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are conditioned.

text: 1090. Katame dhammā appaccayā? Asaṅkhatā dhātu – ime dhammā appaccayā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are non-reacting?⤵The four skandhas; that [material] form also which, being neither visible nor reacting, is included under [mental] states; also unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā appaccayā? Asaṅkhatā dhātu – ime dhammā appaccayā.
ai: Which phenomena are unconditioned?⤵The unconditioned element is unconditioned.

text: 1091. Katame dhammā saṅkhatā? Yeva te dhammā sappaccayā, teva te dhammā saṅkhatā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have [material] form?⤵The four great principles as well as the [material] form that is derived from the four great phenomena.
original: Katame dhammā saṅkhatā? Yeva te dhammā sappaccayā, teva te dhammā saṅkhatā.
ai: Which phenomena are conditioned?⤵Those phenomena that are conditioned (sappaccayā) are also conditioned (saṅkhatā).

text: 1092. Katame dhammā asaṅkhatā? Yo eva so dhammo appaccayo, so eva so dhammo asaṅkhato.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have no material form?⤵The four skandhas, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā asaṅkhatā? Yo eva so dhammo appaccayo, so eva so dhammo asaṅkhato.
ai: Which phenomena are unconditioned?⤵That phenomenon which is unconditioned (appaccayā) is also unconditioned (asaṅkhatā).

text: 1093. Katame dhammā sanidassanā? Rūpāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sanidassanā .
rys_davids: Which are the states that are mundane?⤵Co-Intoxicant states, good, bad and indeterminate, relating to the worlds of Sense, of Form, or of the Formless, [to wit] the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā sanidassanā? Rūpāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sanidassanā .
ai: What are visible phenomena?⤵Visible objects. These are visible phenomena.

text: 1094. Katame dhammā anidassanā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anidassanā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are supra-mundane?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā anidassanā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anidassanā.
ai: What are invisible phenomena?⤵The eye-base... up to the tangible-object-base, the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate, and matter that is invisible, non-impinging, included in the Dhamma-base, and the unconditioned element. These are invisible phenomena.

text: 1095. Katame dhammā sappaṭighā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sappaṭighā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are cognizable in one way and not cognizable in another way?⤵States that are cognizable by sight are not cognizable by hearing; conversely, states that are cognizable by hearing are not cognizable by sight. States that are cognizable by sight are not cognizable by smell … by taste … by body-sensibility, and conversely.⤵States that are cognizable by hearing are not cognizable by smell … by taste … by body-sensibility … by sight, and conversely.⤵So for states that are cognizable by smell, by taste, and by body-sensibility.⤵The Āsava Group ( āsava-gocchakaṃ )
original: Katame dhammā sappaṭighā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sappaṭighā.
ai: What are impinging phenomena?⤵The eye-base... up to the tangible-object-base. These are impinging phenomena.

text: 1096. Katame dhammā appaṭighā? Vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā appaṭighā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are Āsavas?⤵The four Āsavas, [to wit] the Āsava of sensuality, the Āsava of rebirth, the Āsava of speculative opinion, the Āsava of ignorance.⤵In this connexion
original: Katame dhammā appaṭighā? Vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā appaṭighā.
ai: What are non-impinging phenomena?⤵The feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate, and matter that is invisible, non-impinging, included in the Dhamma-base, and the unconditioned element. These are non-impinging phenomena.

text: 1097. Katame dhammā rūpino? Cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ – ime dhammā rūpino.
rys_davids: What is the Āsava of sensuality?⤵That sensual desire, sensual passion, sensual delight, sensual craving, sensual fondness, sensual thirst, sensual fever, sensual languishing, sensual rapacity, which is excited by the pleasures of the senses—this is called the Āsava of sensuality.
original: Katame dhammā rūpino? Cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ – ime dhammā rūpino.
ai: What are material phenomena?⤵The four great primary elements and derived matter dependent on the four great primary elements. These are material phenomena.

text: 1098. Katame dhammā arūpino? Vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā arūpino.
rys_davids: What is the Āsava of rebirth?⤵The desire, the passion for coming into being, delight in coming into being, craving, fondness for coming into being, the fever, the yearning, the hungering to come into being, which is felt concerning rebirths—this is called the Āsava of rebirth.
original: Katame dhammā arūpino? Vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā arūpino.
ai: What are immaterial phenomena?⤵The feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate, and the unconditioned element. These are immaterial phenomena.

text: 1099. Katame dhammā lokiyā? Sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā lokiyā.
rys_davids: What is the Āsava of speculative opinion?⤵To hold that the world is eternal, or that it is not eternal, infinite or finite; that the living soul is the body, or that the living soul is a different thing from the body; or that he who has won truth exists after death, or does not exist after death, or both exists and does not exist after death, or neither exists nor does not exist after death—this kind of opinion, this walking in opinion, this jungle of opinion, wilderness of opinion, disorder of opinion, scuffling of opinion, the fetter of opinion, the grip and tenacity of it, the inclination towards it, the being infected by it, this by-path, wrong road, wrongness, this sectarianism, this shiftiness of grasp— this is called the Āsava of speculative opinion. Moreover, the Āsava of speculation includes all false theories.
original: Katame dhammā lokiyā? Sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā lokiyā.
ai: What are mundane phenomena?⤵Tainted wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and the matter aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate. These are mundane phenomena.

text: 1100. Katame dhammā lokuttarā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā lokuttarā.
rys_davids: What is the Āsava of ignorance?⤵Answer as in § 1061 for “dullness”.⤵These are the states that are Āsavas.
original: Katame dhammā lokuttarā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā lokuttarā.
ai: What are supramundane phenomena?⤵The unincluded paths, and the fruits of the paths, and the unconditioned element. These are supramundane phenomena.

text: 1101. Katame dhammā kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā? Ye te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā , na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā. Ime dhammā kenaci viññeyyā kenaci na viññeyyā.
original: Katame dhammā kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā? Ye te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā , na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā cakkhuviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā sotaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā sotaviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā ghānaviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā. Ye te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā, na te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā; ye vā pana te dhammā jivhāviññeyyā, na te dhammā kāyaviññeyyā. Ime dhammā kenaci viññeyyā kenaci na viññeyyā.
ai: What are phenomena knowable by some (senses), not knowable by others?⤵Those phenomena knowable by eye-consciousness are not knowable by ear-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by ear-consciousness are not knowable by eye-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by eye-consciousness are not knowable by nose-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by nose-consciousness are not knowable by eye-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by eye-consciousness are not knowable by tongue-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by tongue-consciousness are not knowable by eye-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by eye-consciousness are not knowable by body-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by body-consciousness are not knowable by eye-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by ear-consciousness are not knowable by nose-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by nose-consciousness are not knowable by ear-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by ear-consciousness are not knowable by tongue-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by tongue-consciousness are not knowable by ear-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by ear-consciousness are not knowable by body-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by body-consciousness are not knowable by ear-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by ear-consciousness are not knowable by eye-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by eye-consciousness are not knowable by ear-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by nose-consciousness are not knowable by tongue-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by tongue-consciousness are not knowable by nose-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by nose-consciousness are not knowable by body-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by body-consciousness are not knowable by nose-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by nose-consciousness are not knowable by eye-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by eye-consciousness are not knowable by nose-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by nose-consciousness are not knowable by ear-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by ear-consciousness are not knowable by nose-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by tongue-consciousness are not knowable by body-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by body-consciousness are not knowable by tongue-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by tongue-consciousness are not knowable by eye-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by eye-consciousness are not knowable by tongue-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by tongue-consciousness are not knowable by ear-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by ear-consciousness are not knowable by tongue-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by tongue-consciousness are not knowable by nose-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by nose-consciousness are not knowable by tongue-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by body-consciousness are not knowable by eye-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by eye-consciousness are not knowable by body-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by body-consciousness are not knowable by ear-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by ear-consciousness are not knowable by body-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by body-consciousness are not knowable by nose-consciousness; conversely, those phenomena knowable by nose-consciousness are not knowable by body-consciousness.⤵Those phenomena knowable by body-consciousness are not knowable by tongue-consciousness; These are phenomena knowable by some (senses), not knowable by others.

text: Āsavagocchakaṃ
original: Āsavagocchakaṃ
ai: The Taint Group

text: 1102. Katame dhammā āsavā? Cattāro āsavā – kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, diṭṭhāsavo, avijjāsavo.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not Āsavas?⤵Every state, good, bad and indeterminate, which is not included in the foregoing, whether relating to the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded, [to wit] the four skandhas; all [material] form also, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā āsavā? Cattāro āsavā – kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, diṭṭhāsavo, avijjāsavo.
ai: Which are the states that are cankers? Four cankers – the canker of sensual desire, the canker of existence, the canker of views, and the canker of ignorance.

text: 1103. Tattha katamo kāmāsavo? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmarāgo kāmanandī kāmataṇhā kāmasineho kāmapariḷāho kāmamucchā kāmajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati kāmāsavo.
rys_davids: Which are the states that can have Āsavas?⤵Good, bad and indeterminate states, whether relating to the worlds of Sense, Form, or the Formless; [in other words] the five skandhas.
original: Tattha katamo kāmāsavo? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmarāgo kāmanandī kāmataṇhā kāmasineho kāmapariḷāho kāmamucchā kāmajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati kāmāsavo.
ai: Therein, what is the canker of sensual desire? That desire, lust, delight, craving, affection, torment, infatuation, and clinging for sensual objects – this is called the canker of sensual desire.

text: 1104. Tattha katamo bhavāsavo? Yo bhavesu bhavachando [bhavacchando (sī. syā.)] bhavarāgo bhavanandī bhavataṇhā bhavasineho bhavapariḷāho bhavamucchā bhavajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati bhavāsavo.
rys_davids: Which are the states that can not have Āsavas?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths, and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katamo bhavāsavo? Yo bhavesu bhavachando [bhavacchando (sī. syā.)] bhavarāgo bhavanandī bhavataṇhā bhavasineho bhavapariḷāho bhavamucchā bhavajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati bhavāsavo.
ai: Therein, what is the canker of existence? That desire, lust, delight, craving, affection, torment, infatuation, and clinging for existence – this is called the canker of existence.

text: 1105. Tattha katamo diṭṭhāsavo? Sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā; yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho paṭiggāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati diṭṭhāsavo. Sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhāsavo.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are “associated with Āsavas”?⤵The states which are associated with those states, [to wit] the four skandhas.
original: Tattha katamo diṭṭhāsavo? Sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā; yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho paṭiggāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati diṭṭhāsavo. Sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhāsavo.
ai: Therein, what is the canker of views? Whether the world is eternal, or not eternal, or finite, or infinite, or the soul is the same as the body, or different from the body, or a Tathagata exists after death, or does not exist, or both exists and does not exist, or neither exists nor does not exist after death; whatever such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, perversion of views, agitation of views, fetter of views, grasping, adherence, dogmatic belief, perverted grasping, wrong path, false way, wrongness, heretical ground, perverted grasping – this is called the canker of views. All wrong views are the canker of views.

text: 1106. Tattha katamo avijjāsavo? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ , pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃः yaṃ evarūpaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṃgāhanā apariyogāhanā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati avijjāsavo.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are “disconnected with Āsavas”?⤵The states which are disconnected with those states, [to wit] the four skandhas; all [material] form also, and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katamo avijjāsavo? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ , pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃः yaṃ evarūpaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṃgāhanā apariyogāhanā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati avijjāsavo.
ai: Therein, what is the canker of ignorance? Ignorance of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path to its cessation; ignorance of the past, of the future, of both, and of dependent arising in conditionally arisen phenomena; whatever such ignorance, non-seeing, non-comprehension, non-understanding, non-awakening, non-penetration, non-grasping, non-fathoming, non-reflection, non-reviewing, non-direct knowledge, dullness, folly, non-discernment, delusion, utter delusion, confusion, ignorance, flood of ignorance, bond of ignorance, latent disposition of ignorance, obsession of ignorance, chain of ignorance, delusion, root of unwholesome – this is called the canker of ignorance.

text: Ime dhammā āsavā.
original: Ime dhammā āsavā.
ai: These states are cankers.

text: 1107. Katame dhammā no āsavā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no āsavā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are both Āsavas and can have Āsavas?⤵The Āsavas themselves.
original: Katame dhammā no āsavā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no āsavā.
ai: Which are the states that are not cankers?⤵Excluding those states, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the four mental aggregates; all matter, and the unconditioned element – these states are not cankers.

text: 1108. Katame dhammā sāsavā? Kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sāsavā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that can have Āsavas, but are not Āsavas?⤵The states which have the foregoing states ( § 1096 ) as their concomitants; that is to say, with the exception of the Āsavas, all states whatever, good, bad and indeterminate, which can have Āsavas, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, of Form or of the Formless; [in other words] the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā sāsavā? Kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sāsavā.
ai: Which are the states that are associated with cankers?⤵Wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the five aggregates – these states are associated with cankers.

text: 1109. Katame dhammā anāsavā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anāsavā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are both Āsavas and associated with Āsavas?⤵The Āsavas of sensuality together with that of ignorance, and conversely. The Āsava of rebirth together with that of ignorance, and conversely. The Āsava of speculative opinion together with that of ignorance, and conversely.
original: Katame dhammā anāsavā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anāsavā.
ai: Which are the states that are not associated with cankers?⤵The supramundane paths and their fruits, and the unconditioned element – these states are not associated with cankers.

text: 1110. Katame dhammā āsavasampayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā āsavasampayuttā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are associated with Āsavas but are not Āsavas?⤵The states which are associated with the foregoing states ( § 1096 )—the latter themselves excepted—[to wit] the four skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā āsavasampayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā āsavasampayuttā.
ai: Which are the states that are concomitant with cankers?⤵Those states that are concomitant with them – the four mental aggregates – these states are concomitant with cankers.

text: 1111. Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are disconnected with Āsavas but can have Āsavas?⤵The states which are disconnected with those above-named states ( § 1096 ) but which, good, bad, or indeterminate, have them as concomitants, whether they belong to the worlds of Sense, of Form, or of the Formless, [to wit] the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are disjoined from influxes?⤵Those phenomena that are disjoined from them (the influxes), namely, the feeling aggregate... up to... the consciousness aggregate; all matter; and the unconditioned element. These phenomena are disjoined from influxes.

text: 1112. Katame dhammā āsavā ceva sāsavā ca? Teyeva āsavā āsavā ceva sāsavā ca.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are disconnected with Āsavas and can not have Āsavas?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded and the Fruits of the Paths and uncompounded element.⤵The Group of the Fetters ( saṃyojana-gocchakaṃ )
original: Katame dhammā āsavā ceva sāsavā ca? Teyeva āsavā āsavā ceva sāsavā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are influxes and are tainted by influxes?⤵Those very influxes are influxes and are tainted by influxes.

text: 1113. Katame dhammā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sāsavā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā , arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are Fetters?⤵The ten Fetters, to wit, the Fetter of⤵sensuality,⤵repulsion,⤵conceit,⤵speculative opinion,⤵perplexity,⤵perversion as to rule and ritual,⤵the passion for rebirth,⤵envy,⤵meanness,⤵ignorance.⤵In this connexion,
original: Katame dhammā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sāsavā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā , arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā.
ai: Which phenomena are tainted by influxes but are not influxes?⤵Excluding those phenomena that are influxes, the remaining tainted wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the matter aggregate... up to... the consciousness aggregate. These phenomena are tainted by influxes but are not influxes.

text: 1114. Katame dhammā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca? Kāmāsavo avijjāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, avijjāsavo kāmāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, bhavāsavo avijjāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, avijjāsavo bhavāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, diṭṭhāsavo avijjāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, avijjāsavo diṭṭhāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca – ime dhammā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of sensual passion?⤵That sensual desire, sensual passion, sensual delight, sensual craving, sensual fondness, sensual fever, sensual languor, sensual rapacity, which is excited by the pleasures of the senses—this is called the Fetter of sensuality.
original: Katame dhammā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca? Kāmāsavo avijjāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, avijjāsavo kāmāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, bhavāsavo avijjāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, avijjāsavo bhavāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, diṭṭhāsavo avijjāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, avijjāsavo diṭṭhāsavena āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca – ime dhammā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are influxes and are associated with influxes?⤵The sensual desire influx, when associated with the ignorance influx, is an influx and associated with an influx; the ignorance influx, when associated with the sensual desire influx, is an influx and associated with an influx; the desire for existence influx, when associated with the ignorance influx, is an influx and associated with an influx; the ignorance influx, when associated with the desire for existence influx, is an influx and associated with an influx; the wrong view influx, when associated with the ignorance influx, is an influx and associated with an influx; the ignorance influx, when associated with the wrong view influx, is an influx and associated with an influx. These phenomena are influxes and are associated with influxes.

text: 1115. Katame dhammā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of repulsion?⤵Answer as for “hate”, § 1060 .
original: Katame dhammā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with influxes but are not influxes?⤵Excluding those phenomena that are influxes, the feeling aggregate... up to... the consciousness aggregate, when associated with influxes. These phenomena are associated with influxes but are not influxes.

text: 1116. Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of conceit?⤵Conceit at the thought “I am the better man”; conceit at the thought “I am as good [as they]”; conceit at the thought “I am lowly”—all such sort of conceit, overweening conceitedness, loftiness, haughtiness, flaunting a flag, assumption, desire of the heart for self-advertisement—this is called conceit.
original: Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā.
ai: Which phenomena are disjoined from influxes but are tainted by influxes?⤵Those phenomena that are disjoined from influxes but are tainted by influxes, namely, wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the matter aggregate... up to... the consciousness aggregate. These phenomena are disjoined from influxes but are tainted by influxes.

text: 1117. Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of speculative opinion?⤵Answer as for the “Intoxicant of speculative opinion”, § 1099 , with this supplement: And, with the exception of the “Fetter of perversion as to rule and ritual”, all wrong views are included in the Fetter of speculative opinion.
original: Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā.
ai: Which phenomena are disjoined from influxes and are untainted by influxes?⤵The unincluded paths, the fruits of the paths, and the unconditioned element. These phenomena are disjoined from influxes and are untainted by influxes.

text: Nikkhepakaṇḍe paṭhamabhāṇavāro.
original: Nikkhepakaṇḍe paṭhamabhāṇavāro.
ai: The first recitation section in the Summary Chapter.

text: Saṃyojanagocchakaṃ
original: Saṃyojanagocchakaṃ
ai: Group of Fetters

text: 1118. Katame dhammā saṃyojanā? Dasa saṃyojanāni – kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ , mānasaṃyojanaṃ, diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ, vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ, sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ, bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, issāsaṃyojanaṃ, macchariyasaṃyojanaṃ, avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of perplexity?⤵Answer as for “perplexity”, § 1004 .
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanā? Dasa saṃyojanāni – kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ , mānasaṃyojanaṃ, diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ, vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ, sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ, bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, issāsaṃyojanaṃ, macchariyasaṃyojanaṃ, avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ.
ai: Which phenomena are fetters?⤵Ten fetters: the fetter of sensual desire, the fetter of aversion, the fetter of conceit, the fetter of wrong view, the fetter of doubt, the fetter of clinging to rites and rituals, the fetter of desire for existence, the fetter of envy, the fetter of avarice, the fetter of ignorance.

text: 1119. Tattha katamaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmarāgo kāmanandī kāmataṇhā kāmasineho kāmapariḷāho kāmamucchā kāmajjhosānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of perversion as to rule and ritual?⤵Answer as for “perversion”, etc., § 1005 .
original: Tattha katamaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmarāgo kāmanandī kāmataṇhā kāmasineho kāmapariḷāho kāmamucchā kāmajjhosānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ.
ai: What is the Fetter of sensual lust?⤵The desire, lust, delight, craving, affection, burning, infatuation, and clinging for sense objects. This is called the Fetter of sensual lust.

text: 1120. Tattha katamaṃ paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ? Anatthaṃ me acarīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me caratīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me carissatīti āghāto jāyati, piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati. Yo evarūpo cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – idaṃ vuccati paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of the passion for rebirth?⤵Answer as for the “Intoxicant of rebirth”, § 1098 .
original: Tattha katamaṃ paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ? Anatthaṃ me acarīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me caratīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me carissatīti āghāto jāyati, piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati. Yo evarūpo cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – idaṃ vuccati paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ.
ai: What is the Fetter of aversion?⤵Resentment arises thinking: 'He harmed me,' 'He is harming me,' 'He will harm me'; or similar thoughts regarding dear ones or disliked ones; or resentment arises without reason. Such mental resentment, opposition, aversion, hostility, anger, hatred, mental affliction, wrath, malice, enmity, fierceness, mental displeasure. This is called the Fetter of aversion.

text: 1121. Tattha katamaṃ mānasaṃyojanaṃ? Seyyohamasmīti māno, sadisohamasmīti māno, hīnohamasmīti māno. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnamo [uṇṇati uṇṇāmo (syā.)] dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – idaṃ vuccati mānasaṃyojanaṃ.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of envy ( issāsaṃyojanaṃ )?⤵Envy, envying, enviousness—jealousy, the expression and mood of jealousy at the gifts, the hospitality, the respect, affection, reverence and worship accruing to others—this is called the Fetter of envy.
original: Tattha katamaṃ mānasaṃyojanaṃ? Seyyohamasmīti māno, sadisohamasmīti māno, hīnohamasmīti māno. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnamo [uṇṇati uṇṇāmo (syā.)] dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – idaṃ vuccati mānasaṃyojanaṃ.
ai: What is the Fetter of conceit?⤵Conceit that 'I am better,' 'I am equal,' 'I am worse.' Such conceit, thinking, mental elevation, banner-like assertion, desire for prominence of mind. This is called the Fetter of conceit.

text: 1122. Tattha katamaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ? Sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā; yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho paṭiggāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ. Ṭhapetvā sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ.
rys_davids: What is the Fetter of meanness ( maccharisaṃyojanaṃ )?⤵The Five Meannesses, [to wit] meanness as regards dwelling, families, gifts, reputation, doctrine—all this sort of mean , grudging, mean spirit, avarice and ignobleness, niggardliness and want of generosity of heart—this is called the Fetter of meanness.
original: Tattha katamaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ? Sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā; yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho paṭiggāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ. Ṭhapetvā sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ.
ai: What is the Fetter of wrong view?⤵The view that the world is eternal or not, finite or infinite; that the soul is the same as the body or different; that a Tathāgata exists after death or not, or both, or neither.
