original: Katame dhammā anārammaṇā? Sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anārammaṇā.
ai: Which phenomena are without object?⤵All matter, and the unconditioned element. These phenomena are without object.

text: 1193. Katame dhammā cittā? Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – ime dhammā cittā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵conjoined with thought?⤵detached from thought?⤵Answers as in §§ 1191 , 1192 , respectively. (Thought must not be described as conjoined with, or detached from, itself.)
original: Katame dhammā cittā? Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – ime dhammā cittā.
ai: Which phenomena are consciousness?⤵Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-element, mind-consciousness element. These phenomena are consciousness.

text: 1194. Katame dhammā no cittā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittā.
original: Katame dhammā no cittā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittā.
ai: Which phenomena are not consciousness?⤵The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, all matter, and the unconditioned element. These phenomena are not consciousness.

text: 1195. Katame dhammā cetasikā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cetasikā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵sprung from thought?⤵The skandhas of feeling, perception, and synergies; bodily and vocal intimation; or whatever other [material] form there be which is born of thought, caused by thought, sprung from thought, whether it be in the spheres of shapes, sounds, smells, tastes, or the tangible, the elements of space or fluidity, the lightness, plasticity or wieldiness of [material] form, the integration or subsistence of [material] form, or bodily nutriment.⤵not sprung from thought?⤵Thought; also every other kind of [material] form, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā cetasikā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cetasikā.
ai: Which phenomena are mental factors?⤵The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations. These phenomena are mental factors.

text: 1196. Katame dhammā acetasikā? Cittañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā acetasikā.
original: Katame dhammā acetasikā? Cittañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā acetasikā.
ai: Which phenomena are not mental factors?⤵Consciousness, all matter, and the unconditioned element. These phenomena are not mental factors.

text: 1197. Katame dhammā cittasampayuttā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasampayuttā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that⤵come into being together with thought?⤵The skandhas of feeling, perception, and synergies; bodily and vocal intimation.⤵do not come into being together with thought?⤵Thought; also all other kinds of [material] form, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā cittasampayuttā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with consciousness?⤵The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations. These phenomena are associated with consciousness.

text: 1198. Katame dhammā cittavippayuttā? Sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā cittavippayuttā. Cittaṃ na vattabbaṃ – cittena sampayuttantipi, cittena vippayuttantipi.
original: Katame dhammā cittavippayuttā? Sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā cittavippayuttā. Cittaṃ na vattabbaṃ – cittena sampayuttantipi, cittena vippayuttantipi.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from consciousness?⤵All matter, and the unconditioned element. These phenomena are dissociated from consciousness. Consciousness should not be described as associated with consciousness, nor as dissociated from consciousness.

text: 1199. Katame dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵consecutive to thought?⤵not consecutive to thought?⤵Answers as in the two foregoing answers respectively.
original: Katame dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhā.
ai: Which states are conjoined with mind?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, and volitional formations aggregate. These states are conjoined with mind.

text: 1200. Katame dhammā cittavisaṃsaṭṭhā? Sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā cittavisaṃsaṭṭhā. Cittaṃ na vattabbaṃ – cittena saṃsaṭṭhantipi, cittena visaṃsaṭṭhantipi.
original: Katame dhammā cittavisaṃsaṭṭhā? Sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā cittavisaṃsaṭṭhā. Cittaṃ na vattabbaṃ – cittena saṃsaṭṭhantipi, cittena visaṃsaṭṭhantipi.
ai: Which states are disjoined from mind?⤵All matter and the unconditioned element. These states are disjoined from mind. Mind should not be said to be conjoined with mind, nor disjoined from mind.

text: 1201. Katame dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho; kāyaviññatti vacīviññatti; yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ cittajaṃ cittahetukaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ saddāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ ākāsadhātu āpodhātu rūpassa lahutā rūpassa mudutā rūpassa kammaññatā rūpassa upacayo rūpassa santati kabaḷīkāro āhāro – ime dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵conjoined with and sprung from thought?⤵The skandhas of feeling, perception, and synergies.⤵not conjoined with and sprung from thought?⤵Thought itself; all [material] form also, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho; kāyaviññatti vacīviññatti; yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ cittajaṃ cittahetukaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ saddāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ ākāsadhātu āpodhātu rūpassa lahutā rūpassa mudutā rūpassa kammaññatā rūpassa upacayo rūpassa santati kabaḷīkāro āhāro – ime dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānā.
ai: Which states arise from mind?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate; bodily intimation, vocal intimation; and whatever other mind-born, mind-rooted, mind-originated matter there is, such as the visible form base, sound base, smell base, taste base, tangible object base, space element, water element, lightness of matter, malleability of matter, wieldiness of matter, production of matter, continuity of matter, and edible food. These states arise from mind.

text: 1202. Katame dhammā no cittasamuṭṭhānā? Cittañca, avasesañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasamuṭṭhānā.
original: Katame dhammā no cittasamuṭṭhānā? Cittañca, avasesañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasamuṭṭhānā.
ai: Which states do not arise from mind?⤵Mind, the remaining matter, and the unconditioned element. These states do not arise from mind.

text: 1203. Katame dhammā cittasahabhuno? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, kāyaviññatti, vacīviññatti – ime dhammā cittasahabhuno.
rys_davids: Which are the states that⤵are conjoined with and sprung from, and that come into being together with, thought?⤵are not such as are conjoined with and sprung from, and as come into being together with, thought?⤵Answers as in the two foregoing answers respectively.
original: Katame dhammā cittasahabhuno? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, kāyaviññatti, vacīviññatti – ime dhammā cittasahabhuno.
ai: Which states are co-existent with mind?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, bodily intimation, and vocal intimation. These states are co-existent with mind.

text: 1204. Katame dhammā no cittasahabhuno? Cittañca, avasesañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasahabhuno.
original: Katame dhammā no cittasahabhuno? Cittañca, avasesañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasahabhuno.
ai: Which states are not co-existent with mind?⤵Mind, the remaining matter, and the unconditioned element. These states are not co-existent with mind.

text: 1205. Katame dhammā cittānuparivattino? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, kāyaviññatti, vacīviññatti – ime dhammā cittānuparivattino.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵conjoined with and sprung from and consecutive to thought?⤵not conjoined with, sprung from and consecutive to thought?⤵Answers as in the two foregoing answers.
original: Katame dhammā cittānuparivattino? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, kāyaviññatti, vacīviññatti – ime dhammā cittānuparivattino.
ai: Which states follow the mind?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, bodily intimation, and vocal intimation. These states follow the mind.

text: 1206. Katame dhammā no cittānuparivattino? Cittañca, avasesañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittānuparivattino.
original: Katame dhammā no cittānuparivattino? Cittañca, avasesañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittānuparivattino.
ai: Which states do not follow the mind?⤵Mind, the remaining matter, and the unconditioned element. These states do not follow the mind.

text: 1207. Katame dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵of the self?⤵The spheres of the five senses and of ideation.⤵external?⤵The spheres of the five objects of sense and of ideas.
original: Katame dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā.
ai: Which states are conjoined with mind and arise from mind?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, and volitional formations aggregate. These states are conjoined with mind and arise from mind.

text: 1208. Katame dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā? Cittañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā.
original: Katame dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā? Cittañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā.
ai: Which states are not conjoined with mind and do not arise from mind?⤵Mind, all matter, and the unconditioned element. These states are not conjoined with mind and do not arise from mind.

text: 1209. Katame dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵derived?⤵The spheres of the five senses … and bodily nutriment.⤵not derived?⤵The four skandhas, the four great phenomena and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno.
ai: Which states are conjoined with, arisen from, and co-existent with consciousness? The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the volitional formations aggregate – these states are conjoined with, arisen from, and co-existent with consciousness.

text: 1210. Katame dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno? Cittañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno.
original: Katame dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno? Cittañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno.
ai: Which states are not conjoined with, arisen from, and co-existent with consciousness? Consciousness, all matter, and the unconditioned element – these states are not conjoined with, arisen from, and co-existent with consciousness.

text: 1211. Katame dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵grasped at?⤵Co-Intoxicant good and bad states, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, of Form, or of the Formless; [in other words] the four skandhas, and such [material] form as is due to karma having been wrought.⤵not grasped at?⤵Good and bad states that have Āsavas, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, of Form, or of the Formless; [in other words] the four skandhas; also such inoperative thoughts as are neither good, nor bad, nor the effects of karma; the Paths, moreover, that are the Unincluded and the Fruits of the Paths, and unconditioned element.⤵The Group on Grasping ( upādāna-gocchakaṃ )
original: Katame dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – ime dhammā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino.
ai: Which states follow the arising of consciousness and are conjoined with it? The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the volitional formations aggregate – these states follow the arising of consciousness and are conjoined with it.

text: 1212. Katame dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino? Cittañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino.
original: Katame dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino? Cittañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino.
ai: Which states do not follow the arising of consciousness and are conjoined with it? Consciousness, all matter, and the unconditioned element – these states do not follow the arising of consciousness and are conjoined with it.

text: 1213. Katame dhammā ajjhattikā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… manāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā ajjhattikā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have the attribute of Grasping?⤵The four Graspings: the Grasping of sense-desires, the Grasping of speculative opinion, the Grasping of rule and ritual, the Grasping of a theory of the Self.⤵In this connexion,
original: Katame dhammā ajjhattikā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… manāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā ajjhattikā.
ai: Which states are ⤵internal?⤵The eye-base... up to... the mind-base – these states are internal.

text: 1214. Katame dhammā bāhirā? Rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… dhammāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā bāhirā.
rys_davids: What is the Grasping of sense-desires?⤵That sensual desire, sensual passion, sensual delight, sensual craving, sensual cleaving, sensual fever, sensual languishing, sensual rapacity, which is excited by the pleasures of the senses.
original: Katame dhammā bāhirā? Rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… dhammāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā bāhirā.
ai: Which states are ⤵external?⤵The visible form-base... up to... the phenomena-base – these states are external.

text: 1215. Katame dhammā upādā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro – ime dhammā upādā.
rys_davids: What is the Grasping of speculative opinion?⤵“There is no such thing as alms, or sacrifice, or offering; there is neither fruit, nor result of good, or of evil deeds; there is no such thing as this world, or the next; there is no such thing as mother or father, or beings springing into birth without them; there are in the world no recluses or brahmins who have reached the highest point, who have attained the height, who, having understood and realized by themselves alone both this world and the next, make known the same”—all this sort of speculation, this walking in opinion, wilderness of opinion, puppet-show of opinion, scuffling of opinion, this Fetter of opinion, the grip and tenacity of it, the inclination towards it, the being infected by it, this by-path, wrong road, wrongness, this “fording-place”, this shiftiness of grasp—this is what is called the Grasping after speculative opinion.⤵And with the exception of the Graspings of rule and ritual and soul theory, all wrong views are included in the Grasping of speculative opinion.
original: Katame dhammā upādā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro – ime dhammā upādā.
ai: Which states are ⤵derived?⤵The eye-base... up to... edible food – these states are derived.

text: 1216. Katame dhammā no upādā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho, cattāro ca mahābhūtā, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no upādā.
rys_davids: What is the Grasping of rule and ritual?⤵Answer as for “Perversion of mere rule and ritual”, § 1005 .
original: Katame dhammā no upādā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho, cattāro ca mahābhūtā, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no upādā.
ai: Which states are ⤵not derived?⤵The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the volitional formations aggregate, the consciousness aggregate, the four great essential elements, and the unconditioned element – these states are not derived.

text: 1217. Katame dhammā upādiṇṇā? Sāsavā kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; yañca rūpaṃ kammassa katattā – ime dhammā upādiṇṇā .
rys_davids: What is the Grasping of a theory of the Self?⤵Answer as for the “Theory of individuality”, § 1003 .
original: Katame dhammā upādiṇṇā? Sāsavā kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; yañca rūpaṃ kammassa katattā – ime dhammā upādiṇṇā .
ai: Which states are ⤵grasped by kamma?⤵The tainted results of wholesome and unwholesome states belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the feeling aggregate... up to... the consciousness aggregate; and matter produced by kamma – these states are grasped by kamma.

text: 1218. Katame dhammā anupādiṇṇā? Sāsavā kusalākusalā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, yañca rūpaṃ na kammassa katattā, apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anupādiṇṇā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not Graspings?⤵All other states whatever, good, bad and indeterminate (except the foregoing), whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, or of Form, or of the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; [in other words] the four skandhas; all [material] form also and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā anupādiṇṇā? Sāsavā kusalākusalā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, yañca rūpaṃ na kammassa katattā, apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anupādiṇṇā.
ai: Which states are ⤵not grasped by kamma?⤵The tainted wholesome and unwholesome states belonging to the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the feeling aggregate... up to... the consciousness aggregate; and functional states that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor kamma-results; and matter not produced by kamma; and the unincluded paths and path-fruits; and the unconditioned element – these states are not grasped by kamma.

text: Upādānagocchakaṃ
original: Upādānagocchakaṃ
ai: Section on Clinging

text: 1219. Katame dhammā upādānā? Cattāri upādānāni – kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ, sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ [kāmūpādānaṃ diṭṭhūpādānaṃ sīlabbatūpādānaṃ attavādūpādānaṃ (sī.)].
rys_davids: Which are the states that are favourable to Grasping?⤵States that have Āsavas, good, bad and indeterminate, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless; [in other words] the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā upādānā? Cattāri upādānāni – kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ, sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ [kāmūpādānaṃ diṭṭhūpādānaṃ sīlabbatūpādānaṃ attavādūpādānaṃ (sī.)].
ai: Which phenomena are clingings? Four clingings: sensual clinging, clinging to views, clinging to rites and rituals, clinging to a doctrine of self.

text: 1220. Tattha katamaṃ kāmupādānaṃ? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmarāgo kāmanandī kāmataṇhā kāmasineho kāmapariḷāho kāmamucchā kāmajjhosānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati kāmupādānaṃ.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not favourable to Grasping?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths; and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katamaṃ kāmupādānaṃ? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmarāgo kāmanandī kāmataṇhā kāmasineho kāmapariḷāho kāmamucchā kāmajjhosānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati kāmupādānaṃ.
ai: What is sensual clinging? That desire for sensual pleasures, lust for sensual pleasures, delight in sensual pleasures, craving for sensual pleasures, affection for sensual pleasures, agitation due to sensual pleasures, infatuation with sensual pleasures, obsession with sensual pleasures – this is called sensual clinging.

text: 1221. Tattha katamaṃ diṭṭhupādānaṃ? Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā [samaggatā (ka.)] sammāpaṭipannā, ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentīti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati diṭṭhupādānaṃ. Ṭhapetvā sīlabbatupādānañca attavādupādānañca sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhupādānaṃ.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵associated with Grasping?
original: Tattha katamaṃ diṭṭhupādānaṃ? Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā [samaggatā (ka.)] sammāpaṭipannā, ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentīti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati diṭṭhupādānaṃ. Ṭhapetvā sīlabbatupādānañca attavādupādānañca sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhupādānaṃ.
ai: What is clinging to views? The view that there is no giving, no offering, no sacrifice; no fruit or result of good and bad actions; no this world, no other world; no mother, no father; no spontaneously born beings; no recluses and brahmins in the world who are rightly gone, rightly practiced, who have themselves realized and proclaimed this world and the other world by direct knowledge – such a view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, agitation of views, fickleness of views, fetter of views, grasp, holding, adherence, clinging, wrong path, false way, wrongness, heretical tenet, perverse grasp – this is called clinging to views. Excluding clinging to rites and rituals and clinging to a doctrine of self, all wrong views are clinging to views.

text: 1222. Tattha katamaṃ sīlabbatupādānaṃ? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlena suddhi, vatena suddhi, sīlabbatena suddhīti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati sīlabbatupādānaṃ.
rys_davids: disconnected with Grasping?
original: Tattha katamaṃ sīlabbatupādānaṃ? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlena suddhi, vatena suddhi, sīlabbatena suddhīti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati sīlabbatupādānaṃ.
ai: What is clinging to rites and rituals? Among recluses and brahmins outside [this dispensation], the view that purification is through virtue, purification is through vows, purification is through rites and rituals – such a view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, agitation of views, fickleness of views, fetter of views, grasp, holding, adherence, clinging, wrong path, false way, wrongness, heretical tenet, perverse grasp – this is called clinging to rites and rituals.

text: 1223. Tattha katamaṃ attavādupādānaṃ? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati attavādupādānaṃ.
rys_davids: Graspings and also favourable to Grasping?
original: Tattha katamaṃ attavādupādānaṃ? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati attavādupādānaṃ.
ai: What is clinging to a doctrine of self? Here, an uninstructed worldling, not seeing noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained in the noble Dhamma; not seeing true men, not skilled in the Dhamma of true men, not trained in the Dhamma of true men – perceives form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as being in self, or self as being in form. Feeling... perception... mental formations... consciousness he perceives as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as being in self, or self as being in consciousness. Such a view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, agitation of views, fickleness of views, fetter of views, grasp, holding, adherence, clinging, wrong path, false way, wrongness, heretical tenet, perverse grasp – this is called clinging to a doctrine of self.

text: Ime dhammā upādānā.
original: Ime dhammā upādānā.
ai: These phenomena are clingings.

text: 1224. Katame dhammā no upādānā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no upādānā.
rys_davids: favourable to Grasping but not Graspings?⤵Answers exactly analogous to those given to corresponding questions in other Groups, e.g. §§ 1125 , 1141 , 1164 .
original: Katame dhammā no upādānā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no upādānā.
ai: Which phenomena are not clingings? Excluding those phenomena, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and unincluded; the aggregate of feeling... consciousness; and all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not clingings.

text: 1225. Katame dhammā upādāniyā? Sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādāniyā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵both Graspings and associated with Grasping?⤵The Grasping of speculation in conjunction with that of sense is both, and conversely.⤵So is each of the other two Graspings in conjunction with that of sense, and conversely.
original: Katame dhammā upādāniyā? Sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādāniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are objects of clinging? Wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena with taints in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the aggregate of form... consciousness – these phenomena are objects of clinging.

text: 1226. Katame dhammā anupādāniyā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anupādāniyā.
rys_davids: associated with Grasping but not Graspings?
original: Katame dhammā anupādāniyā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā anupādāniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are not objects of clinging? The unincluded paths and their fruits, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not objects of clinging.

text: 1227. Katame dhammā upādānasampayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādānasampayuttā.
rys_davids: disconnected with Grasping yet favourable to it?
original: Katame dhammā upādānasampayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādānasampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with clinging? The mental aggregates (feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness) that are associated with clinging – these phenomena are associated with clinging.

text: 1228. Katame dhammā upādānavippayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā upādānavippayuttā.
rys_davids: disconnected with Grasping and not favourable to it?⤵Answers as in the Groups specified above, §§ 1125 , 1141 , 1164 et seq.⤵The Group on the Vices ( kilesa-gocchakaṃ )
original: Katame dhammā upādānavippayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā upādānavippayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from clinging? The mental aggregates (feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness) that are dissociated from clinging; all physical form, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are dissociated from clinging.

text: 1229. Katame dhammā upādānā ceva upādāniyā ca? Tāneva upādānāni upādānā ceva upādāniyā ca.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are vicious?⤵The ten bases of vice, to wit⤵greed,⤵hate,⤵dullness,⤵conceit,⤵speculative opinion,⤵perplexity,⤵stolidity,⤵distraction,⤵unconscientiousness,⤵disregard of blame.
original: Katame dhammā upādānā ceva upādāniyā ca? Tāneva upādānāni upādānā ceva upādāniyā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are both clinging and objects of clinging? The clingings themselves are both clinging and objects of clinging.

text: 1230. Katame dhammā upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā upādāniyā , te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā.
rys_davids: In this connexion,⤵What is greed? … hate? … dullness? … conceit? … speculative opinion? … perplexity? … stolidity? … distraction?⤵Answers as in §§ 1059 – 1061 , 1116 – 1118 , 1156 , 1159 .
original: Katame dhammā upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā upādāniyā , te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā.
ai: Which phenomena are objects of clinging but not clinging itself? Excluding the clingings themselves, the remaining defiled wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena pertaining to the sense-sphere, form-sphere, and formless-sphere; the five aggregates (form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness) – these phenomena are objects of clinging but not clinging itself.

text: 1231. Katame dhammā upādānā ceva upādānasampayuttā ca? Diṭṭhupādānaṃ kāmupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, kāmupādānaṃ diṭṭhupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, sīlabbatupādānaṃ kāmupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, kāmupādānaṃ sīlabbatupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca , attavādupādānaṃ kāmupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, kāmupādānaṃ attavādupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca – ime dhammā upādānā ceva upādānasampayuttā ca.
original: Katame dhammā upādānā ceva upādānasampayuttā ca? Diṭṭhupādānaṃ kāmupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, kāmupādānaṃ diṭṭhupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, sīlabbatupādānaṃ kāmupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, kāmupādānaṃ sīlabbatupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca , attavādupādānaṃ kāmupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, kāmupādānaṃ attavādupādānena upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca – ime dhammā upādānā ceva upādānasampayuttā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are both clinging and associated with clinging? Clinging to views associated with sensual clinging is both clinging and associated with clinging; sensual clinging associated with clinging to views is both clinging and associated with clinging; clinging to rites and rituals associated with sensual clinging is both clinging and associated with clinging; sensual clinging associated with clinging to rites and rituals is both clinging and associated with clinging; clinging to a doctrine of self associated with sensual clinging is both clinging and associated with clinging; sensual clinging associated with clinging to a doctrine of self is both clinging and associated with clinging – these phenomena are both clinging and associated with clinging.

text: 1232. Katame dhammā upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā.
original: Katame dhammā upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with clinging but not clinging itself? Excluding the clingings themselves, the mental aggregates (feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness) that are associated with clinging – these phenomena are associated with clinging but not clinging itself.

text: 1233. Katame dhammā upādānavippayuttā upādāniyā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā , rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādānavippayuttā upādāniyā.
original: Katame dhammā upādānavippayuttā upādāniyā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā , rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upādānavippayuttā upādāniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from clinging yet are objects of clinging? Those phenomena that are dissociated from clinging, namely, defiled wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena pertaining to the sense-sphere, form-sphere, and formless-sphere; the five aggregates (form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness) – these phenomena are dissociated from clinging yet are objects of clinging.

text: 1234. Katame dhammā upādānavippayuttā anupādāniyā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā upādānavippayuttā anupādāniyā.
original: Katame dhammā upādānavippayuttā anupādāniyā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā upādānavippayuttā anupādāniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from clinging and are not objects of clinging? The supramundane paths, and their fruits, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are dissociated from clinging and are not objects of clinging.

text: Nikkhepakaṇḍe dutiyabhāṇavāro.
original: Nikkhepakaṇḍe dutiyabhāṇavāro.
ai: The second recitation section in the Summary Chapter.

text: Kilesagocchakaṃ
original: Kilesagocchakaṃ
ai: Cluster of Defilements

text: 1235. Katame dhammā kilesā? Dasa kilesavatthūni – lobho, doso, moho, māno, diṭṭhi, vicikicchā, thinaṃ, uddhaccaṃ, ahirīkaṃ, anottappaṃ.
original: Katame dhammā kilesā? Dasa kilesavatthūni – lobho, doso, moho, māno, diṭṭhi, vicikicchā, thinaṃ, uddhaccaṃ, ahirīkaṃ, anottappaṃ.
ai: What are defilements? The ten bases of defilements are: greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, skeptical doubt, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and fearlessness of wrongdoing.

text: 1236. Tattha katamo lobho? Yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandīrāgo cittassa sārāgo icchā mucchā ajjhosānaṃ gedho paligedho saṅgo paṅko ejā māyā janikā sañjananī sibbinī jālinī saritā visattikā suttaṃ visaṭā āyūhinī dutiyā paṇidhi bhavanetti vanaṃ vanatho santhavo sineho apekkhā paṭibandhu āsā āsisanā āsisitattaṃ rūpāsā saddāsā gandhāsā rasāsā phoṭṭhabbāsā lābhāsā dhanāsā puttāsā jīvitāsā jappā pajappā abhijappā jappā jappanā jappitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañjikatā sādhukamyatā adhammarāgo visamalobho nikanti nikāmanā patthanā pihanā sampatthanā kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā rūpataṇhā arūpataṇhā nirodhataṇhā rūpataṇhā saddataṇhā gandhataṇhā rasataṇhā phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dhammataṇhā ogho yogo gantho upādānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ chādanaṃ bandhanaṃ upakkileso anusayo pariyuṭṭhānaṃ latā vevicchaṃ dukkhamūlaṃ dukkhanidānaṃ dukkhappabhavo mārapāso mārabaḷisaṃ māravisayo taṇhānadī taṇhājālaṃ taṇhāgaddulaṃ taṇhāsamuddo abhijjhā lobho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati lobho.
original: Tattha katamo lobho? Yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandīrāgo cittassa sārāgo icchā mucchā ajjhosānaṃ gedho paligedho saṅgo paṅko ejā māyā janikā sañjananī sibbinī jālinī saritā visattikā suttaṃ visaṭā āyūhinī dutiyā paṇidhi bhavanetti vanaṃ vanatho santhavo sineho apekkhā paṭibandhu āsā āsisanā āsisitattaṃ rūpāsā saddāsā gandhāsā rasāsā phoṭṭhabbāsā lābhāsā dhanāsā puttāsā jīvitāsā jappā pajappā abhijappā jappā jappanā jappitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañjikatā sādhukamyatā adhammarāgo visamalobho nikanti nikāmanā patthanā pihanā sampatthanā kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā rūpataṇhā arūpataṇhā nirodhataṇhā rūpataṇhā saddataṇhā gandhataṇhā rasataṇhā phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dhammataṇhā ogho yogo gantho upādānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ chādanaṃ bandhanaṃ upakkileso anusayo pariyuṭṭhānaṃ latā vevicchaṃ dukkhamūlaṃ dukkhanidānaṃ dukkhappabhavo mārapāso mārabaḷisaṃ māravisayo taṇhānadī taṇhājālaṃ taṇhāgaddulaṃ taṇhāsamuddo abhijjhā lobho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati lobho.
ai: Therein, what is greed? That which is lust, attachment, desire, infatuation, clinging, covetousness; craving for sensuality, existence, non-existence, fine-material, immaterial, cessation, forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, mental objects; the flood, bond, knot, clinging, hindrance, latent disposition, root of suffering, covetousness, greed, the unwholesome root. This is called greed.

text: 1237. Tattha katamo doso? Anatthaṃ me acarīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me caratīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me carissatīti āghāto jāyati, piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati. Yo evarūpo cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati doso.
original: Tattha katamo doso? Anatthaṃ me acarīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me caratīti āghāto jāyati, anatthaṃ me carissatīti āghāto jāyati, piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati. Yo evarūpo cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati doso.
ai: Therein, what is hatred? Ill-will arises concerning harm done to oneself or loved ones, or benefit to disliked ones, in the past, present, or future; or ill-will arises without reason. That which is such ill-will, aversion, opposition, anger, wrath, hatred, mental affliction, mental displeasure, fury, animosity, mental non-satisfaction. This is called hatred.

text: 1238. Tattha katamo moho? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ, pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃ . Yaṃ evarūpaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṃgāhanā apariyogāhanā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati moho.
rys_davids: What is unconscientiousness?⤵The absence of any feeling of conscientious scruple when scruples ought to be felt; the absence of conscientious scruple at attaining to bad and evil states.
original: Tattha katamo moho? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ, pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃ . Yaṃ evarūpaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṃgāhanā apariyogāhanā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati moho.
ai: Therein, what is delusion? Ignorance of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path to its cessation; ignorance of the past, future, both past and future; ignorance of dependent arising and dependently arisen phenomena. That which is such ignorance, non-seeing, non-comprehension, dullness, foolishness, delusion, utter delusion, confusion, ignorance, flood of ignorance, bond of ignorance, latent disposition of ignorance, defilement of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root. This is called delusion.

text: 1239. Tattha katamo māno? Seyyohamasmīti māno, sadisohamasmīti māno, hīnohamasmīti māno; yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnamo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati māno.
rys_davids: What is disregard of blame?⤵The absence of any sense of guilt where a sense of guilt ought to be felt, the absence of a sense of guilt at attaining to bad and evil states.⤵These are the states which are vices.
original: Tattha katamo māno? Seyyohamasmīti māno, sadisohamasmīti māno, hīnohamasmīti māno; yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnamo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati māno.
ai: Therein, what is conceit? Conceit thinking: 'I am superior,' 'I am equal,' 'I am inferior.' That which is such conceit, conceiving, elevation, upliftment, a banner, excessive grasping, desire for prominence of mind. This is called conceit.

text: 1240. Tattha katamā diṭṭhi? Sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vāः yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati diṭṭhi. Sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhi.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not vices?⤵All other states whatever (i.e. all except the afore-named ten), good, bad and indeterminate, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; [in other words] the four skandhas, all [material] form also and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katamā diṭṭhi? Sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vāः yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati diṭṭhi. Sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhi.
ai: Therein, what is wrong view? The view: 'The world is eternal,' or 'The world is not eternal,' or 'The world is finite,' or 'The world is infinite'; 'The soul is the same as the body,' or 'The soul is different from the body'; 'A Tathāgata exists after death,' or 'A Tathāgata does not exist after death,' or 'A Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,' or 'A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.' That which is such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, contortion of views, vacillation of views, fetter of views, grasping, adherence, dogmatic belief, misapprehension, wrong path, wrongness, heretical ground, perverted grasping. This is called wrong view. All wrong views are (called) view.

text: 1241. Tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati, dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati, saṅghe kaṅkhati vicikicchati sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, aparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbantāparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhati vicikicchatiः yā evarūpā kaṅkhā kaṅkhāyanā kaṅkhāyitattaṃ vimati vicikicchā dveḷhakaṃ dvedhāpatho saṃsayo, anekaṃsaggāho āsappanā parisappanā apariyogāhanā thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵vicious?⤵States that have Āsavas, good, bad and indeterminate, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, of Form or of the Formless; [in other words] the five skandhas.⤵not vicious?⤵The Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths, and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati, dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati, saṅghe kaṅkhati vicikicchati sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, aparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbantāparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhati vicikicchatiः yā evarūpā kaṅkhā kaṅkhāyanā kaṅkhāyitattaṃ vimati vicikicchā dveḷhakaṃ dvedhāpatho saṃsayo, anekaṃsaggāho āsappanā parisappanā apariyogāhanā thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
ai: Therein, what is skeptical doubt? Doubts and is uncertain about the Teacher, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, the training; about the past, future, both past and future; about dependent arising and dependently arisen phenomena. That which is such doubt, wavering, uncertainty, perplexity, indecision, two-pronged path, uncertainty, hesitation, mental stiffness, mental defilement. This is called skeptical doubt.

text: 1242. Tattha katamaṃ thinaṃ? Yā cittassa akallatā akammaññatā olīyanā sallīyanā līnaṃ līyanā līyitattaṃ thinaṃ thiyanā thiyitattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati thinaṃ.
original: Tattha katamaṃ thinaṃ? Yā cittassa akallatā akammaññatā olīyanā sallīyanā līnaṃ līyanā līyitattaṃ thinaṃ thiyanā thiyitattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati thinaṃ.
ai: Therein, what is sloth? That which is mental unsuitability, unworkability, sinking, drooping, sluggishness, languor, sloth of mind. This is called sloth.

text: 1243. Tattha katamaṃ uddhaccaṃ? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhantattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati uddhaccaṃ.
original: Tattha katamaṃ uddhaccaṃ? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhantattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati uddhaccaṃ.
ai: Therein, what is restlessness? That which is mental agitation, non-calmness, distraction, bewilderment of mind. This is called restlessness.

text: 1244. Tattha katamaṃ ahirikaṃ? Yaṃ na hirīyati hiriyitabbena, na hirīyati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati ahirikaṃ.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵associated with the vices?
original: Tattha katamaṃ ahirikaṃ? Yaṃ na hirīyati hiriyitabbena, na hirīyati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati ahirikaṃ.
ai: Therein, what is shamelessness? That which is not being ashamed of what should be shameful, not being ashamed of committing evil, unwholesome actions. This is called shamelessness.

text: 1245. Tattha katamaṃ anottappaṃ? Yaṃ na ottappati ottappitabbena, na ottappati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati anottappaṃ.
rys_davids: disconnected with the vices?
original: Tattha katamaṃ anottappaṃ? Yaṃ na ottappati ottappitabbena, na ottappati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati anottappaṃ.
ai: What is fearlessness of wrongdoing? Not dreading what should be dreaded, not dreading the committing of evil, unwholesome phenomena – this is called fearlessness of wrongdoing.

text: Ime dhammā kilesā.
original: Ime dhammā kilesā.
ai: These phenomena are defilements.

text: 1246. Katame dhammā no kilesā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho …pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no kilesā.
rys_davids: both vices and vicious?
original: Katame dhammā no kilesā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho …pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā no kilesā.
ai: Which phenomena are not defilements? Excluding those defilements, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena in the sense, fine-material, immaterial, and supramundane spheres; the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate; all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not defilements.

text: 1247. Katame dhammā saṃkilesikā? Sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā saṃkilesikā.
rys_davids: vicious but not themselves vices?⤵Answers as in the corresponding pairs in the “Graspings”, §§ 1221 – 1224 .
original: Katame dhammā saṃkilesikā? Sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā saṃkilesikā.
ai: Which phenomena are conducive to defilement? Wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena subject to taints in the sense, fine-material, and immaterial spheres; the matter aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate – these phenomena are conducive to defilement.

text: 1248. Katame dhammā asaṃkilesikā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā asaṃkilesikā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵both vices and vitiated?⤵The vices themselves.⤵vitiated but not themselves vices?⤵The states which by those ten states are vitiated, the ten themselves excepted; [in other words] the four skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā asaṃkilesikā? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā asaṃkilesikā.
ai: Which phenomena are not conducive to defilement? Supramundane paths, path fruitions, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not conducive to defilement.

text: 1249. Katame dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā.
original: Katame dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho; tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā.
ai: Which phenomena are actually defiled? The three unwholesome roots – greed, hatred, delusion; and defilements co-existent with them, the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them, and bodily, verbal, and mental kamma originating from them – these phenomena are actually defiled.

text: 1250. Katame dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhā? Kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵both vices and associated with vice?⤵Greed, hate, conceit, speculative opinion, perplexity, stolidity, distraction, unconscientiousness, and disregard of blame taken severally in conjunction with dullness, and dullness in conjunction with each of them. Greed, also, in conjunction with distraction, and conversely, and so for the remaining eight bases. Greed, also, in conjunction with unconscientiousness, and conversely, and so for the remaining eight. Greed, also, in conjunction with disregard of blame, and conversely, and so for the remaining eight.
original: Katame dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhā? Kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā asaṃkiliṭṭhā.
ai: Which phenomena are undefiled? Wholesome and indeterminate phenomena in the sense, fine-material, immaterial, and supramundane spheres; the feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate; all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are undefiled.

text: 1251. Katame dhammā kilesasampayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā kilesasampayuttā.
rys_davids: associated with vices but not themselves vices?
original: Katame dhammā kilesasampayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā kilesasampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with defilements? The feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate that are associated with them – these phenomena are associated with defilements.

text: 1252. Katame dhammā kilesavippayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho ; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā kilesavippayuttā.
rys_davids: disconnected with vices but vicious?
original: Katame dhammā kilesavippayuttā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho ; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā kilesavippayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from defilements? The feeling aggregate... up to the consciousness aggregate that are dissociated from them; all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are dissociated from defilements.

text: 1253. Katame dhammā kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā ca? Teva kilesā kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā ca.
rys_davids: disconnected with vices and not vicious?⤵Answers to these three questions as in former groups. See §§ 1226 – 1228 , §§ 1771 – 1173 , etc..⤵In the first edition kilesā was rendered as “Corruptions”. “Vices” is not etymologically a better fit, but, as a stock term for wrong ways or states, it comes nearer in usage to kilesa. These stand, in all but the earliest Pāli (kilesā is hard to find in Vinaya or Dhamma), for the lower, unregenerate side of the average man's nature.⤵The Supplementary Set of Pairs ( piṭṭhidukaṃ )
original: Katame dhammā kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā ca? Teva kilesā kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are both defilements and conducive to defilement? Those very defilements are both defilements and conducive to defilement.

text: 1254. Katame dhammā saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā saṃkilesikā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are to be put away by vision?⤵The Three Fetters, to wit: theory of individuality, perplexity and perversion as to rule and ritual.
original: Katame dhammā saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā saṃkilesikā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā.
ai: Which phenomena are defiling but not defilements? Excluding those phenomena that are defiling, the remaining taints-associated wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the aggregate of form... up to... the aggregate of consciousness – these phenomena are defiling but not defilements.

text: 1255. Katame dhammā kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā ca? Teva kilesā kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā ca.
rys_davids: Identical with §§ 1003 – 1006 .
original: Katame dhammā kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā ca? Teva kilesā kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are defilements and are also defiled? The defilements themselves are defilements and are also defiled.

text: 1256. Katame dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā.
original: Katame dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā, te dhamme ṭhapetvā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā.
ai: Which phenomena are defiled but not defilements? Excluding those phenomena that are defiled, the aggregate of feeling... up to... the aggregate of consciousness – these phenomena are defiled but not defilements.
