anottappena kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañca, anottappaṃ thinena kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañca, uddhaccaṃ anottappena kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañca, anottappaṃ uddhaccena kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañca, ahirikaṃ anottappena kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañca, anottappaṃ ahirikena kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañca – ime dhammā kilesā ceva kilesasampayuttā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are defilements and are associated with defilements? Greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and fearlessness of wrongdoing, when associated with each other in various pairings, are defilements and are associated with defilements.

text: 1258. Katame dhammā kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā te dhamme ṭhapetvā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are not to be put away by vision?⤵All states whatever, good, bad and indeterminate, except the three afore-mentioned, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; [in other words] the four skandhas; all [material] form also and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā te dhamme ṭhapetvā vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with defilements but are not defilements? Excluding those phenomena that are associated, the aggregate of feeling... up to... the aggregate of consciousness – these phenomena are associated with defilements but are not defilements.

text: 1259. Katame dhammā kilesavippayuttā saṃkilesikā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā sāsavā kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā kilesavippayuttā saṃkilesikā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵to be put away by cultivation?⤵All the remaining lust, hate and dullness as well as the vices united with them, the four skandhas associated with them, and the action, bodily, vocal and mental, springing from them.⤵not to be put away by cultivation?⤵Answer as for those states which are not to be put away by insight [ § 1258 ].
original: Katame dhammā kilesavippayuttā saṃkilesikā? Tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā sāsavā kusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā; rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā kilesavippayuttā saṃkilesikā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from defilements but are defiling? Excluding those phenomena that are dissociated, the taints-associated wholesome and indeterminate phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere; the aggregate of form... up to... the aggregate of consciousness – these phenomena are dissociated from defilements but are defiling.

text: 1260. Katame dhammā kilesavippayuttā asaṃkilesikā ? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā kilesavippayuttā asaṃkilesikā.
original: Katame dhammā kilesavippayuttā asaṃkilesikā ? Apariyāpannā maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā kilesavippayuttā asaṃkilesikā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from defilements and are not defiling? The unincluded paths, and their fruits, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are dissociated from defilements and are not defiling.

text: Piṭṭhidukaṃ
original: Piṭṭhidukaṃ
ai: ⤵The Section on Abandonment.

text: 1261. Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbā? Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.
rys_davids: Which are the states the causes of which are to be put away by vision?⤵The Three Fetters, to wit: theory of individuality, perplexity and perversion as to rule and ritual.
original: Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbā? Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.
ai: Which phenomena are to be abandoned by vision? The three fetters: identity view, doubt, and clinging to rites and rituals.

text: 1262. Tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sakkāyadiṭṭhi.
rys_davids: Identical with §§ 1003 – 1006 .
original: Tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sakkāyadiṭṭhi.
ai: What is identity view? Here, an uninstructed ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, unskilled in the noble Dhamma, undisciplined in the noble Dhamma, not seeing the true persons, unskilled in the Dhamma of the true persons, undisciplined in the Dhamma of the true persons, perceives form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. Feeling... perception... mental formations... consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever such view, wrong view... up to... grasping of perversion – this is called identity view.

text: 1263. Tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati…pe… thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
original: Tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati…pe… thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
ai: Among these, what is doubt? Wavering, doubting concerning the Teacher... stiffness of mind, mental defilement – this is called doubt.

text: 1264. Tattha katamo sīlabbataparāmāso? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlena suddhi vatena suddhi sīlabbatena suddhīti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sīlabbataparāmāso. Imāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni, tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā.
original: Tattha katamo sīlabbataparāmāso? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlena suddhi vatena suddhi sīlabbatena suddhīti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sīlabbataparāmāso. Imāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni, tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā.
ai: Among these, what is clinging to rites and rituals? The view among recluses and brahmins outside [this dispensation] that purity comes from morality, purity comes from observances, purity comes from morality and observances – such a view, wrong view... mistaken apprehension – this is called clinging to rites and rituals. These three fetters, and defilements rooted in them, the feeling aggregate... consciousness aggregate associated with them, bodily action, vocal action, mental action originating from them – these states are to be abandoned by seeing.

text: 1265. Katame dhammā na dassanena pahātabbā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na dassanena pahātabbā.
rys_davids: Which are the states the causes of which are not to be put away by insight?⤵Answer as for those “states which are not to be put away (by insight”, § 1258 .
original: Katame dhammā na dassanena pahātabbā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na dassanena pahātabbā.
ai: Which states are not to be abandoned by seeing? Excluding those states, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and unincluded; the feeling aggregate... consciousness aggregate; all matter, and the unconditioned element – these states are not to be abandoned by seeing.

text: 1266. Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Avaseso lobho doso moho, tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
rys_davids: Which are the states the causes of which are⤵to be put away by cultivation?⤵All the remaining lust, hate and dullness: these are the causes that are to be put away by cultivation. And the vices united with them, the four skandhas associated with them, and the action, bodily, vocal and mental, springing from them, are the states the causes of which are to be put away by cultivation.⤵not to be put away by cultivation?⤵Answer as for the “states which are not to be put away by cultivation”, § 1260 .
original: Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Avaseso lobho doso moho, tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
ai: Which states are to be abandoned by development? The remaining greed, hatred, and delusion, and defilements rooted in them, the feeling aggregate... consciousness aggregate associated with them, bodily action, vocal action, mental action originating from them – these states are to be abandoned by development.

text: 1267. Katame dhammā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho …pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
original: Katame dhammā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho …pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
ai: Which states are not to be abandoned by development? Excluding those states, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and unincluded; the feeling aggregate... consciousness aggregate; all matter, and the unconditioned element – these states are not to be abandoned by development.

text: 1268. Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā? Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.
rys_davids: Which are the states⤵“with applied thinking”?⤵The four skandhas when associated with conception (the latter not being included) [which springs up] in a soil wherein is application of thought, either in the worlds of Sense or Form, or in the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā? Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.
ai: Which states have causes to be abandoned by seeing? The three fetters: identity view, doubt, clinging to rites and rituals.

text: 1269. Tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sakkāyadiṭṭhi.
rys_davids: “without applied thinking”?⤵The four skandhas when springing up in a soil void of applied thinking, either in the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or in the life that is Unincluded; applied thinking itself also, and all [material] form and unconditioned element.
original: Tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sakkāyadiṭṭhi.
ai: Among these, what is identity view? Here, an uninstructed ordinary person, not seeing noble ones, unskilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained in the noble Dhamma, not seeing true persons, unskilled in the Dhamma of true persons, not trained in the Dhamma of true persons, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. Similarly, regards feeling... perception... mental formations... consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Such a view, wrong view... mistaken apprehension – this is called identity view.

text: 1270. Tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati…pe… thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
rys_davids: “with sustained thinking”?
original: Tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati…pe… thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati vicikicchā.
ai: Among these, what is doubt? Wavering, doubting concerning the Teacher... stiffness of mind, mental defilement – this is called doubt.

text: 1271. Tattha katamo sīlabbataparāmāso? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlena suddhi vatena suddhi sīlabbatena suddhīti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sīlabbataparāmāso. Imāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni, tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā. Tadekaṭṭho lobho doso moho – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetū. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā.
rys_davids: “without sustained thinking”?⤵Answers (substituting “sustained thinking” for “applied thinking”) as in § 1268 , § 1269 , respectively.
original: Tattha katamo sīlabbataparāmāso? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlena suddhi vatena suddhi sīlabbatena suddhīti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati sīlabbataparāmāso. Imāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni, tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā. Tadekaṭṭho lobho doso moho – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetū. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Among these, what is clinging to rites and rituals? The view among recluses and brahmins outside [this dispensation] that purity comes from morality, purity comes from observances, purity comes from morality and observances – such a view, wrong view... mistaken apprehension – this is called clinging to rites and rituals. These three fetters, and defilements rooted in them, the feeling aggregate... consciousness aggregate associated with them, bodily action, vocal action, mental action originating from them – these states have causes to be abandoned by seeing. The three fetters – identity view, doubt, clinging to rites and rituals – these states are to be abandoned by seeing. Greed, hatred, and delusion rooted in them – these states are causes to be abandoned by seeing. And defilements rooted in them, the feeling aggregate... consciousness aggregate associated with them, bodily action, vocal action, mental action originating from them – these states have causes to be abandoned by seeing.

text: 1272. Katame dhammā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā , rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵with zest?
original: Katame dhammā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā , rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Which states do not have causes to be abandoned by seeing? Excluding those states, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and unincluded; the feeling aggregate... consciousness aggregate; all matter, and the unconditioned element – these states do not have causes to be abandoned by seeing.

text: 1273. Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Avaseso lobho doso moho – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetū. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
rys_davids: without zest?
original: Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Avaseso lobho doso moho – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetū. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Which phenomena have causes to be abandoned by development? The remaining greed, hatred, delusion – these phenomena are causes to be abandoned by development. And defilements associated with them, the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate associated with them, and bodily, verbal, and mental kamma originated from them – these phenomena have causes to be abandoned by development.

text: 1274. Katame dhammā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
rys_davids: accompanied by zest?
original: Katame dhammā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Te dhamme ṭhapetvā avasesā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Which phenomena do not have causes to be abandoned by development? Excluding those phenomena, the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate; and all material phenomena, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena do not have causes to be abandoned by development.

text: 1275. Katame dhammā savitakkā? Savitakkabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, vitakkaṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā savitakkā.
rys_davids: unaccompanied by zest?
original: Katame dhammā savitakkā? Savitakkabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, vitakkaṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā savitakkā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by initial application? In the sphere of initial application, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane, excluding initial application, the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate associated with it – these phenomena are accompanied by initial application.

text: 1276. Katame dhammā avitakkā? Avitakkabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; vitakko ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā avitakkā.
rys_davids: accompanied by ease?
original: Katame dhammā avitakkā? Avitakkabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; vitakko ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā avitakkā.
ai: Which phenomena are not accompanied by initial application? In the sphere without initial application, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate; and initial application, and all material phenomena, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not accompanied by initial application.

text: 1277. Katame dhammā savicārā? Savicārabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, vicāraṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā savicārā.
rys_davids: unaccompanied by ease?⤵Answers to each pair of questions analogous to those in §§ 1268 , 1269 , “zest” or “ease” being substituted in due order for “applied thinking”.
original: Katame dhammā savicārā? Savicārabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, vicāraṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā savicārā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by sustained application? In the sphere of sustained application, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane, excluding sustained application, the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the mental formations aggregate, the consciousness aggregate associated with it – these phenomena are accompanied by sustained application.

text: 1278. Katame dhammā avicārā? Avicārabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; vicāro ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā avicārā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵accompanied by indifference?⤵The three skandhas of perception, synergies and consciousness, when associated with indifference (the latter not being included), [which springs up] in a soil congenial to it, either in the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or in the life that is Unincluded.⤵unaccompanied by indifference?⤵The four skandhas [when springing up] in a soil uncongenial to indifference, either in the worlds of Sense or Form, or in the life that is Unincluded; indifference itself also, and all [material] form and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā avicārā? Avicārabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; vicāro ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā avicārā.
ai: Which phenomena are not accompanied by sustained application? In the sphere without sustained application, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate; and sustained application, and all material phenomena, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not accompanied by sustained application.

text: 1279. Katame dhammā sappītikā? Sappītikabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne , pītiṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sappītikā.
original: Katame dhammā sappītikā? Sappītikabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne , pītiṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sappītikā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by rapture? In the sphere of rapture, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane, excluding rapture, the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate associated with it – these phenomena are accompanied by rapture.

text: 1280. Katame dhammā appītikā? Appītikabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; pīti ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā appītikā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that⤵relate (belong) to the universe of Sense?⤵Take from the waveless deep of woe beneath up to the heaven above of the Parinimittavasavatti devas inclusive—then whatever has there its range, and is therein included, whether it be skandha, element or sphere—form, feeling, perception, synergies, cognition: these are states that relate (belong) to the universe of Sense.
original: Katame dhammā appītikā? Appītikabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; pīti ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā appītikā.
ai: Which phenomena are not accompanied by rapture? In the sphere without rapture, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate; and rapture, and all material phenomena, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not accompanied by rapture.

text: 1281. Katame dhammā pītisahagatā? Pītibhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, pītiṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā pītisahagatā.
rys_davids: do not relate (belong) to the universe of Sense?⤵The universe of Form, that of the Formless and the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā pītisahagatā? Pītibhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, pītiṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā pītisahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are concomitant with rapture? In the sphere of rapture, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane, excluding rapture, the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate associated with it – these phenomena are concomitant with rapture.

text: 1282. Katame dhammā na pītisahagatā? Na pītibhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; pīti ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na pītisahagatā.
rys_davids: relate (belong) to the universe of Form?⤵Take from the Brahma-world below up to the heaven above of the Akaniṭṭha gods inclusive—then whatever states, both of mind and mental properties, have therein their range and are therein included, whether they are states of one who has attained [Jhāna having potential good], or of one in whom [resultant Jhāna] has arisen, or of one living happily under present conditions.
original: Katame dhammā na pītisahagatā? Na pītibhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; pīti ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na pītisahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are not concomitant with rapture? In the sphere without rapture, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate...pe...the consciousness aggregate; and rapture, and all material phenomena, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not concomitant with rapture.

text: 1283. Katame dhammā sukhasahagatā? Sukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sukhasahagatā.
rys_davids: do not relate (belong) to the universe of Form?⤵The universe of Sense, that of the Formless and the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā sukhasahagatā? Sukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā sukhasahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by pleasure?⤵In the plane of pleasure, in the sense-sphere, form-sphere, and the unincluded, excluding pleasure itself, the associated aggregate of perception, aggregate of formations, and aggregate of consciousness – these phenomena are accompanied by pleasure.

text: 1284. Katame dhammā na sukhasahagatā? Na sukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sukhañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na sukhasahagatā.
rys_davids: relate (belong) to the universe of the Formless?⤵Take from the entrance among the denizens of “the sphere of infinite space” as the lower limit, and up to the entrance above among the devas of “the sphere where there is neither perception nor non-perception”—then whatever states, both of mind and mental properties, have therein their range and are therein included, whether they are states of one who has attained [Jhāna having potential good], or of one in whom [resultant Jhāna] has arisen, or of one living happily under present conditions: these are states that relate (belong) to the universe of the Formless.
original: Katame dhammā na sukhasahagatā? Na sukhabhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne; vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho; sukhañca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na sukhasahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are not accompanied by pleasure?⤵Not in the plane of pleasure, in the sense-sphere, form-sphere, formless-sphere, or unincluded; the aggregate of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; and pleasure itself, all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not accompanied by pleasure.

text: 1285. Katame dhammā upekkhāsahagatā? Upekkhābhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne, upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upekkhāsahagatā.
rys_davids: do not relate (belong) to the universe of the Formless?⤵The universe of Sense, that of Form, and the life that is Unincluded.
original: Katame dhammā upekkhāsahagatā? Upekkhābhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare arūpāvacare apariyāpanne, upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā, taṃsampayutto saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā upekkhāsahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are accompanied by equanimity?⤵In the plane of equanimity, in the sense-sphere, form-sphere, formless-sphere, and the unincluded, excluding equanimity itself, the associated aggregate of perception, aggregate of formations, and aggregate of consciousness – these phenomena are accompanied by equanimity.

text: 1286. Katame dhammā na upekkhāsahagatā? Na upekkhābhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, upekkhā ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na upekkhāsahagatā.
rys_davids: belong to the Included?⤵States that have Āsavas, good, bad and indeterminate, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, of Form or of the Formless; [in other words] the five skandhas.
original: Katame dhammā na upekkhāsahagatā? Na upekkhābhūmiyaṃ kāmāvacare rūpāvacare apariyāpanne, vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho, upekkhā ca, sabbañca rūpaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā na upekkhāsahagatā.
ai: Which phenomena are not accompanied by equanimity?⤵Not in the plane of equanimity, in the sense-sphere, form-sphere, or unincluded; the aggregate of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; and equanimity itself, all matter, and the unconditioned element – these phenomena are not accompanied by equanimity.

text: 1287. Katame dhammā kāmāvacarā? Heṭṭhato avicinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito paranimmitavasavattī deve [paranimmitavasavattideve (sī. ka.)] anto karitvā, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā khandhadhātu āyatanā, rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā kāmāvacarā.
rys_davids: belong to the Unincluded?⤵The Paths, and the Fruit of the Paths, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā kāmāvacarā? Heṭṭhato avicinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito paranimmitavasavattī deve [paranimmitavasavattideve (sī. ka.)] anto karitvā, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā khandhadhātu āyatanā, rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā kāmāvacarā.
ai: Which phenomena belong to the sense-sphere?⤵Taking Avīci hell as the lower boundary, and the Paranimmita-vasavattī devas as the upper boundary, whatever aggregates, elements, and sense-bases are included within this range, namely matter, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness – these phenomena belong to the sense-sphere.

text: 1288. Katame dhammā na kāmāvacarā? Rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na kāmāvacarā.
rys_davids: Which are the states by which⤵there is a going away?⤵The four Paths that are the Unincluded.⤵there is no going away?⤵All states, good, bad and indeterminate, except those four, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; [in other words] the four skandhas; all [material] form also, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā na kāmāvacarā? Rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na kāmāvacarā.
ai: Which phenomena do not belong to the sense-sphere?⤵Phenomena of the form-sphere, formless-sphere, and the unincluded – these phenomena do not belong to the sense-sphere.

text: 1289. Katame dhammā rūpāvacarā? Heṭṭhato brahmalokaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito akaniṭṭhe deve [akaniṭṭhadeve (sī. ka.)] anto karitvā, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa [diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārassa (ka.)] vā cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā rūpāvacarā .
original: Katame dhammā rūpāvacarā? Heṭṭhato brahmalokaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito akaniṭṭhe deve [akaniṭṭhadeve (sī. ka.)] anto karitvā, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa [diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārassa (ka.)] vā cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā rūpāvacarā .
ai: Which phenomena belong to the form-sphere?⤵Taking the Brahma-world as the lower boundary, and the Akanittha devas as the upper boundary, whatever mental states and mental factors are included within this range, belonging to one who has attained, or one who has been reborn, or one who dwells in happiness in this very life – these phenomena belong to the form-sphere.

text: 1290. Katame dhammā na rūpāvacarā? Kāmāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na rūpāvacarā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵fixed?⤵The five acts that have immediate results, and those wrong views that are fixed in their consequences; the four Paths also that are the Unincluded.⤵not fixed?⤵Answer as in § 1289 .
original: Katame dhammā na rūpāvacarā? Kāmāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na rūpāvacarā.
ai: Which phenomena do not belong to the form-sphere?⤵Phenomena of the sense-sphere, formless-sphere, and the unincluded – these phenomena do not belong to the form-sphere.

text: 1291. Katame dhammā arūpāvacarā? Heṭṭhato ākāsānañcāyatanupage deve pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito nevasaññānāsaññāyatanupage deve anto karitvā, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā arūpāvacarā.
original: Katame dhammā arūpāvacarā? Heṭṭhato ākāsānañcāyatanupage deve pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito nevasaññānāsaññāyatanupage deve anto karitvā, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā arūpāvacarā.
ai: Which phenomena belong to the formless-sphere?⤵Taking the devas of the base of infinite space as the lower boundary, and the devas of the base of neither perception nor non-perception as the upper boundary, whatever mental states and mental factors are included within this range, belonging to one who has attained, or one who has been reborn, or one who dwells in happiness in this very life – these phenomena belong to the formless-sphere.

text: 1292. Katame dhammā na arūpāvacarā? Kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na arūpāvacarā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that have⤵something beyond?⤵States that have Āsavas, good, bad and indeterminate, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, of Form or of the Formless; in other words, the five skandhas.⤵no “beyond”?⤵The four Paths that are the Unincluded, and the Fruits of the Paths, and unconditioned element.
original: Katame dhammā na arūpāvacarā? Kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na arūpāvacarā.
ai: Which phenomena do not belong to the formless-sphere?⤵Phenomena of the sense-sphere, form-sphere, and the unincluded – these phenomena do not belong to the formless-sphere.

text: 1293. Katame dhammā pariyāpannā? Sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā pariyāpannā.
original: Katame dhammā pariyāpannā? Sāsavā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā pariyāpannā.
ai: Which phenomena are included?⤵Phenomena subject to taints, wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere; the form aggregate... up to... the consciousness aggregate—these phenomena are included.

text: 1294. Katame dhammā apariyāpannā? Maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā apariyāpannā.
rys_davids: Which are the states that are⤵harmful?⤵The three roots of bad (karma): greed, hate and dullness—and the Corruptions united with them; the four skandhas associated with them; the action, bodily, vocal and mental, springing from them.⤵harmless?⤵Good, bad and indeterminate states, whether they relate to the worlds of Sense, Form or the Formless, or to the life that is Unincluded; [in other words] the four skandhas; all [material] form also, and unconditioned element.⤵A Buddhist Manual of Psychological Ethics , a rys_davids of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī, Compendium of States or Phenomena, by Caroline A.F.
