Kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato ekādasa cittuppādā, akusalassa vipākato dve, kiriyato ekādasa, rūpāvacaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppanne vitakkavicāre ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā savitakkasavicārā.
ai: What phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application? Wholesome and unwholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; eleven resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; two resultant unwholesome consciousnesses; eleven functional consciousnesses; the first fine-material jhána, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the first supramundane jhána, wholesome and resultant – excluding the initial application and sustained application arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application.

text: 1400. Katame dhammā avitakkavicāramattā? Rūpāvacarapañcakanaye dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttarapañcakanaye dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppannaṃ vicāraṃ ṭhapetvā, vitakko ca – ime dhammā avitakkavicāramattā.
original: Katame dhammā avitakkavicāramattā? Rūpāvacarapañcakanaye dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttarapañcakanaye dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppannaṃ vicāraṃ ṭhapetvā, vitakko ca – ime dhammā avitakkavicāramattā.
ai: What phenomena are without initial application but with sustained application only? The second fine-material jhána in the five-fold system, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the second supramundane jhána in the five-fold system, wholesome and resultant – excluding the sustained application arising therein – and initial application – these phenomena are without initial application but with sustained application only.

text: 1401. Katame dhammā avitakkaavicārā? Dvepañcaviññāṇāni, rūpāvacaratikatikajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, cattāro āruppā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca lokuttaratikatikajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca pañcakanaye dutiye jhāne [dutiyajjhāne (sī.)], uppanno ca vicāro rūpañca nibbānañca – ime dhammā avitakkaavicārā. Vitakkasahajāto vicāro na vattabbo savitakkasavicārotipi, avitakkavicāramattotipi, avitakkaavicārotipi.
original: Katame dhammā avitakkaavicārā? Dvepañcaviññāṇāni, rūpāvacaratikatikajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, cattāro āruppā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca lokuttaratikatikajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca pañcakanaye dutiye jhāne [dutiyajjhāne (sī.)], uppanno ca vicāro rūpañca nibbānañca – ime dhammā avitakkaavicārā. Vitakkasahajāto vicāro na vattabbo savitakkasavicārotipi, avitakkavicāramattotipi, avitakkaavicārotipi.
ai: What phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application? The two sets of fivefold sense consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána triads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the four immaterial jhána consciousnesses, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána triads, wholesome and resultant, and the second jhána in the five-fold system; and sustained application arising therein; and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application. Sustained application co-arising with initial application should not be said to be accompanied by initial application and sustained application, nor only by sustained application, nor without initial application and without sustained application.

text: 1402. Katame dhammā pītisahagatā? Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro somanassasahagatacittuppādā , akusalato cattāro, kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato pañca, kiriyato pañca, rūpāvacaradukatikajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttaradukatikajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppannaṃ pītiṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā pītisahagatā.
original: Katame dhammā pītisahagatā? Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro somanassasahagatacittuppādā , akusalato cattāro, kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato pañca, kiriyato pañca, rūpāvacaradukatikajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttaradukatikajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppannaṃ pītiṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā pītisahagatā.
ai: What phenomena are accompanied by rapture? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by joy; four unwholesome consciousnesses; five resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; five functional consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána dyads and triads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána dyads and triads, wholesome and resultant – excluding the rapture arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by rapture.

text: 1403. Katame dhammā sukhasahagatā? Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro somanassasahagatacittuppādā, akusalato cattāro, kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato cha, kiriyato pañca, rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppannaṃ sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā sukhasahagatā.
original: Katame dhammā sukhasahagatā? Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro somanassasahagatacittuppādā, akusalato cattāro, kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato cha, kiriyato pañca, rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppannaṃ sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā sukhasahagatā.
ai: What phenomena are accompanied by happiness? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by joy; four unwholesome consciousnesses; six resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; five functional consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána triads and tetrads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána triads and tetrads, wholesome and resultant – excluding the happiness arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by happiness.

text: 1404. Katame dhammā upekkhāsahagatā? Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro upekkhāsahagatacittuppādā, akusalato cha, kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato dasa, akusalassa vipākato cha, kiriyato cha, rūpāvacaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, cattāro āruppā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppannaṃ upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā upekkhāsahagatā. Pīti na pītisahagatā, sukhasahagatā, na upekkhāsahagatā. Sukhaṃ na sukhasahagataṃ, siyā pītisahagataṃ, na upekkhāsahagataṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ pītisahagatanti. Dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā, dukkhasahagatakāyaviññāṇaṃ, yā ca vedanā upekkhā , rūpañca nibbānañca – ime dhammā na vattabbā pītisahagatātipi, sukhasahagatātipi, upekkhāsahagatātipi.
original: Katame dhammā upekkhāsahagatā? Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro upekkhāsahagatacittuppādā, akusalato cha, kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato dasa, akusalassa vipākato cha, kiriyato cha, rūpāvacaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, cattāro āruppā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, lokuttaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca vipākato ca, etthuppannaṃ upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā upekkhāsahagatā. Pīti na pītisahagatā, sukhasahagatā, na upekkhāsahagatā. Sukhaṃ na sukhasahagataṃ, siyā pītisahagataṃ, na upekkhāsahagataṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ pītisahagatanti. Dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā, dukkhasahagatakāyaviññāṇaṃ, yā ca vedanā upekkhā , rūpañca nibbānañca – ime dhammā na vattabbā pītisahagatātipi, sukhasahagatātipi, upekkhāsahagatātipi.
ai: What phenomena are accompanied by equanimity? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity; six unwholesome consciousnesses; ten resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; six resultant unwholesome consciousnesses; six functional consciousnesses; the fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the four immaterial jhána consciousnesses, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the fourth supramundane jhána, wholesome and resultant – excluding the equanimity arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by equanimity. Rapture is not accompanied by rapture, is accompanied by happiness, is not accompanied by equanimity. Happiness is not accompanied by happiness, may be accompanied by rapture, is not accompanied by equanimity, and may not be said to be accompanied by rapture. The two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, body-consciousness accompanied by pain, the feeling of equanimity, and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena should not be said to be accompanied by rapture, nor by happiness, nor by equanimity.

text: 1405. Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittuppādā, vicikicchāsahagato cittuppādo – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā.
original: Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittuppādā, vicikicchāsahagato cittuppādo – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbā.
ai: What phenomena are to be abandoned by insight? The four consciousnesses associated with wrong view, and the consciousness accompanied by doubt – these phenomena are to be abandoned by insight.

text: 1406. Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttā lobhasahagatacittuppādā, dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā – ime dhammā siyā dassanena pahātabbā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
original: Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttā lobhasahagatacittuppādā, dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā – ime dhammā siyā dassanena pahātabbā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
ai: What phenomena are to be abandoned by development? The consciousness accompanied by restlessness – these phenomena are to be abandoned by development. The four greed-rooted consciousnesses dissociated from wrong view, and the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure – these phenomena may be abandoned by insight or by development.

text: 1407. Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
original: Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā.
ai: What phenomena are to be abandoned neither by insight nor by development? Wholesome consciousnesses in the four planes; resultant consciousnesses in the four planes; functional indeterminate consciousnesses in the three planes; and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena are to be abandoned neither by insight nor by development.

text: 1408. Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittuppādā, vicikicchāsahagato cittuppādo, etthuppannaṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā.
original: Katame dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittuppādā, vicikicchāsahagato cittuppādo, etthuppannaṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Which states have roots to be abandoned by seeing? The four consciousnesses associated with wrong view, the consciousness accompanied by doubt, excluding the delusion arising therein – these states have roots to be abandoned by seeing.

text: 1409. Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo, etthuppannaṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttā lobhasahagatacittuppādā, dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā – ime dhammā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
original: Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo, etthuppannaṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttā lobhasahagatacittuppādā, dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā – ime dhammā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Which states have roots to be abandoned by development? The consciousness accompanied by restlessness, excluding the delusion arising therein – these states have roots to be abandoned by development. The four consciousnesses accompanied by greed, dissociated from wrong view, and the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure – these states may have roots to be abandoned by seeing, or may have roots to be abandoned by development.

text: 1410. Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
original: Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā? Vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.
ai: Which states have roots to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development? Delusion accompanied by doubt, delusion accompanied by restlessness, wholesome states in the four planes, resultant states in the four planes, functional indeterminate states in the three planes, and matter, and Nibbāna – these states have roots to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development.

text: 1411. Katame dhammā ācayagāmino? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ – ime dhammā ācayagāmino.
original: Katame dhammā ācayagāmino? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ – ime dhammā ācayagāmino.
ai: Which states lead to accumulation? Wholesome states in the three planes, unwholesome states – these states lead to accumulation.

text: 1412. Katame dhammā apacayagāmino? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā – ime dhammā apacayagāmino.
original: Katame dhammā apacayagāmino? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā – ime dhammā apacayagāmino.
ai: Which states lead to reduction? The four supramundane paths – these states lead to reduction.

text: 1413. Katame dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino? Catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino.
original: Katame dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino? Catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino.
ai: Which states lead neither to accumulation nor to reduction? Resultant states in the four planes, functional indeterminate states in the three planes, and matter, and Nibbāna – these states lead neither to accumulation nor to reduction.

text: 1414. Katame dhammā sekkhā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, heṭṭhimāni ca tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā sekkhā.
original: Katame dhammā sekkhā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, heṭṭhimāni ca tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā sekkhā.
ai: Which states are learners? The four supramundane paths, and the three lower fruits of recluseship – these states are learners.

text: 1415. Katame dhammā asekkhā? Upariṭṭhimaṃ arahattaphalaṃ – ime dhammā asekkhā.
original: Katame dhammā asekkhā? Upariṭṭhimaṃ arahattaphalaṃ – ime dhammā asekkhā.
ai: Which states are perfected? The highest fruit of Arahantship – these states are perfected.

text: 1416. Katame dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā.
original: Katame dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā.
ai: Which states are neither learners nor perfected? Wholesome states in the three planes, unwholesome states, resultant states in the three planes, functional indeterminate states in the three planes, and matter, and Nibbāna – these states are neither learners nor perfected.

text: 1417. Katame dhammā parittā? Kāmāvacarakusalaṃ , akusalaṃ, sabbo kāmāvacarassa vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā parittā.
original: Katame dhammā parittā? Kāmāvacarakusalaṃ , akusalaṃ, sabbo kāmāvacarassa vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā parittā.
ai: Which states are limited? Wholesome states of the sense sphere, unwholesome states, all resultant states of the sense sphere, functional indeterminate states of the sense sphere, and all matter – these states are limited.

text: 1418. Katame dhammā mahaggatā? Rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, kusalābyākatā – ime dhammā mahaggatā.
original: Katame dhammā mahaggatā? Rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, kusalābyākatā – ime dhammā mahaggatā.
ai: What dhammas are exalted? Form-sphere, formless-sphere, wholesome-indeterminate – these dhammas are exalted.

text: 1419. Katame dhammā appamāṇā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā appamāṇā.
original: Katame dhammā appamāṇā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā appamāṇā.
ai: What dhammas are immeasurable? The four paths not included (in the realms), the four fruitions of recluseship, and Nibbāna – these dhammas are immeasurable.

text: 1420. Katame dhammā parittārammaṇā? Sabbo kāmāvacarassa vipāko, kiriyāmanodhātu, kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu somanassasahagatā – ime dhammā parittārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā parittārammaṇā? Sabbo kāmāvacarassa vipāko, kiriyāmanodhātu, kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu somanassasahagatā – ime dhammā parittārammaṇā.
ai: What dhammas have limited objects? All resultant consciousness of the sense-sphere, functional mind-element, functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy – these dhammas have limited objects.

text: 1421. Katame dhammā mahaggatārammaṇā? Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā mahaggatārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā mahaggatārammaṇā? Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā mahaggatārammaṇā.
ai: What dhammas have exalted objects? The base of infinite consciousness, the base of neither perception nor non-perception – these dhammas have exalted objects.

text: 1422. Katame dhammā appamāṇārammaṇā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā appamāṇārammaṇā. Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇavippayuttacittuppādā, kiriyato cattāro ñāṇavippayuttacittuppādā, sabbaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, na appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi, mahaggatārammaṇātipi. Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇasampayuttacittuppādā, kiriyato cattāro ñāṇasampayuttacittuppādā, rūpāvacaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca kiriyato ca, kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu upekkhāsahagatā – ime dhammā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi , mahaggatārammaṇātipi, appamāṇārammaṇātipi. Rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, catutthassa jhānassa vipāko, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ , ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi, mahaggatārammaṇātipi, appamāṇārammaṇātipi. Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā appamāṇārammaṇā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā appamāṇārammaṇā. Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇavippayuttacittuppādā, kiriyato cattāro ñāṇavippayuttacittuppādā, sabbaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, na appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi, mahaggatārammaṇātipi. Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇasampayuttacittuppādā, kiriyato cattāro ñāṇasampayuttacittuppādā, rūpāvacaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca kiriyato ca, kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu upekkhāsahagatā – ime dhammā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi , mahaggatārammaṇātipi, appamāṇārammaṇātipi. Rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, catutthassa jhānassa vipāko, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ , ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi, mahaggatārammaṇātipi, appamāṇārammaṇātipi. Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā.
ai: What dhammas have immeasurable objects? The four paths not included (in the realms), the four fruitions of recluseship – these dhammas have immeasurable objects. From wholesome sense-sphere consciousness, the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge; from functional consciousness, the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge; all unwholesome (consciousness) – these dhammas may have limited objects, may have exalted objects, not immeasurable objects, and may not be describable as having limited objects or as having exalted objects. From wholesome sense-sphere consciousness, the four consciousnesses associated with knowledge; from functional consciousness, the four consciousnesses associated with knowledge; the fourth rūpa-jhāna, both wholesome and functional; functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity – these dhammas may have limited objects, may have exalted objects, may have immeasurable objects, and may not be describable as having limited objects, or as having exalted objects, or as having immeasurable objects. The rūpa-jhānas of the triple and quadruple systems, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the resultant of the fourth jhāna; the base of infinite space; the base of nothingness – these dhammas are not describable as having limited objects, or as having exalted objects, or as having immeasurable objects. Matter and Nibbāna are without object.

text: 1423. Katame dhammā hīnā? Dvādasa akusalacittuppādā – ime dhammā hīnā.
original: Katame dhammā hīnā? Dvādasa akusalacittuppādā – ime dhammā hīnā.
ai: What dhammas are inferior? The twelve unwholesome consciousnesses – these dhammas are inferior.

text: 1424. Katame dhammā majjhimā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā majjhimā.
original: Katame dhammā majjhimā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā majjhimā.
ai: What dhammas are middling? Wholesome (consciousness) in the three planes, resultant (consciousness) in the three planes, functional indeterminate (consciousness) in the three planes, and all matter – these dhammas are middling.

text: 1425. Katame dhammā paṇītā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā paṇītā.
original: Katame dhammā paṇītā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā paṇītā.
ai: What dhammas are superior? The four paths not included (in the realms), the four fruitions of recluseship, and Nibbāna – these dhammas are superior.

text: 1426. Katame dhammā micchattaniyatā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittuppādā, dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā – ime dhammā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā.
original: Katame dhammā micchattaniyatā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittuppādā, dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā – ime dhammā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā.
ai: What dhammas are fixed in wrongness? The four consciousnesses associated with wrong view, the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure – these dhammas may be fixed in wrongness, may be unfixed.

text: 1427. Katame dhammā sammattaniyatā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā – ime dhammā sammattaniyatā.
original: Katame dhammā sammattaniyatā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā – ime dhammā sammattaniyatā.
ai: What dhammas are fixed in rightness? The four paths not included (in the realms) – these dhammas are fixed in rightness.

text: 1428. Katame dhammā aniyatā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatacittuppādā, vicikicchāsahagato cittuppādo, uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā aniyatā.
original: Katame dhammā aniyatā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatacittuppādā, vicikicchāsahagato cittuppādo, uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā aniyatā.
ai: Which phenomena are indeterminate? The four consciousnesses accompanied by greed dissociated from wrong view, consciousness accompanied by doubt, consciousness accompanied by restlessness, wholesome (consciousness) in the three planes, resultant (consciousness) in the four planes, functional indeterminate (consciousness) in the three planes, matter, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are indeterminate.

text: 1429. Katame dhammā maggārammaṇā? Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇasampayuttacittuppādā, kiriyato cattāro ñāṇasampayuttacittuppādā – ime dhammā siyā maggārammaṇā, na maggahetukā; siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggādhipatinotipi . Cattāro ariyamaggā na maggārammaṇā, maggahetukā; siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggādhipatinoti. Rūpāvacaracatutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca kiriyato ca, kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu upekkhāsahagatā – ime dhammā siyā maggārammaṇā; na maggahetukā, na maggādhipatino; siyā na vattabbā maggārammaṇāti. Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇavippayuttacittuppādā, sabbaṃ akusalaṃ, sabbo kāmāvacarassa vipāko, kiriyato cha cittuppādā, rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, catutthassa jhānassa vipāko, cattāro āruppā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā maggārammaṇā? Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇasampayuttacittuppādā, kiriyato cattāro ñāṇasampayuttacittuppādā – ime dhammā siyā maggārammaṇā, na maggahetukā; siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggādhipatinotipi . Cattāro ariyamaggā na maggārammaṇā, maggahetukā; siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggādhipatinoti. Rūpāvacaracatutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca kiriyato ca, kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu upekkhāsahagatā – ime dhammā siyā maggārammaṇā; na maggahetukā, na maggādhipatino; siyā na vattabbā maggārammaṇāti. Kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇavippayuttacittuppādā, sabbaṃ akusalaṃ, sabbo kāmāvacarassa vipāko, kiriyato cha cittuppādā, rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, catutthassa jhānassa vipāko, cattāro āruppā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā.
ai: Which phenomena are path-objects? The four wisdom-associated wholesome consciousnesses of the sense sphere, and the four wisdom-associated functional consciousnesses – these phenomena may be path-objects, are not path-causes; they may be path-dominant, or cannot be described as path-objects or path-dominant. The four Noble Paths are not path-objects, are path-causes; they may be path-dominant, or cannot be described as path-dominant. The fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome and functional, and the functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity – these phenomena may be path-objects; are not path-causes, are not path-dominant; or cannot be described as path-objects. The four wisdom-dissociated wholesome consciousnesses of the sense sphere, all unwholesome (consciousness), all resultant (consciousness) of the sense sphere, the six functional consciousnesses, the three and fourfold fine-material jhānas, wholesome, resultant, and functional, the resultant of the fourth jhána, the four immaterial (attainments), wholesome, resultant, and functional, and the four fruits of recluseship – these phenomena cannot be described as path-objects, path-causes, or path-dominant. Matter and Nibbāna are objectless.

text: 1430. Katame dhammā uppannā? Catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, yañca rūpaṃ kammassa katattā – ime dhammā siyā uppannā, siyā uppādino; na vattabbā anuppannāti. Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, yañca rūpaṃ na kammassa katattā – ime dhammā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinoti. Nibbānaṃ na vattabbaṃ uppannantipi, anuppannantipi, uppādinotipi.
original: Katame dhammā uppannā? Catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, yañca rūpaṃ kammassa katattā – ime dhammā siyā uppannā, siyā uppādino; na vattabbā anuppannāti. Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, yañca rūpaṃ na kammassa katattā – ime dhammā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinoti. Nibbānaṃ na vattabbaṃ uppannantipi, anuppannantipi, uppādinotipi.
ai: Which phenomena are arisen? Resultant (consciousness) in the four planes and matter born of kamma – these phenomena may be arisen, may be arising; cannot be described as unarisen. Wholesome (consciousness) and unwholesome (consciousness) in the four planes, functional indeterminate (consciousness) in the three planes, and matter not born of kamma – these phenomena may be arisen, may be unarisen; cannot be described as arising. Nibbāna cannot be described as arisen, unarisen, or arising.

text: 1431. Nibbānaṃ ṭhapetvā sabbe dhammā siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Nibbānaṃ na vattabbaṃ atītantipi, anāgatantipi , paccuppannantipi.
original: Nibbānaṃ ṭhapetvā sabbe dhammā siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Nibbānaṃ na vattabbaṃ atītantipi, anāgatantipi , paccuppannantipi.
ai: Except Nibbāna, all phenomena may be past, may be future, may be present. Nibbāna cannot be described as past, future, or present.

text: 1432. Katame dhammā atītārammaṇā? Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā atītārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā atītārammaṇā? Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā atītārammaṇā.
ai: Which phenomena have past objects? The base of infinite consciousness and the base of neither perception nor non-perception – these phenomena have past objects.

text: 1433. Niyogā anāgatārammaṇā natthi.
original: Niyogā anāgatārammaṇā natthi.
ai: Necessarily, there are no future objects.

text: 1434. Katame dhammā paccuppannārammaṇā? Dvepañcaviññāṇāni, tisso ca manodhātuyo – ime dhammā paccuppannārammaṇā. Kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato dasa cittuppādā, akusalassa vipākato manoviññāṇadhātu upekkhāsahagatā, kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu somanassasahagatā – ime dhammā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā. Kāmāvacarakusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kiriyato nava cittuppādā, rūpāvacaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca kiriyato ca – ime dhammā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā; siyā na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, catutthassa jhānassa vipāko, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ, cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā paccuppannārammaṇā? Dvepañcaviññāṇāni, tisso ca manodhātuyo – ime dhammā paccuppannārammaṇā. Kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato dasa cittuppādā, akusalassa vipākato manoviññāṇadhātu upekkhāsahagatā, kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu somanassasahagatā – ime dhammā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā. Kāmāvacarakusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kiriyato nava cittuppādā, rūpāvacaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca kiriyato ca – ime dhammā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā; siyā na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, catutthassa jhānassa vipāko, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ, cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā.
ai: Which phenomena have present objects? The two sets of fivefold sense consciousnesses and the three mind-elements – these phenomena have present objects. The ten resultant consciousnesses of the sense sphere, the resultant mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity of the unwholesome, the functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy – these phenomena may have past objects, may have future objects, may have present objects. Wholesome (consciousness) of the sense sphere, unwholesome (consciousness), the nine functional consciousnesses, the fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome and functional – these phenomena may have past objects, may have future objects, may have present objects; or cannot be described as having past, future, or present objects. The three and fourfold fine-material jhānas, wholesome, resultant, and functional, the resultant of the fourth jhána, the base of infinite space, the base of nothingness, the four supramundane paths, and the four fruits of recluseship – these phenomena cannot be described as having past, future, or present objects. Matter and Nibbāna are objectless.

text: 1435. Anindriyabaddharūpañca nibbānañca ṭhapetvā, sabbe dhammā siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Anindriyabaddharūpañca nibbānañca bahiddhā.
original: Anindriyabaddharūpañca nibbānañca ṭhapetvā, sabbe dhammā siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Anindriyabaddharūpañca nibbānañca bahiddhā.
ai: Except matter not bound to faculties and Nibbāna, all phenomena may be internal, may be external, may be internal and external. Matter not bound to faculties and Nibbāna are external.

text: 1436. Katame dhammā ajjhattārammaṇā? Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā ajjhattārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā ajjhattārammaṇā? Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā ajjhattārammaṇā.
ai: Which phenomena have internal objects? The base of infinite consciousness and the base of neither perception nor non-perception – these phenomena have internal objects.

text: 1437. Katame dhammā bahiddhārammaṇā? Rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, catutthassa jhānassa vipāko, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ, cattāro maggā apariyāpannā cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā bahiddhārammaṇā. Rūpaṃ ṭhapetvā, sabbeva kāmāvacarā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā, rūpāvacaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca kiriyato ca – ime dhammā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā. Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ ajjhattārammaṇantipi, bahiddhārammaṇantipi, ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇantipi. Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā.
original: Katame dhammā bahiddhārammaṇā? Rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānā kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca, catutthassa jhānassa vipāko, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ, cattāro maggā apariyāpannā cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni – ime dhammā bahiddhārammaṇā. Rūpaṃ ṭhapetvā, sabbeva kāmāvacarā kusalākusalābyākatā dhammā, rūpāvacaraṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ kusalato ca kiriyato ca – ime dhammā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā. Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ ajjhattārammaṇantipi, bahiddhārammaṇantipi, ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇantipi. Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā.
ai: Which phenomena have external objects? The three and fourfold fine-material jhānas, wholesome, resultant, and functional, the resultant of the fourth jhána, the base of infinite space, the four supramundane paths, and the four fruits of recluseship – these phenomena have external objects. Except matter, all wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena of the sense sphere, and the fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome and functional – these phenomena may have internal objects, may have external objects, may have internal and external objects. The base of nothingness cannot be described as having internal, external, or internal and external objects. Matter and Nibbāna are objectless.

text: 1438. Katame dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā? Rūpāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā.
original: Katame dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā? Rūpāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā.
ai: What are the phenomena that are visible and with resistance? The visible object – these phenomena are visible and with resistance.

text: 1439. Katame dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā.
original: Katame dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā.
ai: What are the phenomena that are invisible but with resistance? The eye-base... the tangible object – these phenomena are invisible but with resistance.

text: 1440. Katame dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, nibbānañca – ime dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā.
original: Katame dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, nibbānañca – ime dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā.
ai: What are the phenomena that are invisible and without resistance? Wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, functional in the three planes, and that matter which is invisible and without resistance and is included in the dharma-base, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are invisible and without resistance.

text: Tikaṃ.
original: Tikaṃ.
ai: Triad.

text: Dukaatthuddhāro
original: Dukaatthuddhāro
ai: Elucidation of Dyads

text: Hetugocchakaṃ
original: Hetugocchakaṃ
ai: Chapter on Roots

text: 1441. Katame dhammā hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū. Alobho kusalahetu, adoso kusalahetu, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalesu uppajjanti. Amoho kusalahetu, kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇavippayutte cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalesu uppajjati. ⤵ Lobho aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Doso dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Moho sabbākusalesu uppajjati. ⤵ Alobho vipākahetu adoso vipākahetu, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, catūsu bhūmīsu vipākesu uppajjanti. Amoho vipākahetu, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, cattāro ñāṇavippayutte cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, catūsu bhūmīsu vipākesu uppajjati. ⤵ Alobho kiriyahetu adoso kiriyahetu, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyesu uppajjanti . Amoho kiriyahetu, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, cattāro ñāṇavippayutte cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyesu uppajjati – ime dhammā hetū.
original: Katame dhammā hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū. Alobho kusalahetu, adoso kusalahetu, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalesu uppajjanti. Amoho kusalahetu, kāmāvacarakusalato cattāro ñāṇavippayutte cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalesu uppajjati. ⤵ Lobho aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Doso dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Moho sabbākusalesu uppajjati. ⤵ Alobho vipākahetu adoso vipākahetu, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, catūsu bhūmīsu vipākesu uppajjanti. Amoho vipākahetu, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, cattāro ñāṇavippayutte cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, catūsu bhūmīsu vipākesu uppajjati. ⤵ Alobho kiriyahetu adoso kiriyahetu, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyesu uppajjanti . Amoho kiriyahetu, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, cattāro ñāṇavippayutte cittuppāde ṭhapetvā, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyesu uppajjati – ime dhammā hetū.
ai: What are the phenomena that are roots? The three wholesome roots, the three unwholesome roots, the three indeterminate roots. Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hatred is a wholesome root, they arise in wholesome states in the four planes. Non-delusion is a wholesome root, it arises in wholesome states in the four planes, excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge in sensuous wholesome states.⤵ Greed arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. Hatred arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure. Delusion arises in all unwholesome states.⤵ Non-greed is a resultant root, non-hatred is a resultant root, they arise in resultant states in the four planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous resultant. Non-delusion is a resultant root, it arises in resultant states in the four planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous resultant, and excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge.⤵ Non-greed is a functional root, non-hatred is a functional root, they arise in functional states in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional. Non-delusion is a functional root, it arises in functional states in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional, and excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge – these phenomena are roots.

text: 1442. Katame dhammā na hetū? Ṭhapetvā hetū, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā na hetū.
original: Katame dhammā na hetū? Ṭhapetvā hetū, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā na hetū.
ai: What are the phenomena that are not roots? Excluding the roots, wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, functional in the three planes, and matter, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are not roots.

text: 1443. Katame dhammā sahetukā? Vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ – ime dhammā sahetukā.
original: Katame dhammā sahetukā? Vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ – ime dhammā sahetukā.
ai: What are the phenomena that are associated with roots? The remaining unwholesome states, excluding the delusion accompanied by doubt and the delusion accompanied by restlessness; wholesome in the four planes; resultant in the four planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous resultant; functional in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional – these phenomena are associated with roots.

text: 1444. Katame dhammā ahetukā? Vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, dvepañcaviññāṇāni, tisso ca manodhātuyo, pañca ca ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā ahetukā.
original: Katame dhammā ahetukā? Vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, dvepañcaviññāṇāni, tisso ca manodhātuyo, pañca ca ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā ahetukā.
ai: What are the phenomena that are rootless? The delusion accompanied by doubt, the delusion accompanied by restlessness, the two five-fold consciousnesses, the three mind-elements, the five rootless mind-consciousness-elements, and matter, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are rootless.

text: 1445. Katame dhammā hetusampayuttā? Vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ – ime dhammā hetusampayuttā.
original: Katame dhammā hetusampayuttā? Vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ – ime dhammā hetusampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with roots? Excluding delusion accompanied by doubt and delusion accompanied by restlessness, the remaining unwholesome; wholesome in the four planes; resultant in the four planes, excluding rootless consciousness of the sense sphere; functional indeterminate in the three planes, excluding rootless consciousness of the sense sphere – these phenomena are associated with roots.

text: 1446. Katame dhammā hetuvippayuttā? Vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, dvepañcaviññāṇāni tisso ca manodhātuyo pañca ca ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā hetuvippayuttā.
original: Katame dhammā hetuvippayuttā? Vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, dvepañcaviññāṇāni tisso ca manodhātuyo pañca ca ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā hetuvippayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from roots? Delusion accompanied by doubt, delusion accompanied by restlessness, the two sets of fivefold sense consciousness, the three mind-elements, the five rootless mind-consciousness elements, matter, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are dissociated from roots.

text: 1447. Katame dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca? Yattha dve tayo hetū ekato uppajjanti – ime dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca.
original: Katame dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca? Yattha dve tayo hetū ekato uppajjanti – ime dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are roots and are rooted? Where two or three roots arise together – these phenomena are roots and are rooted.

text: 1448. Katame dhammā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, etthuppanne hetū ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Ahetukā dhammā na vattabbā – hetū ceva sahetukā cātipi, sahetukā ceva na ca hetūtipi.
original: Katame dhammā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, etthuppanne hetū ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Ahetukā dhammā na vattabbā – hetū ceva sahetukā cātipi, sahetukā ceva na ca hetūtipi.
ai: Which phenomena are rooted but are not roots? Wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, excluding rootless consciousness of the sense sphere; functional indeterminate in the three planes, excluding rootless consciousness of the sense sphere, excluding the roots that arise therein – these phenomena are rooted but are not roots. Rootless phenomena should not be called "roots and rooted" nor "rooted but not roots."

text: 1449. Katame dhammā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca? Yattha dve tayo hetū ekato uppajjanti – ime dhammā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca.
original: Katame dhammā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca? Yattha dve tayo hetū ekato uppajjanti – ime dhammā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are roots and are associated with roots? Where two or three roots arise together – these phenomena are roots and are associated with roots.

text: 1450. Katame dhammā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, etthuppanne hetū ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Hetuvippayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cātipi, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetūtipi.
original: Katame dhammā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, etthuppanne hetū ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Hetuvippayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cātipi, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetūtipi.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with roots but are not roots? Wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, excluding rootless consciousness of the sense sphere; functional indeterminate in the three planes, excluding rootless consciousness of the sense sphere, excluding the roots that arise therein – these phenomena are associated with roots but are not roots. Phenomena dissociated from roots should not be called "roots and associated with roots" nor "associated with roots but not roots."

text: 1451. Katame dhammā na hetū sahetukā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, etthuppanne hetū ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā na hetū sahetukā.
original: Katame dhammā na hetū sahetukā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, etthuppanne hetū ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā na hetū sahetukā.
ai: Which phenomena are not roots but are rooted? Wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, excluding rootless consciousness of the sense sphere; functional indeterminate in the three planes, excluding rootless consciousness of the sense sphere, excluding the roots that arise therein – these phenomena are not roots but are rooted.

text: 1452. Katame dhammā na hetū ahetukā? Dvepañcaviññāṇāni, tisso ca manodhātuyo, pañca ca ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā na hetū ahetukā . Hetū dhammā na vattabbā – na hetū sahetukātipi, na hetū ahetukātipi.
original: Katame dhammā na hetū ahetukā? Dvepañcaviññāṇāni, tisso ca manodhātuyo, pañca ca ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā na hetū ahetukā . Hetū dhammā na vattabbā – na hetū sahetukātipi, na hetū ahetukātipi.
ai: Which phenomena are not roots and are rootless? The two sets of fivefold sense consciousness, the three mind-elements, the five rootless mind-consciousness elements, matter, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are not roots and are rootless. Roots should not be called "not roots but rooted" nor "not roots and rootless."

text: Cūḷantaradukaṃ
original: Cūḷantaradukaṃ
ai: Minor Intermediate Dyad

text: 1453. Katame dhammā sappaccayā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā sappaccayā.
original: Katame dhammā sappaccayā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā sappaccayā.
ai: Which phenomena are with conditions? Wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, functional indeterminate in the three planes, and all matter – these phenomena are with conditions.

text: 1454. Katame dhammā appaccayā? Nibbānaṃ – ime dhammā appaccayā.
original: Katame dhammā appaccayā? Nibbānaṃ – ime dhammā appaccayā.
ai: What are the unconditioned phenomena? Nibbana – these are the unconditioned phenomena.

text: 1455. Katame dhammā saṅkhatā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā saṅkhatā.
original: Katame dhammā saṅkhatā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā saṅkhatā.
ai: What are the conditioned phenomena? Wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, functional in the three planes, and all matter – these are the conditioned phenomena.

text: 1456. Katame dhammā asaṅkhatā? Nibbānaṃ – ime dhammā asaṅkhatā.
original: Katame dhammā asaṅkhatā? Nibbānaṃ – ime dhammā asaṅkhatā.
ai: What are the unconditioned phenomena? Nibbana – these are the unconditioned phenomena.

text: 1457. Katame dhammā sanidassanā? Rūpāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sanidassanā.
original: Katame dhammā sanidassanā? Rūpāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sanidassanā.
ai: What are the visible phenomena? The visible object – these are the visible phenomena.

text: 1458. Katame dhammā anidassanā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ …pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, nibbānañca – ime dhammā anidassanā.
original: Katame dhammā anidassanā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ …pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, nibbānañca – ime dhammā anidassanā.
ai: What are the invisible phenomena? The eye-base ...pe... the tangible-base, wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, functional in the three planes, and that matter which is invisible, non-impinging, included in the dhamma-base, and Nibbana – these are the invisible phenomena.

text: 1459. Katame dhammā sappaṭighā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sappaṭighā.
original: Katame dhammā sappaṭighā? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – ime dhammā sappaṭighā.
ai: What are the impinging phenomena? The eye-base ...pe... the tangible-base – these are the impinging phenomena.

text: 1460. Katame dhammā appaṭighā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, nibbānañca – ime dhammā appaṭighā.
original: Katame dhammā appaṭighā? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, nibbānañca – ime dhammā appaṭighā.
ai: What are the non-impinging phenomena? Wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, functional in the three planes, and that matter which is invisible, non-impinging, included in the dhamma-base, and Nibbana – these are the non-impinging phenomena.

text: 1461. Katame dhammā rūpino? Cattāro ca mahābhūtā, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ – ime dhammā rūpino.
original: Katame dhammā rūpino? Cattāro ca mahābhūtā, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ – ime dhammā rūpino.
ai: What are the material phenomena? The four great primaries, and derivative matter dependent on the four great primaries – these are the material phenomena.

text: 1462. Katame dhammā arūpino? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, nibbānañca – ime dhammā arūpino.
original: Katame dhammā arūpino? Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, nibbānañca – ime dhammā arūpino.
ai: What are the immaterial phenomena? Wholesome in the four planes, unwholesome, resultant in the four planes, functional in the three planes, and Nibbana – these are the immaterial phenomena.

text: 1463. Katame dhammā lokiyā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā lokiyā.
original: Katame dhammā lokiyā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā lokiyā.
ai: What are the mundane phenomena? Wholesome in the three planes, unwholesome, resultant in the three planes, functional in the three planes, and all matter – these are the mundane phenomena.

text: 1464. Katame dhammā lokuttarā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā lokuttarā. Sabbe [sabbeva (syā.)] dhammā kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.
original: Katame dhammā lokuttarā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā lokuttarā. Sabbe [sabbeva (syā.)] dhammā kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.
ai:
What are the transcendent states? The four supramundane paths, the four fruition states, and Nibbāna 

– these states are transcendent. All states are knowable by some, not knowable by some.

text: Āsavagocchakaṃ
original: Āsavagocchakaṃ
ai: The Section on Taints

text: 1465. Katame dhammā āsavā? Cattāro āsavā – kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, diṭṭhāsavo, avijjāsavo. Kāmāsavo aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati bhavāsavo catūsu diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati diṭṭhāsavo catūsu diṭṭhigatasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Avijjāsavo sabbākusalesu uppajjati – ime dhammā āsavā.
original: Katame dhammā āsavā? Cattāro āsavā – kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, diṭṭhāsavo, avijjāsavo. Kāmāsavo aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati bhavāsavo catūsu diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati diṭṭhāsavo catūsu diṭṭhigatasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Avijjāsavo sabbākusalesu uppajjati – ime dhammā āsavā.
ai: What are the taints? The four taints: taint of sensual desire, taint of existence, taint of views, taint of ignorance. The taint of sensual desire arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. The taint of existence arises in the four consciousnesses accompanied by greed dissociated from wrong view. The taint of views arises in the four consciousnesses associated with wrong view. The taint of ignorance arises in all unwholesome states. These states are taints.

text: 1466. Katame dhammā no āsavā? Ṭhapetvā āsave avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ , catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā no āsavā.
original: Katame dhammā no āsavā? Ṭhapetvā āsave avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ , catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā no āsavā.
ai: What are not taints? Excluding the taints, the remaining unwholesome states, wholesome states in the four planes, resultant states in the four planes, functional indeterminate states in the three planes, matter, and Nibbāna – these states are not taints.

text: 1467. Katame dhammā sāsavā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā sāsavā.
original: Katame dhammā sāsavā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā sāsavā.
ai: What are tainted states? Wholesome states in the three planes, unwholesome states, resultant states in the three planes, functional indeterminate states in the three planes, and all matter – these states are tainted.

text: 1468. Katame dhammā anāsavā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā anāsavā.
original: Katame dhammā anāsavā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā anāsavā.
ai: What are untainted states? The four supramundane paths, the four fruition states, and Nibbāna – these states are untainted.

text: 1469. Katame dhammā āsavasampayuttā? Dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā etthuppannaṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā, vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā āsavasampayuttā.
original: Katame dhammā āsavasampayuttā? Dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā etthuppannaṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā, vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā āsavasampayuttā.
ai: What are states concomitant with taints? Excluding the delusion arising in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, excluding the delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness, the remaining unwholesome states – these states are concomitant with taints.

text: 1470. Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā? Dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppanno moho, vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā.
original: Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā? Dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppanno moho, vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā.
ai: What are states dissociated from taints? The delusion arising in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, the delusion accompanied by doubt, the delusion accompanied by restlessness, wholesome states in the four planes, resultant states in the four planes, functional indeterminate states in the three planes, matter, and Nibbāna – these states are dissociated from taints.

text: 1471. Katame dhammā āsavā ceva sāsavā ca? Teva āsavā āsavā ceva sāsavā ca.
original: Katame dhammā āsavā ceva sāsavā ca? Teva āsavā āsavā ceva sāsavā ca.
ai: What are states that are both taints and tainted? Those same taints are both taints and tainted.

text: 1472. Katame dhammā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā? Ṭhapetvā āsave, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā. Anāsavā dhammā na vattabbā – āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi.
original: Katame dhammā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā? Ṭhapetvā āsave, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā. Anāsavā dhammā na vattabbā – āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi.
ai: What are states that are tainted but not taints? Excluding the taints, the remaining unwholesome states, wholesome states in the three planes, resultant states in the three planes, functional indeterminate states in the three planes, and all matter – these states are tainted but not taints. Untainted states are not to be called “both taints and tainted” nor “tainted but not taints.”

text: 1473. Katame dhammā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca? Yattha dve tayo āsavā ekato uppajjanti – ime dhammā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca.
original: Katame dhammā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca? Yattha dve tayo āsavā ekato uppajjanti – ime dhammā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are both cankers and associated with cankers? Where two or three cankers arise together – these phenomena are both cankers and associated with cankers.

text: 1474. Katame dhammā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā? Ṭhapetvā āsave, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā. Āsavavippayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi.
original: Katame dhammā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā? Ṭhapetvā āsave, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā. Āsavavippayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with cankers but are not cankers themselves? Excluding the cankers, the remaining unwholesome phenomena – these phenomena are associated with cankers but are not cankers themselves. Phenomena disjoined from cankers are not to be called 'both cankers and associated with cankers' nor 'associated with cankers but not cankers themselves'.

text: 1475. Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā? Dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppanno moho, vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā.
original: Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā? Dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppanno moho, vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccasahagato moho, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā.
ai: Which phenomena are disjoined from cankers but still have cankers? Ignorance arising in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, ignorance accompanied by doubt, ignorance accompanied by restlessness, wholesome phenomena in the three planes, resultant phenomena in the three planes, functional phenomena in the three planes, and all material phenomena – these phenomena are disjoined from cankers but still have cankers.

text: 1476. Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā. Āsavasampayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – āsavavippayuttā sāsavātipi, āsavavippayuttā anāsavātipi.
original: Katame dhammā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā. Āsavasampayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – āsavavippayuttā sāsavātipi, āsavavippayuttā anāsavātipi.
ai: Which phenomena are disjoined from cankers and are without cankers? The four supramundane paths, the four supramundane fruits, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are disjoined from cankers and are without cankers. Phenomena associated with cankers are not to be called 'disjoined from cankers but having cankers' nor 'disjoined from cankers and without cankers'.

text: Saṃyojanagocchakaṃ
original: Saṃyojanagocchakaṃ
ai: Saṃyojanagocchakaṃ

text: 1477. Katame dhammā saṃyojanā? Dasa saṃyojanāni – kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ, mānasaṃyojanaṃ, diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ, vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ, sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ, bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, issāsaṃyojanaṃ, macchariyasaṃyojanaṃ, avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ. Kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Mānasaṃyojanaṃ catūsu diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ catūsu diṭṭhigatasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchāsahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ catūsu diṭṭhigatasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ catūsu diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Issāsaṃyojanañca macchariyasaṃyojanañca dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjanti. Avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ sabbākusalesu uppajjati – ime dhammā saṃyojanā.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanā? Dasa saṃyojanāni – kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ, mānasaṃyojanaṃ, diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ, vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ, sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ, bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, issāsaṃyojanaṃ, macchariyasaṃyojanaṃ, avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ. Kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Mānasaṃyojanaṃ catūsu diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ catūsu diṭṭhigatasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchāsahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ catūsu diṭṭhigatasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ catūsu diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Issāsaṃyojanañca macchariyasaṃyojanañca dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjanti. Avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ sabbākusalesu uppajjati – ime dhammā saṃyojanā.
ai: Which phenomena are fetters? The ten fetters: sensual craving, ill-will, conceit, wrong view, doubt, adherence to rites and rituals, craving for existence, envy, avarice, ignorance. Sensual craving arises in the eight greed-rooted consciousnesses. Ill-will arises in the two hate-rooted consciousnesses. Conceit arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses disjoined from wrong view. Wrong view arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view. Doubt arises in the doubt-rooted consciousness. Adherence to rites and rituals arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view. Craving for existence arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses disjoined from wrong view. Envy and avarice arise in the two hate-rooted consciousnesses. Ignorance arises in all unwholesome consciousnesses – these phenomena are fetters.

text: 1478. Katame dhammā no saṃyojanā. Ṭhapetvā saṃyojane avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā no saṃyojanā.
original: Katame dhammā no saṃyojanā. Ṭhapetvā saṃyojane avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā no saṃyojanā.
ai: Which phenomena are not fetters? Excluding the fetters, the remaining unwholesome phenomena, wholesome phenomena in the four planes, resultant phenomena in the four planes, functional phenomena in the three planes, material phenomena, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are not fetters.

text: 1479. Katame dhammā saṃyojaniyā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojaniyā.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojaniyā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojaniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are capable of being fettered? Wholesome phenomena in the three planes, unwholesome phenomena, resultant phenomena in the three planes, functional phenomena in the three planes, and all material phenomena – these phenomena are capable of being fettered.

text: 1480. Katame dhammā asaṃyojaniyā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā asaṃyojaniyā.
original: Katame dhammā asaṃyojaniyā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā asaṃyojaniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are not capable of being fettered? The four supramundane paths, the four supramundane fruits, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are not capable of being fettered.

text: 1481. Katame dhammā saṃyojanasampayuttā? Uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojanasampayuttā.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanasampayuttā? Uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojanasampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with fetters? Excluding ignorance accompanied by restlessness, the remaining unwholesome phenomena – these phenomena are associated with fetters.

text: 1482. Katame dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā? Uddhaccasahagato moho, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā? Uddhaccasahagato moho, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā.
ai: Which dhammas are disjoined from fetters? Delusion accompanied by restlessness, wholesome consciousness in the four planes, resultant consciousness in the four planes, functional indeterminate consciousness in the three planes, matter, and Nibbana – these dhammas are disjoined from fetters.

text: 1483. Katame dhammā saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā ca? Tāneva saṃyojanāni saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā ca.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā ca? Tāneva saṃyojanāni saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā ca.
ai: Which dhammas are both fetters and conducive to fetters? The fetters themselves are both fetters and conducive to fetters.

text: 1484. Katame dhammā saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā? Ṭhapetvā saṃyojane avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā. Asaṃyojaniyā dhammā na vattabbā – saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cātipi, saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanātipi.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā? Ṭhapetvā saṃyojane avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā. Asaṃyojaniyā dhammā na vattabbā – saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cātipi, saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanātipi.
ai: Which dhammas are conducive to fetters but are not fetters? Excluding the fetters, the remaining unwholesome dhammas, wholesome consciousness in the three planes, resultant consciousness in the three planes, functional indeterminate consciousness in the three planes, and all matter – these dhammas are conducive to fetters but are not fetters. Dhammas not conducive to fetters should not be called "both fetters and conducive to fetters" nor "conducive to fetters but not fetters."

text: 1485. Katame dhammā saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca? Yattha dve tīṇi saṃyojanāni ekato uppajjanti – ime dhammā saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca? Yattha dve tīṇi saṃyojanāni ekato uppajjanti – ime dhammā saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca.
ai: Which dhammas are both fetters and conjoined with fetters? Where two or three fetters arise together – these dhammas are both fetters and conjoined with fetters.

text: 1486. Katame dhammā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā? Ṭhapetvā saṃyojane, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā. Saṃyojanavippayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cātipi, saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanātipi.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā? Ṭhapetvā saṃyojane, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā. Saṃyojanavippayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cātipi, saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanātipi.
ai: Which dhammas are conjoined with fetters but are not fetters? Excluding the fetters, the remaining unwholesome dhammas – these dhammas are conjoined with fetters but are not fetters. Dhammas disjoined from fetters should not be called "both fetters and conjoined with fetters" nor "conjoined with fetters but not fetters."

text: 1487. Katame dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā? Uddhaccasahagato moho, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā? Uddhaccasahagato moho, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā.
ai: Which dhammas are disjoined from fetters but conducive to fetters? Delusion accompanied by restlessness, wholesome consciousness in the three planes, resultant consciousness in the three planes, functional indeterminate consciousness in the three planes, and all matter – these dhammas are disjoined from fetters but conducive to fetters.

text: 1488. Katame dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyā. Saṃyojanasampayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyātipi, saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyātipi.
original: Katame dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyā. Saṃyojanasampayuttā dhammā na vattabbā – saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyātipi, saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyātipi.
ai: Which dhammas are disjoined from fetters and not conducive to fetters? The four supramundane paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbana – these dhammas are disjoined from fetters and not conducive to fetters. Dhammas conjoined with fetters should not be called "disjoined from fetters but conducive to fetters" nor "disjoined from fetters and not conducive to fetters."

text: Ganthagocchakaṃ
original: Ganthagocchakaṃ
ai: Group of Bodily Ties

text: 1489. Katame dhammā ganthā? Cattāro ganthā – abhijjhākāyagantho, byāpādo kāyagantho, sīlabbataparāmāso kāyagantho, idaṃsaccābhiniveso kāyagantho. Abhijjhākāyagantho aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Byāpādo kāyagantho dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Sīlabbataparāmāso kāyagantho ca idaṃsaccābhiniveso kāyagantho ca catūsu diṭṭhigatasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjanti – ime dhammā ganthā.
original: Katame dhammā ganthā? Cattāro ganthā – abhijjhākāyagantho, byāpādo kāyagantho, sīlabbataparāmāso kāyagantho, idaṃsaccābhiniveso kāyagantho. Abhijjhākāyagantho aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Byāpādo kāyagantho dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppajjati. Sīlabbataparāmāso kāyagantho ca idaṃsaccābhiniveso kāyagantho ca catūsu diṭṭhigatasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjanti – ime dhammā ganthā.
ai: Which dhammas are ties? There are four ties: covetousness bodily tie, ill-will bodily tie, attachment to rites and rituals bodily tie, and dogmatic adherence to 'this is the truth' bodily tie. The covetousness bodily tie arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. The ill-will bodily tie arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure. The attachment to rites and rituals bodily tie and the dogmatic adherence to 'this is the truth' bodily tie arise in the four consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view – these dhammas are ties.

text: 1490. Katame dhammā no ganthā? Ṭhapetvā ganthe, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā no ganthā.
original: Katame dhammā no ganthā? Ṭhapetvā ganthe, avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā no ganthā.
ai: Which dhammas are not ties? Excluding the ties, the remaining unwholesome dhammas, wholesome consciousness in the four planes, resultant consciousness in the four planes, functional indeterminate consciousness in the three planes, matter, and Nibbana – these dhammas are not ties.

text: 1491. Katame dhammā ganthaniyā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā ganthaniyā.
original: Katame dhammā ganthaniyā? Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā ganthaniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are tied? Wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional states in the three planes, and all matter – these phenomena are tied.

text: 1492. Katame dhammā aganthaniyā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā aganthaniyā.
original: Katame dhammā aganthaniyā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā, cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, nibbānañca – ime dhammā aganthaniyā.
ai: Which phenomena are untied? The four supramundane paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are untied.

text: 1493. Katame dhammā ganthasampayuttā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittuppādā , cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatacittuppādā, etthuppannaṃ lobhaṃ ṭhapetvā, dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā, etthuppannaṃ paṭighaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā ganthasampayuttā.
original: Katame dhammā ganthasampayuttā? Cattāro diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittuppādā , cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatacittuppādā, etthuppannaṃ lobhaṃ ṭhapetvā, dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā, etthuppannaṃ paṭighaṃ ṭhapetvā – ime dhammā ganthasampayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are associated with ties? The four consciousnesses accompanied by wrong view, the four greed-rooted consciousnesses dissociated from wrong view (excluding the greed arising therein), and the two displeasure-accompanied consciousnesses (excluding the aversion arising therein) – these phenomena are associated with ties.

text: 1494. Katame dhammā ganthavippayuttā? Catūsu diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppanno lobho, dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppannaṃ paṭighaṃ, vicikicchāsahagato cittuppādo, uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā ganthavippayuttā.
original: Katame dhammā ganthavippayuttā? Catūsu diṭṭhigatavippayuttalobhasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppanno lobho, dvīsu domanassasahagatesu cittuppādesu uppannaṃ paṭighaṃ, vicikicchāsahagato cittuppādo, uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo, catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, rūpañca, nibbānañca – ime dhammā ganthavippayuttā.
ai: Which phenomena are dissociated from ties? The greed arising in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses dissociated from wrong view, the aversion arising in the two displeasure-accompanied consciousnesses, the consciousness accompanied by doubt, the consciousness accompanied by restlessness, wholesome states in the four planes, resultant states in the four planes, functional states in the three planes, matter, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are dissociated from ties.

text: 1495. Katame dhammā ganthā ceva ganthaniyā ca? Teva ganthā ganthā ceva ganthaniyā ca.
original: Katame dhammā ganthā ceva ganthaniyā ca? Teva ganthā ganthā ceva ganthaniyā ca.
ai: Which phenomena are both ties and tied? The ties themselves are both ties and tied.

text: 1496. Katame dhammā ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā? Ṭhapetvā ganthe avasesaṃ akusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ, tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko, tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ, sabbañca rūpaṃ – ime dhammā ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā.
